톈원이라는 이름은 고대 시인 굴원의 시 '천문'에서 왔고, 하늘에 던지는: The name Tianwen comes from the poem Tianwen by the ancient poet Qu Yuan, and it means questions to heaven. Tianwen-1 was launched on July 23, 2020, entered Mars orbit in February 2021, and the landing came three months later. Zhurong weighs 240 kg. The rover reported finding minerals containing water in the crust of sand dunes. NASA's Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter photographed the tracks Zhurong left and its lander. The name Zhurong was chosen by an online vote. It worked for more than three times the 90 Martian days that had been planned.
티코의 이름은 망원경 없이 하늘을 재어 이름난 덴마크 천문학자에서 왔고,: Tycho is named after the Danish astronomer who became famous for measuring the sky without a telescope, and Kepler used his observations to find the laws of planetary motion. In 1968 Surveyor 7 analyzed soil near here and showed that highland soil has more aluminum and less iron than the soil of the dark plains. In the novel and film 2001: A Space Odyssey, a buried black slab called a monolith is found near this crater. The inner wall of the crater is stepped, where it collapsed in layers, and part of the floor is rock that melted in the impact and hardened again.
달의 지질 시대 가운데 가장 젊은 시대를 이 분화구의 이름을 따 코페르니: The youngest period in the Moon's geological history is named the Copernican period after this crater. The crater was named by Riccioli in 1651 in honor of the Polish astronomer Copernicus, who published his book on the Sun-centered universe in 1543. Olivine, which probably came from deep inside the Moon, has been found on the central peaks. Boulders thrown out when the crater formed landed around it in lines and left small craters. Copernicus died in 1543, the year his book On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres came out. The Lunar Orbiter 2 photograph mentioned above was taken on November 23, 1966.
The name Sea of Tranquility goes back to the Moon map made by Riccioli in 1651. Apollo 11 brought back 21.5 kg of soil and rock, mostly basalt that hardened between 3.6 and 3.9 billion years ago, which for the first time allowed the age of a lunar sea to be measured directly. Three small craters near the landing site were named Armstrong, Aldrin and Collins after the astronauts. The landing spot itself is called Tranquility Base. Apollo 11 landed on July 20, 1969, and the two astronauts worked outside for about two and a half hours, staying on the Moon for about 21 hours in all. The mirror they left behind still sends back laser beams fired from Earth.
비의 바다라는 이름은 1651년 리치올리가 붙였습니다. 분지가 생길 때: The name Sea of Showers was given by Riccioli in 1651. Material thrown out when the basin formed covered the Fra Mauro region where Apollo 14 landed, and the age of rocks there puts the impact at about 3.8 billion years ago. Inside the sea lies the crater Archimedes, 83 km across. The place is also known as a mascon, where gravity is stronger than in the surrounding area. Apollo 14 landed at Fra Mauro on February 5, 1971, and Alan Shepard hit two golf balls there. On the northwest edge of the sea is the half-circle Sinus Iridum, the Bay of Rainbows, about 250 km across.
폭풍의 대양이라는 이름도 1651년 리치올리가 붙였습니다. 이 땅 밑에는: The name Ocean of Storms was also given by Riccioli in 1651. Beneath this region, the heat-producing radioactive element thorium is gathered in much larger amounts than elsewhere on the Moon, and Lunar Prospector mapped it for the first time in 1998. In 1969 Apollo 12 landed next to Surveyor 3, which had come down two and a half years earlier, and the astronauts walked over and brought its camera and other parts, about 10 kg, back to Earth. They became material for studying how a machine changed after a long stay on the Moon.
분지의 이름 에이트켄은 미국 천문학자 로버트 에이트켄에서 왔습니다. 19: The basin's name, Aitken, comes from the American astronomer Robert Aitken. Laser data from the Clementine spacecraft in 1994 gave the first good view of how deep this huge feature is. The basin is thought to have formed about 4.25 billion years ago, and the soil brought back by Chang'e 6 came from inside it. The floor inside holds more iron and thorium than its surroundings. American scientists have long listed bringing samples back from here as an important goal. A depth of 8 km is close to the height of Mount Everest.
섀클턴은 남극-에이트켄 분지의 가장자리에 걸쳐 있습니다. 일본의 가구야는: Shackleton lies on the edge of the South Pole-Aitken basin. Japan's Kaguya, launched in 2007, photographed the inner wall of this crater and reported in 2008 that no clear exposed ice could be seen on the floor. Later the laser altimeter of America's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter measured that the floor is a little brighter than its surroundings, and scientists considered the chance that scattered frost lies there. The ridge near the crater's rim is part of a candidate landing region for Artemis III.
아폴로 15호는 1971년 7월 30일 이 산맥의 기슭에 내렸고, 달에서: Apollo 15 landed at the foot of this range on July 30, 1971, and it was the first mission to use a rover on the Moon. The rover covered about 27.9 km over three days. The astronauts Scott and Irwin collected 77 kg of soil and rock, and a white rock more than 4 billion years old among them is called the Genesis Rock. The nearby Mons Hadley is about 4,600 m high. Scott dropped a hammer and a feather from the same height on the Moon and showed that they fall together, and the scene was broadcast on television. The two men worked outside for about 18 and a half hours in total over three moonwalks.
알프스 산맥은 길이 약 280km이고 가장 높은 몽블랑은 약 3,600m: The Alps range is about 280 km long, and its highest peak, Mont Blanc, is about 3,600 m. Hevelius named it after the Alps of Earth in the 17th century. The valley cuts straight across the range and links Mare Imbrium with Mare Frigoris, the Sea of Cold. Its walls are steep and its floor is flat. Nearby is the crater Cassini, 57 km across, and inside it sits a smaller crater, Cassini A, about 15 km wide. The Sea of Cold, Mare Frigoris, is a long band of sea in the north of the Moon, about 1,500 km in length. The thin groove on the floor is thought to be a trace left by flowing lava.
구름의 바다는 지름 약 700km의 어두운 평원으로, 이름은 1651년: The Sea of Clouds is a dark plain about 700 km across, and Riccioli gave it its name in 1651. The Straight Wall is a fault where the west side has dropped below the east side, and it is thought to have formed as the sea filled with lava cooled and grew heavier, cracking the ground at its edge. The nearby crater Birt is 17 km wide, and a crack called Rima Birt, about 50 km long, runs beside it. To the west is the 61 km crater Bullialdus, which holds a central peak. In 1964 Ranger 7 sent back 4,316 pictures before it hit Mare Cognitum, the Known Sea, next to this sea.
루나 3호는 1959년 10월 4일 발사되어 7일에 달 뒷면을 찍었습니다: Luna 3 was launched on October 4, 1959, and photographed the far side of the Moon on October 7. Passing about 6,200 km above the far side, it took 29 pictures, and 17 usable ones were sent to Earth. Soviet scientists were the first to give names to features in the pictures, such as the Sea of Moscow, Tsiolkovsky, Mendeleev and Lomonosov. About 70 percent of the far side was revealed for the first time in these photographs. The camera developed and dried the film inside the spacecraft, scanned it and sent it by radio. The pictures were blurry, but they showed for the first time that the far side has almost no seas and many mountains.
콘스탄틴 치올콥스키는 1857년 러시아에서 태어나 열 살 무렵 성홍열로: Konstantin Tsiolkovsky was born in Russia in 1857, lost most of his hearing to scarlet fever at about age ten, could not attend school and taught himself. In 1903 he published a paper that set out in an equation the relation between the speed a rocket gains and the amount of fuel it burns. The equation is still basic to rocket design and is called the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation. He died in 1935, 22 years before Sputnik. In the east of Russia, a city named Tsiolkovsky stands next to the Vostochny Cosmodrome.
루노호트 2호는 1973년 1월에 내려 약 4개월 동안 39km를 달렸고: Lunokhod 2 landed in January 1973 and drove 39 km in about four months, a distance that stood as the record on another world until Opportunity passed it in 2014. The Apollo 17 astronauts Cernan and Schmitt landed on December 11, 1972, and over three days walked for more than 22 hours and collected about 110 kg of soil and rock. Schmitt was the only professional geologist to go to the Moon. They are still the last people to have stood on it. Schmitt held a doctorate.
위난의 바다는 마스콘이라 부르는, 둘레보다 중력이 센 곳 가운데 하나입니: Mare Crisium is one of the places called mascons, where gravity is stronger than in the surroundings. The Soviet Luna 20 landed in the Apollonius highlands north of this sea in February 1972 and brought back about 55 g of soil. The basalt brought back by Luna 24 hardened about 3.3 billion years ago. Riccioli named the sea in 1651, and on its west side lies the crater Proclus, which throws out bright rays. While Luna 15 was circling the Moon, the Soviet Union told the United States its orbit so that it would not collide with Apollo 11.
플라톤의 이름은 고대 그리스 철학자에서 왔고, 1651년 리치올리가 붙였: Plato is named after the ancient Greek philosopher, and Riccioli gave it the name in 1651. To the south stand the lone mountains Mons Pico and Mons Piton, and Mons Pico is about 2,400 m high. There is also a straight mountain ridge about 90 km long, called Montes Recti. Some of the changes in the brightness of the floor that early observers recorded may have been an illusion caused by the changing angle of the sunlight. The books of Plato contain the story of Atlantis. On the west wall of the crater there is a scar where a large part has collapsed.
1787년 윌리엄 허셜은 달의 어두운 쪽에서 이 분화구 근처가 붉게 빛나: In 1787 William Herschel saw a reddish glow near this crater on the dark part of the Moon and took it for a volcano. In 1963 two observers at Lowell Observatory in America also reported seeing red light here. The crater is about 3.5 km deep, and Schroter's Valley begins at a round head about 10 km wide and then narrows, a shape that earned it the nickname Cobra Head. Aristarchus, who lived in the third century BC, tried to compare the distances to the Sun and the Moon and judged that the Sun is far larger than Earth.
케플러가 1609년과 1619년에 발표한 행성 운동의 법칙은 행성이 타원: The laws of planetary motion that Kepler published in 1609 and 1619 state that planets travel in elliptical orbits. After his death, his novel Somnium, published in 1634, described a journey to the Moon, and the book is counted among the earliest works of science fiction. The new star he observed in 1604 is called Kepler's supernova. The Kepler space telescope that NASA launched in 2009 was named after him and confirmed more than 2,600 planets. He was born in 1571 and died in 1630.
클라비우스 분화구 안에는 지름 약 50km의 작은 분화구 러더퍼드와 포터: Inside Clavius are two smaller craters, Rutherfurd and Porter, each about 50 km across, which stand out most in the bow-shaped line of craters. The depth is about 3.5 km. SOFIA carried a telescope 2.7 m wide on a Boeing 747 and observed from above 12 km, and it was operated until 2022. By picking up the signal that water molecules give off in infrared light, it detected water at this crater. Clavius was born in Bamberg, Germany, and taught in Rome, and the Gregorian calendar he helped to make came into use in 1582.
무지개의 만이라는 이름은 1651년 이탈리아의 조반니 리촐리가 펴낸 달: The name Bay of Rainbows comes from a lunar map published in 1651 by the Italian astronomer Giovanni Riccioli. Long wrinkle ridges, crumpled as the lava cooled, run across the floor of the bay. On December 14, 2013, Chang'e 3 landed on the Mare Imbrium close to the bay and sent out the Yutu rover. It was the first spacecraft to land on the Moon in 37 years, since the Soviet Luna 24 in 1976, and China's first lunar landing. Yutu developed a fault in its moving parts before its second lunar night in January 2014, but it kept sending signals afterward.
이름은 가까이 있는 라이너 분화구에서 왔고, 감마는 옛 달 지도에서 그: The name comes from the nearby crater Reiner, and gamma is the Greek letter that old lunar maps used for a marking in its neighborhood. The magnetic field here was measured from orbit by the small subsatellites that Apollo 15 and 16 left behind and later by Lunar Prospector in 1998. It is far weaker than Earth's field but clearly stronger than the ground around it. The lunar surface darkens over time as the solar wind and tiny meteorites strike it, and this swirl is thought to stay bright because that effect is weaker here. How the magnetic field itself formed is still not settled, and one idea ties it to an old impact.
꼭대기의 분화구는 용암이 차 있던 방이 비워질 때마다 무너져 생긴 여섯: The summit crater is made of six overlapping calderas, each formed when the chamber that once held lava emptied and the ground collapsed; the deepest is about 3 km. Hawaii's Mauna Kea measures about 10 km from the sea floor, and Olympus Mons is more than twice that. A study of images from Europe's Mars Express concluded that some lava on the flanks is only a few million years old. That suggests volcanic activity on Mars may not be completely over.
계곡은 하나의 홈이 아니라 멜라스, 코프라테스, 오피르 같은 이름을 가진: The canyon is not one groove but a group of linked valleys with names such as Melas, Coprates and Ophir. Huge landslide scars remain on the canyon walls. Orbiters found sulfate minerals in the layered deposits inside, minerals that form where water is present. In 2021 Europe's ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter showed that the ground in the middle of the canyon holds a large amount of water-bearing material. That is one reason it is named as a possible place to obtain water if people go there.
타르시스 고원은 폭 5,000km쯤, 둘레 땅보다 10km쯤 높이 솟은: The Tharsis plateau is a vast bulge about 5,000 km wide and about 10 km higher than the surrounding land. Schiaparelli gave it a name taken from a faraway land in the Bible. Mars has no moving crustal plates, so the hot source beneath stayed in one place for billions of years and kept pouring out lava. The carbon dioxide and water vapor released then are thought to have affected the early atmosphere and climate of Mars. The crater at the top of Arsia Mons is about 110 km wide.
헬라스라는 이름은 1877년 스키아파렐리가 망원경으로 본 밝은 무늬에 그: The name Hellas was given by Schiaparelli in 1877 to a bright patch he saw through his telescope, using the old Greek name for Greece. The basin is known as a place where Martian dust storms often begin, and the planet-wide storm of 2001 started here. On the eastern rim, valleys that look carved by long-ago flowing water run outward, and the slopes show patterns of soil that flowed down like glaciers. The floor sits far below the surrounding land, so dust and ice tend to collect there.
2008년 5월 25일 피닉스 착륙선이 북위 68도의 북극관 가까이에 내: On May 25, 2008, the Phoenix lander touched down near the north polar cap at 68 degrees north, dug into the ground and confirmed water ice only a few centimeters below the soil. Phoenix also saw snow falling from the sky with its laser, and it ended its mission on November 2 of that year when winter cut off its power. The radar on the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter looked as deep as 2 km into the ice and showed layers of ice and sand laid down in turn as the climate changed. The north cap is the largest store of water ice on Mars.
1969년 마리너 7호는 남극관 위를 지나며 적외선으로 온도를 재어, 이: In 1969 Mariner 7 flew over the south polar cap and measured temperatures with infrared, showing that the cover is frozen carbon dioxide. The thick dry ice cap sits slightly off the center of the pole. In 2020 a few more signals like the 2018 lake signal appeared around the same place. But at that depth it is tens of degrees below zero, so water would need a great deal of dissolved salt to stay liquid, and studies since 2021 point out that minerals such as clays can produce the same signal.
이름의 주인 코롤료프는 살아 있는 동안 이름이 알려지지 않아 ‘수석 설계: Sergei Korolev, for whom the crater is named, was known only as the Chief Designer while he lived, and his name was made public only after he died in 1966. In 1938 he was arrested on false charges and spent time in a prison camp in Siberia. Europe's Mars Express showed this crater in 2018 in one picture stitched together from images taken on several orbits. Sand dunes ring the crater floor, and the mound of ice in the middle fills most of the crater's depth.
사진은 1976년 7월 25일에 찍혔고, 미국항공우주국은 당시 보도자료에: The picture was taken on July 25, 1976, and in its press release at the time NASA explained it as a trick of light and shadow. The name Cydonia comes from an ancient city on the Greek island of Crete and was given by Schiaparelli to a bright area he saw through his telescope. The face spread widely in 1987, when an author claimed in a book that it was a ruin left by an alien civilization. The first new picture taken by Mars Global Surveyor in April 1998 quieted that claim.
시르티스 메이저에는 니리 파테라와 메로에 파테라라는 화산 분화구가 있습니: Syrtis Major has two volcanic craters called Nili Patera and Meroe Patera. Orbiters found material rich in silica around Nili Patera, which may be a trace of a place where hot water once welled up. Until the early 20th century some people took the seasonal changes of this dark patch for plants growing. That idea faded in the 1960s when spacecraft showed it was dust moved by the wind. Next to it on the east lies the Isidis impact basin, about 1,500 km across.
혜성의 이름은 1969년 사진 건판에서 이 혜성을 찾아낸 소련의 천문학자: The comet is named after the Soviet astronomers Klim Churyumov and Svetlana Gerasimenko, who found it on photographic plates in 1969. It has the shape of a rubber duck, with two lobes joined together, and its longest side is about 4 km. Rosetta's instruments measured the ratio of heavy hydrogen in the comet's water at more than three times that of Earth's oceans, casting doubt on the idea that Earth's water came from comets. It also detected molecular oxygen in the comet's gas for the first time.
보이저 1호는 이오에서 활화산 아홉 곳을 찾았고, 넉 달 뒤 지나간 2호: Voyager 1 found nine active volcanoes on Io, and Voyager 2, which passed four months later, saw eight of them still erupting. Only Pele had stopped erupting in the meantime. Later, Galileo and ground-based telescopes concluded that a boiling lava lake lies at Pele's site. The lava is hotter than 1,000 degrees. Even after the eruption stopped, the red ring around it stayed in nearly the same place as in 1979, showing how quickly Io's ground is resurfaced.
2014년 카시니 사진을 분석한 연구는 줄무늬를 따라 약 100곳의 분출: A study of Cassini images published in 2014 found about 100 vents along the stripes. The vents send out roughly 200 kg of water into space every second. In October 2015 Cassini dropped to 49 km above the surface and flew through the plume, and a 2017 report suggested that hydrogen gas in the plume could come from hot water meeting rock on the sea floor. In 2023 salts containing phosphorus, an element essential to life, were detected in the ice grains.
1993년 3월 24일 캘리포니아 팔로마산 천문대에서 찍은 사진에 진주: A photograph taken on March 24, 1993, at Palomar Observatory in California showed comet fragments strung out in a line like a string of pearls. The number nine in the name means it was the ninth comet found jointly by the Shoemakers and Levy. The fragments were labeled with letters from A to W. The energy of the largest fragment, G, when it struck is estimated at about 6 million megatons of TNT. Jupiter turns once in about ten hours, and when the impact sites rotated into view from Earth, the Hubble Space Telescope photographed the scars.
착륙선은 지구로 곧바로 신호를 보내지 못해, 위를 나는 비행체가 받아 지: The lander could not send its signals straight to Earth, so a spacecraft flying overhead received them and relayed them. The cameras obtained color by using red, green and blue filters in turn, and in the pictures the sky and ground of Venus look orange. Analysis of the soil showed a basalt rich in potassium, similar in makeup to a certain kind of volcanic rock on Earth. The wind was a slow one, around 1 m per second. Its twin, Venera 14, survived for 57 minutes.
명왕성은 1930년 2월 18일 로웰 천문대의 사진 건판 비교로 확인되었: Pluto was confirmed on February 18, 1930, by comparing photographic plates at Lowell Observatory, and its name was suggested by Venetia Burney, an eleven-year-old girl in Oxford, England. New Horizons left on January 19, 2006, and passed 12,500 km above Pluto on July 14, 2015. It carries a small part of the ashes of Tombaugh, who died in 1997. Because the heart sits in a fixed place, Pluto turns with the heart always facing the side of Charon.
육각형을 처음 알아본 사람은 미국의 데이비드 고드프리로, 보이저 자료를: The first person to recognize the hexagon was David Godfrey of the United States, who found it while going back over Voyager data. It takes 10 hours 39 minutes 24 seconds to go around once, the same as the rotation period of Saturn's interior measured by radio signals at the time of Voyager. The hexagon is about 30,000 km across, more than twice the diameter of Earth. In 2013 Cassini photographed the eye of the storm at its center from very close. Around the eye, clouds circle at roughly 500 km per hour.
누리호의 첫 발사는 2021년 10월 21일이었고, 3단 엔진이 계획보다: Nuri's first launch was on October 21, 2021, and its third-stage engine shut off earlier than planned, so a dummy satellite did not reach orbital speed. After the cause was fixed, the second launch in June 2022 succeeded, and on the third launch, on May 25, 2023, it placed working satellites, including the Next Generation Small Satellite 2, into orbit. The launch site faces the sea to the south, so rockets do not fly over populated land. The center is run by the Korea Aerospace Research Institute.
메신저라는 이름은 수성의 표면, 우주 환경, 지구화학, 거리 측정을 뜻하: The name MESSENGER is built from the first letters of the English words for Mercury's surface, space environment, geochemistry and ranging. Launched on August 3, 2004, the spacecraft flew past Mercury three times in 2008 and 2009 before entering orbit. It showed that the center of Mercury's magnetic field is shifted north of the planet's center by about a fifth of its radius, and in 2012 it confirmed water ice in polar craters. It also found that Mercury's ground holds more volatile elements, such as sulfur and potassium, than expected.
혼돈 지형은 유로파 곳곳에 있고, 얼음 껍질이 얇아지거나 아래의 물이 올: Chaos terrain appears in many places on Europa, and it is thought to form where the ice shell thins or water from below rises up. Galileo was launched from a space shuttle in 1989 and deliberately plunged into Jupiter's atmosphere on September 21, 2003. This was to keep microbes from Earth from being carried to Europa someday. The follow-up spacecraft, Europa Clipper, left on October 14, 2024, and is due to arrive in 2030 and make 49 close passes of Europa.
7호는 1970년 8월 17일 떠나 넉 달 가까이 날았습니다. 신호가 약: Venera 7 left on August 17, 1970, and flew for nearly four months. The weakness of its signal is thought to be because the lander tipped over and its antenna pointed away from Earth. Its successor, Venera 8, landed on the day side of Venus on July 22, 1972, sent signals for about 50 minutes and made the first measurement of the makeup of the soil there. Then in 1975 Venera 9 sent the first pictures of the surface of Venus. Venera 7's success opened this road.
던은 2007년 9월 27일 떠나 2011년 소행성 베스타를 먼저 돌았고: Dawn left on September 27, 2007, orbited the asteroid Vesta first in 2011, and reached Ceres on March 6, 2015. Dawn is the first spacecraft to orbit two bodies in turn. Ceres was found on January 1, 1801, by the Italian Giuseppe Piazzi, and at 940 km across it is the largest object in the asteroid belt. Dawn ended its mission on November 1, 2018, when its fuel ran out, and it is still circling Ceres today. It is expected not to fall onto Ceres for several decades.
39A에서 처음 뜬 새턴 5는 1967년 11월 9일의 무인 아폴로 4호: The first Saturn V to leave from 39A was the uncrewed Apollo 4 on November 9, 1967, and in May 1973 it launched the space station Skylab. The first flight of the space shuttle Columbia left from here on April 12, 1981, and the final flight, by Atlantis, on July 8, 2011. SpaceX's Falcon Heavy made its first flight from here on February 6, 2018. The astronauts who rode Crew Dragon on May 30, 2020, were Doug Hurley and Bob Behnken.
2009년 7월 카시니의 적외선 카메라는 타이탄 북극의 호수 면이 햇빛을: In July 2009 Cassini's infrared camera saw, for the first time, the surface of a lake near Titan's north pole reflecting sunlight like a mirror. This was the clearest evidence yet that the lakes hold liquid. A Titan year lasts 29.5 Earth years, so one season lasts about 7 years. In 2005 Huygens landed on dry ground near the equator and photographed dried-up riverbeds. The American Dragonfly rotorcraft is planned to launch in 2028 and arrive in 2034.
카론은 1978년 6월 미국 해군 천문대의 제임스 크리스티가 명왕성 사진: Charon was found in June 1978 by James Christy of the US Naval Observatory, who noticed that Pluto's image in a photograph was smeared in one direction. He pushed for the name Charon because it sounded like his wife Charlene's name. Charon is 1,212 km across, more than half the size of Pluto, and the two bodies orbit each other 19,600 km apart, each always showing the same face to the other. Their common center of mass lies outside Pluto, so Pluto and Charon are closer to a pair circling each other.
해왕성은 태양빛을 지구의 900분의 1쯤밖에 받지 못하지만, 받는 열의: Neptune receives only about one nine-hundredth of the sunlight that Earth does, yet it gives off 2.6 times the heat it receives. This heat from inside is thought to feed its storms and fast winds. The atmosphere is mostly hydrogen and helium, and methane absorbs red light to give it a blue color. Neptune was discovered in 1846, and because its year is about 165 Earth years long, it returned to its discovery position for the first time only in 2011.
트리톤 표면 온도는 영하 235도로, 태양계에서 잰 땅 가운데 가장 차가: Triton's surface temperature is minus 235 degrees, among the coldest ground measured in the solar system. Triton orbits in the direction opposite to Neptune's rotation, so it is thought to be a body captured from far away. Neptune's magnetic axis is tilted 47 degrees from its rotation axis, a large offset like that of Uranus. Voyager 2 left on August 20, 1977, 16 days before its twin Voyager 1, and used the chance that comes once in 175 years, when the planets line up on one side, to pass the four planets in turn.
천왕성의 자전축은 98도 누워 있어, 1986년에는 남극이 태양을 마주: Uranus is tipped on its side, with its rotation axis tilted 98 degrees, so in 1986 its south pole faced the Sun. Voyager 2 measured the length of the day, 17 hours 14 minutes, for the first time from changes in radio signals, and the largest of the newly found moons, Puck, is about 162 km across. In 2022 the American planetary science decadal plan placed a Uranus orbiter and atmospheric probe first among the next large missions. No new spacecraft has gone to Uranus in nearly 40 years.
소유스 TMA-12의 승무원은 러시아의 세르게이 볼코프, 올레그 코노넨코: The crew of Soyuz TMA-12 were Russia's Sergey Volkov and Oleg Kononenko, and Yi So-yeon. Yi was born in Gwangju in 1978 and studied at KAIST, and she is a biotechnology researcher. The flight lasted about 10 days and 21 hours in all. Volkov and Kononenko stayed on the station, and Yi came home on Soyuz TMA-11 with Peggy Whitson of the United States and Yuri Malenchenko of Russia. That return capsule came down steeply.
보이저 2호는 1977년 8월 20일 쌍둥이 1호보다 16일 먼저 떠났고: Voyager 2 left on August 20, 1977, 16 days before its twin Voyager 1, and both carry a golden record holding the sounds and pictures of Earth. At the boundary Voyager 2 crossed, the density of the plasma suddenly rose. The power from its nuclear battery drops by about 4 watts a year, so the team plans to switch off instruments one by one to keep the signal going into the 2030s. The signal takes about 17 hours to reach Earth. In 2020 no commands could be sent for eight months while the Canberra antenna was being repaired.
탐사선의 이름은 1958년 태양에서 입자가 끊임없이 불어 나온다는 태양풍: The probe is named for Eugene Parker, who proposed in 1958 the theory of the solar wind, a constant stream of particles blowing out from the Sun. It is the first NASA spacecraft named for a living person, and Parker, then 91, watched the launch in person in August 2018. The probe found switchbacks, in which the direction of the magnetic field in the solar wind suddenly kinks. In April 2021 it entered the corona, and that was announced in December of the same year.
이름은 그리스 신화에서 아프로디테가 목욕했다는 샘에서 왔고, 1877년: The name comes from the spring in Greek myth where Aphrodite bathed, and Schiaparelli gave it in 1877. The plain spreads around 47 degrees north and is nearly 3,000 km wide. Dust storms that arise in the northern hemisphere of Mars in spring and autumn often travel south across this plain. For this reason Acidalia is one of the corridors that scientists watch when studying the weather on Mars. No lander has set down here, but orbiters have studied it for a long time.
스키아파렐리는 밀라노 브레라 천문대에서 일했고, 1877년 화성이 가장: Schiaparelli worked at the Brera Observatory in Milan and, in 1877 when Mars came closest, drew a map of fine lines linking light and dark areas. He chose dozens of the place names still used on Mars today. He believed Mercury always shows the same face to the Sun, but radar showed in 1965 that this was wrong. On October 19, 2016, the test lander's inertial measurement unit briefly malfunctioned, and it dropped its parachute early at about 3.7 km altitude and hit the ground.
와디럼의 가장 높은 봉우리 움 앗 다미산은 요르단 전체에서 가장 높은 곳: Jabal Umm ad Dami, the highest peak in Wadi Rum, is the highest point in all of Jordan, at about 1,850 m. Among the rocks lie the remains of a temple built by the Nabataeans in the 1st century. In the Arab Revolt of 1917, the British officer Lawrence passed through here on his way to Aqaba, and the story later became a film. Red Planet in 2000, The Martian in 2015 and Dune in 2021 were all filmed in this desert. Bedouin herders still live here today.
1957년 5월 15일 R-7 로켓의 첫 시험은 실패였고, 8월 21일의: The first test of the R-7 rocket on May 15, 1957, failed, and the test on August 21 succeeded, so the same rocket was used to launch Sputnik. On November 3, 1957, Sputnik 2 left carrying the dog Laika. On October 24, 1960, a rocket exploded on its launch pad and killed dozens of people. The Soviet space shuttle Buran flew only once, uncrewed, from here on November 15, 1988. The launch site covers more than 6,700 square kilometers.
2016년 국제 시추단이 바다 밑 지층 1,300m 가까이 구멍을 뚫어,: In 2016 an international drilling team bored down nearly 1,300 m beneath the sea floor and confirmed directly, from the samples, the ring of granite that rose up during the impact. The force of the impact is estimated at more than a billion times that of the Hiroshima atomic bomb. Dust and sulfur particles thrown up by the impact blocked sunlight and lowered temperatures for several years. The drill samples also contained traces of life returning to this spot not long after the impact.
충돌 속도는 초속 12km쯤이었고, 폭발의 세기는 TNT 1,000만 톤: The impact speed was about 12 km per second, and the force of the explosion is estimated at about 10 million tons of TNT. The rim of the pit rises about 45 m above the surrounding plain. The Canyon Diablo meteorite fragments collected across the ground now total several tens of tons. Barringer founded a mining company in 1906 to look for the iron underground, and he had still not found it when he died in 1929. The official scientific name today is Barringer Crater, though people commonly call it Meteor Crater.
켁 망원경의 거울은 통짜가 아니라 지름 1.8m인 육각형 거울 36장을: The Keck mirrors are not single pieces of glass. Each is made of 36 hexagonal segments, 1.8 m across, fitted together, and a computer adjusts the position of every segment twice a second, down to the nanometer. Keck I saw first light in 1993 and Keck II in 1996. The Subaru telescope has used an 8.2 m mirror since 1999 to photograph wide areas of sky at once. Andrea Ghez, who shared the 2020 Nobel Prize in Physics, used the Keck telescopes to track stars near the center of our galaxy and confirmed that a giant black hole sits there. The two Keck telescopes can also be combined and used together as a single interferometer, in which the distance between the two mirrors works like a larger telescope's eye.
알마는 1mm 안팎의 짧은 전파를 봅니다. 이 전파는 차갑고 빛이 가려진: ALMA observes short radio waves of about one millimeter, which light up cold dust and gas hidden from ordinary light. A 2014 image of the young star HL Tauri showed several round gaps in its disk of dust, which are thought to be paths swept clear by newborn planets. The crews live at a separate base at 2,900 m, and go up to the antennas at 5,000 m only for the time they need. Chajnantor is said to mean the place of departure in a local old language. ALMA is also the Spanish word for soul. The name stands for Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array.
한국천문연구원은 칠레, 남아프리카공화국, 호주에 지름 1.6m 망원경을: The Korea Astronomy and Space Science Institute runs a network called KMTNet, with one 1.6 m telescope each in Chile, South Africa and Australia, since 2015. The three sites take turns as the Earth rotates and watch the same patch of sky almost without a break. Its main job is to find exoplanets by catching the brief brightening that happens when the gravity of a passing star bends the light of a more distant one. In 2012 Korea also joined the Giant Magellan Telescope project, which will combine seven mirrors of 8.4 m each. The camera on each telescope takes in 4 square degrees of sky at a time, and sweeps widely across the star-rich direction of the galactic center.
이곳에서는 일본의 우주 화물선과 소행성 탐사선도 떠났습니다. 고노토리라고: Japan's cargo ship and an asteroid probe also left from here. The supply ship HTV, called Kounotori, was carried by H-IIB rockets and made nine trips to the International Space Station between September 2009 and May 2020. On December 3, 2014, an H-IIA launched the asteroid probe Hayabusa2. Hayabusa2 gathered about 5.4 g of dust from the asteroid Ryugu and dropped the capsule holding it in the Australian desert on December 6, 2020. The site is run by JAXA, the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency. On February 17, 2024, the second H3, Japan's new main rocket, succeeded here. The first H3, in March 2023, had failed because its second-stage engine did not ignite.
2024년 5월 3일에는 창정 5호가 창어 6호를 싣고 이곳에서 떠났습니: On May 3, 2024, a Long March 5 carried Chang'e 6 from here. In early June the probe landed in the Apollo basin on the far side of the Moon and scooped up soil, and it came back to the Inner Mongolia desert on June 25. It was the first time anyone had brought back soil from the far side. The soil weighed 1,935.3 g. Wenchang lies at about 19 degrees north, the closest to the equator of China's launch sites. The first launch of the Long March 5 also took place here, on November 3, 2016. On April 29, 2021, a Long March 5B lifted Tianhe, the core module of the Tiangong station, which weighs about 22 tons.
MESSENGER's pictures show that the floor of the basin is a smooth plain of hardened lava. Round wrinkle ridges and cracks overlap there, and the ground is thought to have been warped as the lava cooled, shrank and sank. Mariner 10 passed Mercury three times between March 1974 and March 1975 and photographed about 45 percent of its surface. MESSENGER orbited Mercury for a little over four years from March 2011 and completed a map of the whole planet in March 2013. The odd terrain on the opposite side of Mercury is also counted as evidence of how large this impact was. The name was given by the Mariner 10 team.
메신저가 2012년 11월 발표한 값에 따르면 북극 분화구들에 갇힌 물: According to figures MESSENGER released in November 2012, the water ice trapped in the north polar craters is estimated at 100 billion to 1 trillion tons. That much ice could wrap the whole of Washington, D.C. in a block 3 to 5 km thick. The dark material that covers the ice is about 10 to 20 cm thick, and is thought to shield the ice like a blanket so that sunlight does not melt it. When its fuel ran out on April 30, 2015, MESSENGER ended its mission by crashing into the surface of Mercury. MESSENGER became the first spacecraft to enter orbit around Mercury, on March 18, 2011. It carried on for more than four years, well beyond the one year first planned.
디스커버리호는 1776년 영국을 떠난 제임스 쿡의 세 번째 항해에서 레졸: HMS Discovery was the partner of Resolution on the third voyage of James Cook, which left England in 1776. When Cook was killed in Hawaii in February 1779, Discovery's captain, Charles Clerke, took over the expedition, but he too died of illness that August. The two ships returned to England in October 1780. Unlike the Moon, Mercury has such scarps all over the planet, and since the Mariner 10 photographs they have been counted as evidence that Mercury shrank as it cooled. Clerke died at sea off Petropavlovsk in Kamchatka, Russia, and was buried there.
이 땅을 처음 찍은 매리너 10호는 1973년 11월 3일 지구를 떠나: Mariner 10, which first photographed this ground, left Earth on November 3, 1973, swung by Venus in February 1974 to bend its path with Venus's gravity, and reached Mercury on March 29. It was the first probe to use the gravity of one planet to reach another, and the first to visit two planets. In March 1975 the nitrogen gas it used to hold its direction ran out and contact was lost, and it still circles the Sun today. Mariner 10 sent back more than 7,000 pictures of Mercury and Venus together. Mercury in them looked like the Moon, but its plains and cliffs were spread out differently.
Hollows are tens of meters deep and look bluish on the floor. The MESSENGER team first reported them in a science journal in September 2011. Many studies hold that they form in ground rich in easily vaporized material such as sulfur, and they may still be growing today. BepiColombo, sent jointly by Europe and Japan, left on October 20, 2018, and is due to enter orbit around Mercury in late 2026, when it will look at the hollows more closely. The name hollows comes from an English word for a hollowed-out place, and the MESSENGER team chose it to refer to this kind of terrain.
호쿠사이는 1760년 에도에서 태어나 1849년까지 산 일본의 화가입니다: Hokusai was a Japanese painter who was born in Edo in 1760 and lived until 1849. He used the name Hokusai from 1798, and changed his name nearly thirty times in his life. The Great Wave off Kanagawa is one sheet of the series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, which came out around 1831. When Japanese prints became popular in Europe in the late 1800s, this print was one that Western painters liked to collect. The rays of Hokusai crater are counted among the longest on Mercury. Despite its name, Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji actually consists of 46 sheets.
안토니오 비발디는 1678년 베네치아에서 태어났습니다. 머리털이 붉어 붉: Antonio Vivaldi was born in Venice in 1678. Because of his red hair he was called the Red Priest, and he became a priest in 1703. From the same year he taught the violin at the Pietà, an institution that cared for orphan girls. The collection of concertos that contains The Four Seasons was published in Amsterdam in 1725. Vivaldi died in Vienna in 1741, and his music was forgotten for a long time before people began playing it again in the 20th century. Each of the four concertos in The Four Seasons comes with a short poem describing the scenery of the season, so listeners can tell which passage depicts what.
1986년 3월 6일 베가 1호가 8,890km, 9일 베가 2호가 8,: On March 6, 1986, Vega 1 passed the nucleus of Halley's Comet at a distance of 8,890 km, and Vega 2 did the same on the 9th at 8,030 km. The two probes showed that the nucleus is shaped like a potato about 15 km long, and that its surface is very dark. The precise position of the nucleus they measured guided the European Space Agency's Giotto, which came within 596 km on March 14. The Vega landers also touched down on Venus and measured the makeup of the soil. Vega 1 and Vega 2 left Baikonur in Kazakhstan on Proton rockets on December 15 and 21, 1984.
베네라 9호보다 앞서 베네라 7호가 1970년 12월 15일 금성에 내려: Before Venera 9, Venera 7 landed on Venus on December 15, 1970 and sent the first signal from the ground of another planet. The signal lasted about 23 minutes. Venera 9 used a gamma-ray instrument to find that the rock has a makeup similar to basalt, and measured the wind near the ground at less than 1 m per second. In March 1982 Venera 13 and 14 sent the first color pictures of the surface of Venus. Venera 9 left on a Proton rocket on June 8, 1975 and Venera 10 on June 14, and the trip to Venus took about four and a half months.
In the air the probe measured, helium was a little less abundant than in the gas the Sun formed from. Heavy elements such as carbon, sulfur and argon were two to three times more abundant than in the Sun. This supports the idea that Jupiter first gathered icy lumps carrying such elements and then pulled in gas, but the matter is still debated. The main Galileo spacecraft left aboard the space shuttle Atlantis on October 18, 1989, and ended its mission on September 21, 2003 by deliberately plunging into Jupiter's air so that Earth life would not be carried to Europa.
칼리스토는 목성에서 약 188만km 떨어져 있어, 갈릴레이 위성 가운데: Callisto is about 1.88 million km from Jupiter, so it receives the least of Jupiter's strong radiation among the Galilean moons. For this reason NASA, in a 2003 study, named Callisto as a candidate site for a crewed base in the exploration of the Jupiter system. From changes in the magnetic field measured by the Galileo spacecraft, some scientists also think a salty ocean may lie beneath the icy surface. Callisto goes around Jupiter once every 16.7 days and always shows the same face to it. Callisto is 4,821 km across, almost as wide as Mercury, but much less massive. It is the outermost of the four moons Galileo first saw in 1610.
갈릴레이는 1610년 1월 7일 밤 목성 곁에서 작은 별 셋을 보았고 며: On the night of January 7, 1610, Galileo saw three small stars beside Jupiter, and a few days later he counted four. The names of these four moons were given by the German Simon Marius in a book of 1614. Ganymede is the name of a handsome boy in Greek myth whom Zeus, turned into an eagle, carried away. Ganymede goes around Jupiter once every 7.15 days, and its orbit is locked in a 1 to 2 to 4 ratio with Europa and Io, so they tug at one another. Voyager 2 came within about 62,000 km of Ganymede on July 9, 1979 and was the first to show the boundary between the dark ground and the bright grooved terrain in detail.
대적점의 바람은 가운데에서는 거의 없다가 가장자리로 갈수록 빨라지며, 한: The winds of the Great Red Spot are almost still at its center and grow faster toward the edge, and one turn takes about 6 Earth days. The cloud tops stand about 8 km higher than their surroundings. In 2019 the Hubble Space Telescope photographed red flakes peeling off the spot, but NASA explained that the storm was not falling apart. In March 1979 Voyager 1 took close pictures of the spot and for the first time showed the clouds swirling inside the storm. The spot can be made out even with a small telescope, and amateur observers have watched it for a long time.
가니메데는 지름이 수성보다 8%쯤 크지만 돌 대신 얼음이 많아 질량은 수: Ganymede is about 8 percent wider than Mercury, but it has ice instead of rock in large part, so its mass is less than half that of Mercury. The European Space Agency's Juice left on April 14, 2023, will reach Jupiter in July 2031, and will enter orbit around Ganymede in December 2034. It will be the first probe to orbit a moon other than Earth's. On its passes over Ganymede it will also use radar to measure the depth of the ocean under the ice and the thickness of the icy shell. NASA's Europa Clipper also left in October 2024 and is due to reach Jupiter in 2030, so two spacecraft will look at Jupiter's icy moons together.
레아는 지름 1,527km로 토성의 위성 가운데 둘째로 큽니다. 1672: Rhea is 1,527 km across, the second largest of Saturn's moons. Giovanni Cassini found it on December 23, 1672, and the Cassini spacecraft was named after him. Its density is about 1.24 times that of water, so roughly three quarters of it is ice and the rest is rock. Rhea goes around Saturn once every 4.5 days and always keeps the same face toward the planet. Its name comes from the goddess Rhea of Greek myth, wife of Cronus and mother of Zeus. Cassini entered orbit around Saturn in July 2004 and studied the Saturn system for nearly 13 years, ending its mission on September 15, 2017 by diving into Saturn's air.
1876년 12월 미국의 아사프 홀이 첫 하얀 폭풍을 기록했고, 이듬해: In December 1876 the American Asaph Hall recorded the first white storm, and the next year he found Mars's two moons, Phobos and Deimos. The storm of 1933 was found on August 3 by Will Hay, a British amateur astronomer who was also a comedy actor. The storm of 1990 was first seen by the American amateur Stuart Wilber. Saturn spins once in about 10 hours 33 minutes and takes 29.4 years to go around the Sun, so a white storm is something one sees about once in a generation. Cassini was the first spacecraft to watch a great white storm from close by.
미마스는 토성에서 약 18만 5,500km 떨어져 22.6시간에 한 바퀴: Mimas is about 185,500 km from Saturn and goes around it once every 22.6 hours. Its density is about 1.15 times that of water, so it is nearly a lump of ice. The gravity of Mimas plays a part in making the Cassini Division, the empty gap between Saturn's rings. Ring particles at the edge of the gap go around Saturn twice while Mimas goes around once, so they are pulled by Mimas at the same place every time and pushed out of their orbits. Herschel found Mimas with his 40-foot telescope, whose mirror was 1.2 m across. Cassini came within about 9,500 km of Mimas on February 13, 2010 and took close pictures of Herschel crater.
카메라 앞쪽 렌즈는 지름 1.55m로, 천문용으로 만든 렌즈 가운데 가장: The lens at the front of the camera is 1.55 m across, the largest lens ever made for astronomy. A single frame covers an area of sky larger than 40 full moons. It repeats 30-second exposures all night, taking close to 1,000 pictures a night, and over 10 years it plans to record about 20 billion galaxies and 17 billion stars. Because it shoots the same places over and over, an alert goes out within minutes when a star changes in brightness or a supernova suddenly flares. The first pictures showed one part of the Virgo Cluster of galaxies, and images of the Trifid and Lagoon nebulae were released with them.

That telescope will have 197 dishes, made up of 133 new ones plus MeerKAT's 64. In Australia, SKA-Low is being built from more than 130,000 rod-shaped antennas. In 2007 South Africa passed a law to protect astronomy areas, and it restricts devices that give off radio waves around the Karoo.

It can follow a single object for about 1 to 2.5 hours at a time. In return, its structure is simple, and it could be built far more cheaply than an ordinary telescope of the same size. The area that actually collects light equals that of a mirror about 9 m across. Its main work is spectroscopy, splitting starlight into a rainbow to measure what the star is made of and how fast it moves. SALT is run by the South African Astronomical Observatory, whose headquarters is in Cape Town. The same site at Sutherland also has a 1.9 m telescope.

The cabin carrying the receiver hangs from six cables running down from six towers around the dish, and moves about 140 m above it. Dr. Nan Rendong first proposed the plan in 1994, and construction began in 2011 and finished in 2016. Nan died in 2017, the year after the telescope was completed. He built the observatory in Delhi first, in 1724, and built the one in Jaipur after founding the city in 1727. Jaipur has twelve instruments, one for each of the twelve zodiac signs along the ecliptic. He also obtained European astronomical tables and studied them, but he compiled tables corrected by his own measurements and published them around 1735. 달로 가는 길에 지구에서 2만 9천km쯤 떨어져 찍었다. 태양을 등지고: Taken on the way to the Moon, about 29,000 km from Earth. With the Sun behind the camera the whole Earth is lit.
토성이 태양을 가린 동안 220만km 밖에서 찍은 165장을 이어 붙였다: While Saturn hid the Sun, 165 frames taken from 2.2 million km away were joined. The small dot outside the rings at the left is Earth.
한 장에 담긴 지구와 달: Earth and Moon in one frame
떠난 지 13일째, 1,166만km 밖에서 찍었다. 지구와 달을 한 장에: Taken on its 13th day out, from 11.66 million km away: the first photograph of Earth and the Moon together.
색을 강조한 사진 둘을 붙인 것이다. 크기의 비는 맞고, 둘 사이는 실제: Two photographs with their colours strengthened, put together. The sizes are in proportion; the two are set closer than they really are.
핵에서 596km까지 다가가며 찍었다. 길이 15km쯤 되는 땅콩 모양의: Taken while closing to 596 km from the core. Gas spouts from a black, peanut-shaped core about 15 km long.

화성 표면 20,000km 안에서 포보스와 데이모스를 한 화면에: Phobos and Deimos in one frame, from within 20,000 km of Mars's surface
멀리서 지구와 달을 한 화면에, 지구의 겉보기 지름이 0.1 → 1.5도: Earth and the Moon in one frame from far away, Earth 0.1 → 1.5 degrees across (Voyager 1, 1977)
허블 우주망원경 3,000km 안에서 허블과 지구를 한 화면에: Hubble and Earth in one frame, from within 3,000 km of the Hubble telescope

궁수자리 쪽 은하 중심을 화면 가운데 10도 안에: The galaxy's centre, toward Sagittarius, within 10 degrees of the middle of the screen

핼리 혜성 5,000km 안에서 혜성과 태양을 한 화면에 (지오토, 19: The comet and the Sun in one frame, from within 5,000 km of Halley's Comet (Giotto, 1986)

Looking at the Sun from so close! I only ever saw it through a filter.
I saw Mercury only a few times in my life, and here you are looking your fill for me.
So that is what the first star of every dawn looks like.
Our house must be down there somewhere. I have washing out in the yard.
That is the Moon I looked up at when I was fifteen. It has not changed a bit.
So the red dot I saw in my telescope in 2003 was land as wide as this.
That red spot has grown smaller since I first saw it.
The first time I saw the rings in a telescope I thought my breath had stopped.
In my telescope it was one blue dot, and your eyes see all of it.
You went all that way. Are you not cold?
I was sorry the day it stopped being a planet. And it had a heart all along.
You stopped by even that little place. How careful you are.
So this is what that faint thing looks like from close by. Thank you.
The comet I went out to see every evening in 1997. I am glad to see it again.
A comet found the same year as my notebook. We are the same age.
So many stars. From here the street lamps hide most of them.
Now I see what you saw. Thank you.
I put your photographs up on the wall. There are quite a few already.
You have gone far. Mind you eat properly.
I never saw a total eclipse in my life. You have, and that will do.
달에서 지구가 뜨는 걸 보다니. 1968년 아폴로 8호가 찍은 그 사진: To see Earth rise from the Moon! It is like the picture Apollo 8 took in 1968.
I am inside that dot. Did you see me wave?
The plain from the film. That scene, though, was shot in a desert in Jordan.
The Mars I saw at the cinema in 2015 was that very desert. You would not think it was Earth.
The Sun again. Mind your eyes. I never looked without a filter, not even at the eclipse of 2009.
Mercury again. I went out before sunrise and missed it time after time.
금성을 또 보냈구나. 2012년에 태양 앞을 지나던 검은 점이 저것이란다: Venus again. That is the black dot I saw crossing the Sun in 2012.
Our house again. This time I went out into the yard and waved.
The Moon again. I never tire of it either.
Mars again. In my telescope I saw nothing but the white cap.
목성을 또 찍었구나. 1994년에 혜성이 부딪혀 든 멍은 이제 없지?: Jupiter again. The bruise the comet left in 1994 is gone by now, is it?
Saturn again. In 1995 the rings lay flat and could not be seen for days.
Uranus again. Does it really go round lying down?
Neptune again. Just the blue I saw in the newspaper in 1989.
Pluto again. I grow fonder of that heart each time.
Ceres again. They called it a planet at first, you know.
Halley again. It comes back in 2061: you see it for me then.
Hale-Bopp again. It brings back those evenings out in the yard.
That comet again. It looks like a duck and makes me laugh every time.
Another total eclipse. I do envy you.
Earth rising again. Lovely however often I see it.
That dot again. I waved this time too.
Next time, frame it so I can tell what you were photographing.
One star. Try it a little larger and a little off centre.
Two stars. Your hand is getting better.
Three stars. This one I must frame.
2020년 5월 30일. 39A 발사대에서 팰컨 9이 크루 드래건을 싣고: May 30, 2020. A Falcon 9 leaves pad 39A with Crew Dragon. Hurley and Behnken are aboard.
미국 땅에서 사람이 궤도로 오르는 것은 9년 만이고, 민간 회사의 우주선: People rise to orbit from American soil for the first time in nine years, and for the first time ever on a private company's ship.
2분 30초 뒤 1단이 떨어집니다. 2단은 드래건을 밀고 궤도로 가고,: Two minutes and thirty seconds on, the first stage lets go. The second pushes Dragon on to orbit; the first turns back.
1단이 엔진을 다시 켜 속도를 줄이고 다리 넷을 폅니다. 대서양에 띄운: The first stage lights its engines again to slow down and puts out four legs. It comes down to a ship afloat in the Atlantic.
1단이 배 위에 섰습니다. 드래건은 19시간 뒤 국제우주정거장에 닿았습니: The first stage stands on the ship. Nineteen hours later Dragon reached the International Space Station.
케네디 39A 발사대에 내려서면 \"그날로\" 단추가 뜹니다. 누르면 2: Stand at Kennedy pad 39A and a "That day" button appears. Press it to watch Crew Dragon lift off in 2020.
1969년 7월 20일. 암스트롱과 올드린이 탄 착륙선 이글이 고요의 바: July 20, 1969. The lander Eagle, with Armstrong and Aldrin aboard, comes down toward the Sea of Tranquility.
컴퓨터가 고른 자리는 바위가 널린 분화구였습니다. 암스트롱이 손으로 몰아: The place the computer picked was a crater strewn with boulders. Armstrong takes the controls and flies on past it.
\"60초.\" 연료가 얼마 남지 않았다고 지상에서 알립니다. 엔진 바람: "Sixty seconds." The ground calls that the fuel is nearly gone. The engine blows dust out in every direction.
\"휴스턴, 여기는 고요의 기지. 이글은 착륙했다.\" 한국 시간으로 7: "Houston, Tranquility Base here. The Eagle has landed." In Korea it was 5:17 in the morning of July 21.
2005년 1월 14일. 카시니에서 떨어져 나온 하위헌스가 낙하산을 펴고: January 14, 2005. Huygens, let go by Cassini, opens its parachute and comes down into Titan's orange haze.
2시간 30분 동안 내려오며 강줄기와 바닷가처럼 보이는 땅을 찍어 보냈습: For two and a half hours on the way down it sent pictures of land that looked like rivers and a shore.
바닥은 영하 179도. 물이 언 얼음 자갈이 널린, 젖은 모래 같은 땅이: The ground was at minus 179 degrees: something like wet sand, strewn with pebbles of water ice.
사람이 만든 것이 가장 먼 곳에 내려앉은 순간입니다. 그 뒤로도 한 시간: No thing people have made has landed farther away. It went on sending for over an hour.
1976년 7월 20일. 바이킹 1호 착륙선이 궤도선에서 떨어져 나와 크: July 20, 1976. The Viking 1 lander lets go of its orbiter and comes down toward Chryse Planitia.
낙하산을 버린 뒤 엔진 셋으로 속도를 줄입니다. 땅을 덜 건드리려고 불꽃: With the parachute gone, three engines slow it. Their flames are spread wide so as to disturb the ground less.
It happened to be seven years to the day since Apollo 11 landed on the Moon.
내린 지 25초 뒤 첫 사진을 찍기 시작했습니다. 제 발판과 화성의 자갈: Twenty-five seconds after landing it began its first photograph: its own footpad and the pebbles of Mars.
2012년 8월 6일. 무게 899kg의 큐리오시티는 에어백으로 받기에는: August 6, 2012. At 899 kg, Curiosity was too heavy to be caught by airbags.
그래서 로켓을 뿜는 하강단이 공중에 멈춰 서고, 줄로 차를 매달아 천천히: So a descent stage on rockets hovers in the air and lowers the rover slowly on cables.
대기권에 들어서 땅에 닿기까지 7분. 신호가 늦어 지구에서는 지켜볼 수밖: Seven minutes from the top of the air to the ground. The signal was so late that Earth could only wait.
바퀴가 닿자 줄을 끊고 하강단은 멀리 날아가 떨어졌습니다. 게일 분화구에: When the wheels touched, the cables were cut and the descent stage flew off to crash far away. This is the moment it landed in Gale Crater.
2017년 9월 15일. 13년 동안 토성을 돈 카시니가 연료를 거의 다: September 15, 2017. After 13 years round Saturn and with its fuel almost gone, Cassini dives into the planet.
엔셀라두스와 타이탄의 바다를 지구의 미생물로 더럽히지 않으려고 고른 끝이: This end was chosen so that microbes from Earth would never soil the seas of Enceladus and Titan.
시속 11만km. 안테나를 지구로 돌린 채 추진기를 끝까지 뿜으며 대기: 110,000 km an hour. With its antenna held on Earth and its thrusters firing to the last, it sends what it learns of the air.
신호가 끊겼습니다. 마지막 전파는 83분 뒤 지구에 닿았고, 카시니는 토: The signal stopped. The last radio waves reached Earth 83 minutes later, and Cassini became part of Saturn.
소라야, 왔구나. 반찬은 부엌에 두고 이 수첩 좀 보련.\n\n: Sora, dear, there you are. Leave the side dishes in the kitchen and have a look at this notebook.
열다섯 살 때부터 하늘에서 본 것을 적어 온 수첩이란다. 본 것은 적고,: I have written down what I saw in the sky since I was fifteen. What I saw, I wrote in. What I could not see, I left as an empty slot.
I counted them. There are more than a hundred and eighty empty slots.
내 망원경으로는 거기까지였단다. 나머지는 가까이 가서 봐야 채울 수 있는: That was as far as my telescope could take me. The rest are slots that can only be filled by going there and looking.
나는 이제 멀리 못 간단다. 무릎이 말을 안 들어.\n\n: I cannot go far any more. My knees will not listen to me.
그런데 너는 날 수 있잖니. 지난달에 우리 집 지붕 위를 날아다니는 걸: But you can fly, can't you? Last month I saw you flying about over our roof. And how prettily you flew.
그래서 부탁이 하나 있단다. 빈칸 좀 채워 주련. 가서 본 대로만 적으면: So I have one thing to ask. Fill in the empty slots for me, will you? Just write what you see when you get there. There is no hurry. One slot at a time will do.
첫 칸은 달이다. 1969년 7월 21일, 내가 이 수첩을 시작한 날의: The first slot is the Moon: the Moon of July 21, 1969, the day I began this notebook.
Come back and tell me about it.
심부름으로 온 할머니 댁. 할머니는 마실 나가셨고, 마루에 낡은 수첩과: Grandma's house, on an errand. Grandma is out visiting, and an old notebook and a note lie on the wooden floor.
햇빛이 드는 마루 위의 낡은 수첩과 접힌 쪽지, 돋보기안경과 연필: An old notebook and a folded note on a sunlit wooden floor, with reading glasses and a pencil
한낮의 골목. 돌담 사이 기와지붕 대문이 반쯤 열려 있고 섬돌 위에 보자: An alley at midday. Between stone walls a tile-roofed gate stands half open, and on the step sits a food box wrapped in cloth
토요일 한낮. 엄마 심부름으로 반찬통을 들고 옆집 할머니 댁에 왔다. 대: Saturday, midday. Mum sent me next door to Grandma's with a box of side dishes. The gate is half open, but nobody answers when I call.
마루에 낡은 수첩이 놓여 있다. 표지 모서리가 닳아 둥글다. 그 위에 접: An old notebook lies on the wooden floor, the corners of its cover worn round. On it, a folded note. On the outside it says "To Sora".
마루에 펼친 낡은 수첩. 왼쪽에 오려 붙인 달 사진, 오른쪽에 줄지은 네: The old notebook lying open. On the left a pasted cutting of the Moon, on the right rows of square slots. Only the top few hold small drawings; the rest are empty
백여든 개도 넘는다고?: More than a hundred and eighty?
Filling in blanks? I'm good at that.
As I set down on the Moon, a note fell out of the first page of the notebook.
여름 새벽의 마당. 마루 끝에 내놓은 흑백 텔레비전에 달 착륙선이 비치고: A yard at dawn in summer. A black-and-white television set out at the edge of the porch shows the lunar lander; an empty bench, rubber shoes left off and a fan lie about
열다섯 살이었단다. 그날은 임시 공휴일이라 학교에 안 갔지.\n\n: I was fifteen. It was made a holiday that day, so there was no school.
텔레비전 있는 집이 드물어서 이웃집 마당에 온 동네가 모였단다. 새벽부터: Few houses had a television, so the whole neighbourhood gathered in a neighbour's yard. It was shown live from before dawn, but the black-and-white picture was so dim I could hardly tell what was what.
그래도 사람이 달에 내려섰다는 건 알았지. 그날 밤 달을 한참 올려다보고: Still, I knew a person had stepped onto the Moon. That night I looked up at the Moon for a long time and wrote the first page of this notebook.
할머니가 본 달에 나 서 있어!: I'm standing on the Moon Grandma saw!
The whole town in one yard? Fun.
When forty slots were filled, another note came out of the notebook.
마루 위에 펼친 신문과 가위, 풀. 오려 낸 사진에 줄무늬 목성과 연기를: A newspaper spread on the wooden floor, with scissors and paste. The cutting shows striped Jupiter and a small moon spouting smoke
신문에서 보이저 1호가 보낸 목성 사진을 봤단다.\n\n: I saw in the newspaper the pictures of Jupiter that Voyager 1 sent.
The moons that were only four dots in my telescope each had a face of its own. On Io a volcano was erupting: the first live volcano ever found off the Earth.
I cut that picture out and looked at it for a long while.
마흔 칸이다. 쪽지가 또 나왔어!: Forty slots. Another note came out!
She saw it in a newspaper photo.
점 넷이 달 넷이었어!: The four dots were four moons!
When a hundred slots were filled, another note came out of the notebook.
동트기 전의 옥상. 망원경이 낮은 하늘을 향해 있고, 지평선 위에 아주: A rooftop before daybreak. A telescope points low in the sky, and over the horizon is a very faint comet
핼리 혜성이 76년 만에 온다고 해서 몇 달을 기다렸단다.\n\n: They said Halley's Comet was coming for the first time in 76 years, and I waited for months.
새벽에 옥상에 올라가 지평선 가까이에서 겨우 찾았는데, 생각보다 희미해서: I went up on the roof at dawn and barely found it near the horizon. It was fainter than I had thought, and I was let down. I could not even see a tail.
희미해도 봤잖아. 난 가까이서 볼게!: Faint, but you saw it. I'll see it up close!
A note at the hundredth slot too.
Aw, she didn't even see the tail.
When the last slot was filled, the very last page of the notebook opened.
펼쳐진 수첩의 맨 뒷장. 왼쪽에 신문에서 오린 사진이 붙어 있고 오른쪽에: The last page of the open notebook. On the left a cutting from a newspaper is pasted in; on the right are four lines of handwriting
1990년 신문에서 사진 한 장을 봤단다.\n60억 km 밖에서 찍은 지:
In 1990 I saw a photograph in the newspaper.
Earth, taken from 6 billion km away, was like a speck of dust.
언젠가 그 자리에서 우리 집을 돌아보고 싶었는데, 나는 못 갔다.\n\n: I wanted some day to look back at our house from that very spot, but I never went.
You who read this page have been there and back. Come and tell me about it.
At the gate of Grandma's house. Sora knocks.
2009.7.22. 부분일식. 태양이 80%쯤 가려졌다. 필터를 대고 봤: 2009.7.22. Partial eclipse. About 80% of the Sun covered. Watched through a filter.
Low in the east before sunrise. Seen only a few times in my life.
2012.6.6. 금성이 태양 앞을 지나감. 검은 점 하나를 봤다. 다음: 2012.6.6. Venus crossed the Sun. Saw one black dot. Next in 2117.
하루가 일 년보다 길대. 이상해!: A day longer than a year. Weird!
1972.12. 아폴로 17호가 찍은 둥근 지구. 잡지에서 오려 붙이고: 1972.12. The round Earth taken by Apollo 17. Cut from a magazine, pasted in, looked at for a long time.
That's home. 71% of it is sea.
