유럽의 로제타는 2004년 떠나 10년을 날아 2014년 8월 추류모프-: Europe's Rosetta left in 2004, flew ten years and in August 2014 reached Comet Churyumov-Gerasimenko, becoming the first spacecraft to orbit a comet. The lander Philae, sent down on November 12, could not fire the harpoons that were to fix it to the ground: it bounced twice and fell into the shade of a cliff, and after 57 hours of work its battery ran out. Rosetta watched for two years as the comet woke on its way toward the Sun, then set down on the comet in September 2016.
로제타가 찍은 추류모프-게라시멘코 혜성(2014년 9월). 고무 오리처럼: Comet Churyumov-Gerasimenko, photographed by Rosetta (September 2014): two lumps joined like a rubber duck.
티코는 달 남쪽 고지대에 있는 지름 85km, 깊이 4.8km의 분화구입: Tycho is a crater 85 km across and 4.8 km deep in the Moon's southern highlands. Made about 108 million years ago, it is very young for a large crater on the Moon. So the bright soil thrown out then has not yet faded, and at full Moon its white rays, running over 1,500 km in every direction, can be seen even by eye. Its central peak rises about 2 km from the floor.
Tycho Crater, photographed by the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter.
코페르니쿠스는 폭풍의 대양 동쪽에 있는 지름 93km, 깊이 3.8km의: Copernicus is a crater 93 km across and 3.8 km deep, east of the Ocean of Storms. It was made about 800 million years ago. Its inner walls have slumped in steps like stairs and several peaks rise in the middle, which makes it the model of a large impact crater. It shows well even in a small telescope.
허블 우주망원경이 찍은 코페르니쿠스 분화구(오른쪽 위의 밝은 고리)와 사: Copernicus Crater (the bright ring at the upper right) and its rays spreading every way, photographed by the Hubble Space Telescope.
고요의 바다는 지름 870km쯤의 어두운 평원입니다. 물은 없고, 30억: The Sea of Tranquility is a dark plain about 870 km across. It holds no water: it is basalt ground, where lava that flowed out over 3 billion years ago filled the low land and hardened. People of old saw it in telescopes, took it for a sea, and the name has stayed. Apollo 11 landed in the south-west of this sea in 1969.
The Sea of Tranquility. The dark part is hardened lava.
비의 바다는 39억 년쯤 전 지름 수백 km의 천체가 부딪혀 생긴 분지에: The Sea of Rains is a basin about 1,100 km across, made about 3.9 billion years ago by the impact of a body hundreds of km wide and later filled with lava. The land pushed up by that impact became the mountains round the sea: the Apennines, the Alps and the Caucasus. From Earth it is the large dark circle at the upper left of the Moon's face.
달 정찰 궤도선이 찍은 비의 바다. 오른쪽 아래 가장자리가 아펜니노 산맥: The Sea of Rains, photographed by the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter. The Apennine Mountains run along its lower right edge.
폭풍의 대양은 달 앞면 서쪽을 덮은 가장 넓은 어두운 땅으로, 남북으로: The Ocean of Storms is the widest dark land, covering the west of the Moon's near side: over 2,500 km from north to south and about 4 million km² in area. Unlike the other seas it is not a round basin but uneven in shape. Luna 9, Surveyor 1, Apollo 12 and Chang'e 5 all landed here.
The Ocean of Storms, as a drawing: a dark plain of basalt and low wrinkle ridges. It is not a photograph.
남극-에이트켄 분지는 달 뒷면의 남극에서 에이트켄 분화구까지 걸친 지름: The South Pole-Aitken basin is an impact basin about 2,500 km across and 8 km deep, reaching from the south pole to Aitken Crater on the Moon's far side. It is the largest and oldest on the Moon (over 4 billion years) and one of the largest impact scars in the solar system. It is dug so deep that stuff from inside the Moon is thought to lie bare, and Chang'e 4 and 6 landed inside it.
The far side of the Moon. The South Pole-Aitken basin is inside the red line.
섀클턴은 달 남극점에 거의 겹쳐 있는 지름 21km, 깊이 4km의 분화: Shackleton is a crater 21 km across and 4 km deep, lying almost exactly on the Moon's south pole. The Moon's axis stands nearly upright, so the peaks of its rim are almost always in sunlight and its floor has had none for billions of years. Water ice is thought to lie on that floor, colder than minus 180 degrees, which makes it a place named for when people go to the Moon again.
Shackleton Crater. The shaded floor was photographed by Danuri's ShadowCam and joined in.
아펜니노 산맥은 비의 바다 남동쪽 가장자리를 따라 600km쯤 뻗은 산맥: The Apennine Mountains run about 600 km along the south-eastern edge of the Sea of Rains. They were not pushed up as mountains on Earth are: the rim of the basin was heaved up by the impact that made the Sea of Rains. The highest, Mons Huygens, is about 5,500 m. Apollo 15 landed at the foot of this range.
The Apennine Mountains, photographed by the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter. The Sea of Rains is at the upper left.
알프스 계곡은 달의 알프스 산맥을 곧게 가로지르는 길이 166km, 폭: The Alpine Valley is a valley about 166 km long and 10 km wide that cuts straight across the lunar Alps. Water did not carve it: when the Sea of Rains was made the ground split, the strip between two faults sank, and lava filled its floor. A thin groove like a little stream runs down the middle of the floor.
달 정찰 궤도선이 찍은 알프스 계곡. 산맥을 비스듬히 가로지르는 곧은 골: The Alpine Valley, photographed by the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter: a straight valley cutting aslant across the mountains.
직선벽은 구름의 바다에 있는 길이 110km쯤의 곧은 단층입니다. 벽이라: The Straight Wall is a straight fault about 110 km long in the Sea of Clouds. It is called a wall, but at 240 → 300 m high and over 2 km wide it is really a gentle slope of about 10 degrees. Around first quarter, with the Sun low, it casts a long shadow and shows as a black line; around last quarter it catches the light and shows as a white one.
The Straight Wall, photographed by the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter: the straight line running up and down.
모스크바의 바다는 달 뒷면 북쪽에 있는 지름 280km쯤의 어두운 평원입: The Sea of Moscow is a dark plain about 280 km across in the north of the Moon's far side. The crust of the far side is thick and lava could seldom rise through it, so seas are rare there. It was found and named from the first photographs of the far side, taken by the Soviet Luna 3 in October 1959.
The Sea of Moscow, photographed by Lunar Orbiter 5.
치올콥스키는 달 뒷면에 있는 지름 185km쯤의 분화구입니다. 밝은 뒷면: Tsiolkovskiy is a crater about 185 km across on the Moon's far side. In the middle of the bright highlands of the far side its floor alone is filled with black lava, and a white central peak rises from it like an island, so it stands out strongly. It was found in the photographs of Luna 3 and named after Konstantin Tsiolkovsky, the Russian who founded the theory of rockets.
Tsiolkovskiy Crater, photographed from lunar orbit by Apollo 15.
맑음의 바다는 지름 670km쯤의 둥근 바다입니다. 38억 년쯤 전의 충: The Sea of Serenity is a round sea about 670 km across: an impact basin about 3.8 billion years old that filled with lava. The lava differs in colour between the middle and the edge, so the rim looks darker. Seen from Earth it is about where the body of the Moon rabbit is. Apollo 17 landed in a valley at its south-eastern edge in 1972, and Lunokhod 2 at its eastern edge in 1973.
The Sea of Serenity, photographed by the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter.
위난의 바다는 달 앞면 동쪽 가장자리에 있는 지름 550km쯤의 바다입니: The Sea of Crises is a sea about 550 km across at the eastern edge of the Moon's near side. It joins no other sea and stands alone, so even by eye it shows as a black dot. Being at the edge it looks from Earth like an oval squeezed sideways, but it is really longer from east to west. Luna 24 took soil from here in 1976, and Blue Ghost landed here in 2025.
The Sea of Crises, photographed by the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter.
플라톤은 비의 바다 북쪽 가장자리, 알프스 산맥 서쪽 끝에 있는 지름 1: Plato is a crater about 100 km across at the northern edge of the Sea of Rains, at the western end of the Alps. After it was made about 3.8 billion years ago, lava filled its floor smooth, so it is flat and dark with no central peak. The 17th-century astronomer Hevelius called it "the Greater Black Lake". Its walls rise about 2 km from the floor and, when the Sun is low, throw saw-toothed shadows across it.
Plato Crater, photographed by the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter. Lava made its floor flat.
아리스타르코스는 폭풍의 대양 한가운데 고원에 있는 지름 40km의 분화구: Aristarchus is a crater 40 km across on a plateau in the middle of the Ocean of Storms. It is young, made about 450 million years ago, and the soil thrown up has not yet faded, so it shines brightest on the Moon's near side: it can be seen by eye even at crescent Moon, lit only by earthshine. Right beside it is Schröter's Valley, about 160 km long, the largest winding valley on the Moon: a channel cut by flowing lava.
Aristarchus (the bright crater in the middle), photographed from lunar orbit by Apollo 15. The channel winding down to the right is Schröter's Valley.
케플러는 폭풍의 대양과 섬들의 바다 사이에 있는 지름 30km쯤, 깊이: Kepler is a crater about 30 km across and 2.7 km deep between the Ocean of Storms and the Sea of Islands. Its bright rays run over 300 km across the dark lava plain, so it shows very well for its small size. Its rays overlap those from Copernicus Crater to the east. It is named after Johannes Kepler, who found the laws by which planets move.
Kepler Crater (at the top), photographed at a slant by Lunar Orbiter 3.
클라비우스는 달 남쪽 고지대에 있는 지름 231km의 분화구입니다. 40: Clavius is a crater 231 km across in the Moon's southern highlands. It is very old, about 4 billion years, and small craters lie on its floor in a curve, in order of size. In 2020 SOFIA, an infrared telescope carried on an aeroplane, found water molecules in sunlit ground here: the first time water was confirmed outside the everlasting shade. The Moon base of the film "2001: A Space Odyssey" is here too.
달 정찰 궤도선이 찍은 클라비우스. 바닥에 작은 분화구들이 활처럼 늘어서: Clavius, photographed by the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter. Small craters lie in a curve on its floor.
무지개의 만은 비의 바다 북서쪽에 붙은 지름 250km쯤의 만입니다. 큰: The Bay of Rainbows is a bay about 250 km across on the north-west of the Sea of Rains. It was a large impact crater; lava from the Sea of Rains flowed in and covered its south-eastern wall, leaving a half moon. The wall that remains is the Jura Mountains, about 3 km high. Just at sunrise only the mountain tops catch the light and rise from the dark like a golden arc: "the Golden Handle".
The Bay of Rainbows, photographed by the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter. The round rim is the Jura Mountains.
라이너 감마는 폭풍의 대양 서쪽에 있는 길이 70km쯤의 밝은 무늬입니다: Reiner Gamma is a bright marking about 70 km long in the west of the Ocean of Storms. It is neither a crater nor a mountain: only a swirl like a tadpole drawn on flat ground. Such markings are called lunar swirls. The ground here keeps a magnetic field, rare on the Moon, which is thought to turn aside the particles flying from the Sun, so the soil has not darkened.
Reiner Gamma, photographed by the Clementine probe.
올림푸스산은 높이 22km쯤, 밑지름 600km쯤의 방패 화산입니다. 에: Olympus Mons is a shield volcano about 22 km high and about 600 km across at its base. Two and a half times as high as Everest and wider than the Korean peninsula, it is the largest volcano known in the solar system. Its slopes are so gentle, about 5 degrees, that standing on it you would not know it for a mountain: its foot lies beyond the horizon. At the top are nested craters 80 km wide, and its foot ends in cliffs up to 8 km high. The crust of Mars does not move, so lava kept piling up in one place.
Olympus Mons, photographed by the Viking 1 orbiter.
마리너 계곡은 길이 4,000km, 폭 최대 200km, 깊이 최대 7k: Valles Marineris is a canyon 4,000 km long, up to 200 km wide and up to 7 km deep. It crosses a fifth of the way round Mars: laid on the United States it would reach from the east coast to the west. It is not a valley cut by a river but a rift that opened when the crust split as the Tharsis plateau to the west rose. Mariner 9, which entered orbit round Mars in 1971, found it and gave it its name.
바이킹 궤도선 사진을 이어 붙인 화성. 가운데를 가로지르는 긴 틈이 마리: Mars, pieced together from Viking orbiter photographs. The long rift across the middle is Valles Marineris.
타르시스 고원 위에는 아르시아산, 파보니스산, 아스크레우스산이 남서에서: On the Tharsis plateau Arsia Mons, Pavonis Mons and Ascraeus Mons stand in a row from south-west to north-east, 700 km apart. All three are shield volcanoes 14 → 18 km high. The middle one, Pavonis Mons, is right on the equator of Mars. Olympus Mons lies about 1,200 km north-west of this row. The plateau is so heavy that it has put the whole of Mars a little out of shape.
The three Tharsis volcanoes, photographed by the Viking 1 orbiter. They stand in a row.
헬라스 분지는 화성 남반구에 있는 지름 2,300km, 깊이 7km쯤의: The Hellas basin is an impact basin about 2,300 km across and 7 km deep in the southern half of Mars. A large body struck about 4 billion years ago; it is one of the largest impact scars that can be seen in the solar system. Its floor is the lowest place on Mars: the air above it is deeper, so the pressure is about twice the Martian average. That is still only about a hundredth of Earth's. In winter frost and fog cover it, and even telescopes on Earth show it as a bright circle.
A map of the heights of the Hellas basin. Purple is lowest.
NASA 고도계 자료, Martin Pauer 제작: NASA altimeter data, made by Martin Pauer
The north polar cap of Mars is a cap of ice about 1,000 km across and about 2 km thick. It is mostly water ice; every winter carbon dioxide from the air freezes and about 1 m of dry ice settles on it, to vanish in summer. Ice and dust lie in layer on layer, holding the record of Mars's past weather. Seen from above, its valleys are cut in a spiral like a pinwheel.
화성 정찰 궤도선이 찍은 북극관(2006년). 골짜기가 소용돌이 모양으로: The north polar cap, photographed by the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (2006). Its valleys are cut in a spiral.
화성의 남극관은 북극관보다 높은 땅에 있어 더 춥습니다. 그래서 물 얼음: The south polar cap of Mars lies on higher ground than the north cap and is colder. So the dry ice about 8 m thick that covers its water ice does not all go even in summer. The water ice beneath is over 3 km thick in places. In 2018 Europe's Mars Express found by radar a signal that looked like a lake 1.5 km under the ice, but whether it is really water is still argued.
The south polar cap in summer, photographed by Mars Global Surveyor (2000).
Korolev is a crater 82 km across on a plain at 73 degrees north on Mars. It is filled with water ice 1.8 km thick, about 2,200 km³ of it. The crater is so deep that the air over the ice cools, sinks and lies there as a lid of cold air, so the ice does not melt even in summer. It is named after Sergei Korolev of the Soviet Union, who built Sputnik, the first satellite, and Gagarin's rocket.
Korolev Crater seen at a slant, made from Mars Express data.
시도니아는 화성 북반구의 고지대와 평원이 만나는 곳으로, 깎여 남은 언덕: Cydonia is where the highlands of Mars's northern half meet the plains, with many worn-down hills. In a photograph by the Viking 1 orbiter in July 1976 one hill about 2 km long looked like a human face with eyes, nose and mouth, and became famous as "the Face on Mars". Shadows from a low Sun had done it. When Mars Global Surveyor photographed it again far more sharply in 1998 and 2001, it was an ordinary hill.
화성 정찰 궤도선이 찍은 \"얼굴\" 언덕. 오른쪽 아래 작은 사진이 1: The "Face" hill, photographed by the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter. The small picture at the lower right is Viking 1's of 1976.
시르티스 메이저는 화성 적도 가까이에 있는 폭 1,300km쯤의 어두운: Syrtis Major is a dark land about 1,300 km wide near the equator of Mars. Christiaan Huygens saw it through a telescope in 1659 and drew it, making it the first feature recorded on another planet. Watching the marking come round again, he worked out the length of Mars's day: about 24 hours. It was taken for a sea, but it is really a low shield volcano covered in basalt lava, and it looks dark because the wind sweeps its dust away.
바이킹 궤도선 사진을 이어 붙인 시르티스 메이저. 가운데의 어두운 땅입니: Syrtis Major, pieced together from Viking orbiter photographs: the dark land in the middle.
1979년 3월 보이저 1호가 이오를 지나며 찍은 사진의 가장자리에, 우: At the edge of a photograph Voyager 1 took as it passed Io in March 1979 was a plume rising like an umbrella: the first active volcano found off the Earth. Pele's eruptions rise 300 km, and the sulfur that falls draws a red ring 1,200 km across. Io is hot because Jupiter and the other moons pull on it in turn and knead its inside, and it is the most volcanic body in the solar system.
보이저 1호가 찍은 펠레 화산의 분출. 오른쪽 위 가장자리에 연기가 우산: The eruption of Pele, photographed by Voyager 1. At the upper right edge the plume rises like an umbrella; the dark spot under it is the vent.
엔셀라두스 남극에는 길이 130km쯤의 균열 넷이 나란히 나 있어 호랑이: At the south pole of Enceladus four cracks about 130 km long run side by side: the tiger stripes. In 2005 Cassini found water and grains of ice spouting from them hundreds of km high: proof of a salty sea under the shell of ice. The ice it spouts becomes Saturn's E ring. Cassini flew right through the jets and measured salt and organic matter.
The jets at the south pole of Enceladus, photographed by Cassini.
슈메이커-레비 9 혜성은 1992년 목성에 너무 가까이 지나다 스물한 조: Comet Shoemaker-Levy 9 passed too close to Jupiter in 1992 and broke into twenty-one pieces. From July 16 to 22, 1994, the pieces struck Jupiter's southern half one after another at 60 km a second. The largest scar was the size of Earth, and the dark bruises showed for months even in small telescopes. It was the first time people watched two bodies of the solar system collide.
Jupiter, photographed by the Hubble Space Telescope. The impact scars are in a row in the southern half.
보이저 2호는 떠난 지 12년 만인 1989년 8월 25일 해왕성 북극: Twelve years after leaving, on August 25, 1989, Voyager 2 passed 4,950 km above the clouds of Neptune's north pole. It found the Great Dark Spot, a dark storm the size of Earth, and winds of 2,000 km an hour, and showed that the rings are whole and not broken. Five hours later it passed the moon Triton and photographed nitrogen geysers. It is still the only spacecraft to have been to Neptune.
보이저 2호는 1986년 1월 24일 천왕성 구름 위 81,500km를: Voyager 2 passed 81,500 km above the clouds of Uranus on January 24, 1986. In a meeting of a little over six hours it found ten new moons and two rings, and learned that the axis of the magnetic field leans 59 degrees from the spin axis. On the moon Miranda it photographed a cliff 20 km high. It is still the only spacecraft to have been to Uranus.
Uranus, photographed by Voyager 2. It shows almost no markings.
소련의 베네라 13호는 1982년 3월 1일 금성에 내렸습니다. 땅의 온: The Soviet Venera 13 landed on Venus on March 1, 1982. The ground was at 457 degrees and the pressure 89 times Earth's; built to last 32 minutes, the lander lasted 127. It took the first colour photographs of the surface of Venus and drilled up soil to measure what it was made of. Its microphone recorded the wind and the noise of its own gear: the sound of another planet, sent to Earth for the first time.
베네라 13호가 찍은 금성의 땅. 오른쪽 아래에 착륙선의 톱니 모양 가장: The ground of Venus, photographed by Venera 13. At the lower right are the lander's saw-toothed edge and the arm that tested the ground.
2015년 7월 뉴허라이즌스가 다가가며 찍은 명왕성에는 폭 1,600km: The photographs New Horizons took as it closed in on Pluto in July 2015 showed a bright heart about 1,600 km wide. It is named after Clyde Tombaugh, who found Pluto in 1930. The left half of the heart is Sputnik Planitia, covered in nitrogen ice: land so young that it has not one crater. The ice is warmed from below and churns slowly as if boiling, laying down a new surface.
Pluto, photographed by New Horizons. The bright heart is Tombaugh Regio.
토성 북극에는 북위 78도를 따라 여섯 변을 가진 구름 띠가 돌고 있습니: At Saturn's north pole a band of cloud with six sides turns along 78 degrees north. It was found in 1988 by looking again at photographs Voyager 2 took in 1981. Each side is about 14,500 km long, more than Earth is wide. It was still there when Cassini photographed it again in 2006. It is thought to be the shape made by a fast belt of wind as it ripples.
카시니가 찍은 토성 북극(2012년). 가운데가 소용돌이이고, 바깥쪽 모: Saturn's north pole, photographed by Cassini (2012). The whirl is in the middle; the angled band outside it is one side of the six-sided band of cloud.
The Naro Space Center is Korea's launch site, on the island of Oenarodo in Goheung, South Jeolla. On January 30, 2013, the rocket Naro put a satellite in orbit from here for the first time. On June 21, 2022, Nuri, with engines too built in Korea, put a test satellite up to 700 km. Danuri, which left for the Moon in August 2022, was launched from Florida in the United States.
Nuri leaving the Naro Space Center (its first launch, October 21, 2021).
America's MESSENGER became the first spacecraft to orbit Mercury in March 2011. In four years it mapped the whole of Mercury and found water ice inside polar craters where sunlight never comes. When its fuel ran out its orbit sank, and on April 30, 2015, it fell here at 3.9 km a second. It is thought to have made a new crater about 16 m across.
The land where MESSENGER fell (above) and the height of its last orbit (below).
코나마라 혼돈 지형은 유로파의 얼음 껍질이 조각조각 깨져 떠다니다가 다시: Conamara Chaos is where Europa's shell of ice broke into pieces that drifted and froze again. Photographs taken by Galileo in 1997 showed the pieces of ice turned and shifted like rafts. That means what lay under the ice was once water, or soft ice. Under Europa's shell there is thought to be more water than in all of Earth's seas together.
The rafts of ice of Conamara, photographed by Galileo.
소련의 베네라 7호는 1970년 12월 15일 금성에 내렸습니다. 낙하산: The Soviet Venera 7 landed on Venus on December 15, 1970. Its parachute tore, it hit at about 17 m a second and fell over, yet it sent a weak signal for 23 minutes: the first time a thing people made sent a signal from the surface of another planet. From that signal it was learned that the ground of Venus is at 475 degrees and the pressure about 90 times Earth's.
A model of the Venera 7 lander in a museum.
오카토르는 세레스에 있는 지름 92km의 충돌구입니다. 2015년 던이: Occator is a crater 92 km across on Ceres. In the photographs Dawn took as it drew near in 2015, the bright spots on its floor shone like a lighthouse and drew much attention. From close by they proved to be a deposit of sodium carbonate. Salt water is thought to have risen from underground: the water went and the salt stayed. It means salt water may still lie inside Ceres.
Occator Crater, photographed by Dawn. The white spots on its floor are salt.
미국 플로리다 케네디 우주센터의 39A 발사대입니다. 1969년 7월 1: Launch pad 39A at the Kennedy Space Center in Florida, USA. On July 16, 1969, the Saturn V rocket carrying Apollo 11 left from here, and four days later it landed on the Moon. Everyone who went to the Moon, from Apollo 8 to 17 and Apollo 13 among them, set out from here (only Apollo 10 used pad 39B next to it). Later the first and last flights of the space shuttle left from this pad too.
이소연은 2008년 4월 8일 카자흐스탄 바이코누르에서 소유스 TMA-1: Yi So-yeon left Baikonur in Kazakhstan aboard Soyuz TMA-12 on April 8, 2008. Two days later she reached the International Space Station, where she stayed about nine days and did eighteen experiments. It was the first space flight by a Korean. Coming back on April 19, the return capsule fell steeply and she bore more than 8 times Earth's gravity.
Yi So-yeon (left) with Yuri Malenchenko and Peggy Whitson on the International Space Station.
NASA (국제우주정거장 승무원 촬영): NASA (photo by the International Space Station crew)
크라켄 해는 타이탄 북극 가까이에 있는 가장 큰 바다로, 넓이가 40만: Kraken Mare is the largest sea on Titan, near its north pole, about 400,000 km² in area. Cassini's radar found it in 2007. It is filled not with water but with methane and ethane at minus 180 degrees. On Titan methane rains, runs in rivers and flows into the seas. Titan is the only place off the Earth where liquid stands on the surface.
카시니의 레이더로 본 크라켄 해. 검고 푸른 곳이 메탄 바다이고 노란 곳: Kraken Mare as seen by Cassini's radar. The black and blue parts are methane sea and the yellow is land (the colours are added).
카론의 북극에는 지름 375km쯤의 붉은 갈색 땅이 있습니다. 2015년: At Charon's north pole is a reddish brown land about 375 km across. New Horizons found it in 2015; it was nicknamed Mordor after a land in a novel, and its official name is now Neverland Regio. Methane escaped from Pluto's air is thought to freeze at Charon's cold pole and to be turned into red stuff by the ultraviolet in sunlight. Winter at Charon's poles lasts over 100 years and reaches minus 258 degrees.
Charon, photographed by New Horizons. The red part at the top is Mordor.
보이저 2호는 2018년 11월 5일 태양풍이 닿는 범위의 끝을 지났습니: On November 5, 2018, Voyager 2 passed the end of the reach of the solar wind: the second spacecraft to enter the space between the stars, after Voyager 1 in 2012. Unlike Voyager 1, its instrument for measuring plasma still worked, so it measured the very moment of crossing. It is also the only spacecraft to have visited Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune.
A drawing of Voyager 2 entering the space between the stars.
파커 태양 탐사선은 2018년 떠나 금성을 일곱 번 스치며 궤도를 줄였습: The Parker Solar Probe left in 2018 and shrank its orbit by skimming Venus seven times. On December 24, 2024, it came within 6.1 million km of the Sun's surface. Its speed then was 192 km a second, the fastest of anything people have made. The front of its carbon shield, 11 cm thick, heated to nearly 1,000 degrees, while the instruments behind stayed at about 30.
A drawing of the Parker Solar Probe nearing the Sun.
1989년 보이저 2호가 해왕성 남반구에서 지구만 한 검은 폭풍을 찍었습: In 1989 Voyager 2 photographed a dark storm the size of Earth in Neptune's southern half. It was like Jupiter's Great Red Spot, and so was called the Great Dark Spot. Round it blew winds of over 2,000 km an hour, the fastest in the solar system. When the Hubble Space Telescope looked again in 1994 it was gone. Since then similar dark spots have come and gone several times.
Neptune's Great Dark Spot, photographed by Voyager 2.
착륙 마지막 순간 컴퓨터가 고른 자리가 바위투성이여서 암스트롱이 손으로: In the last moments the place the computer picked was strewn with boulders, so Armstrong flew on past it by hand; less than a minute of fuel was left when they landed. The two stayed on the Moon 21 hours 36 minutes. Aldrin said the flag they planted was blown over by the engine as they left. The laser mirror they left is still in use.
원래는 미국 독립 200돌인 7월 4일에 내리려 했으나, 궤도에서 찍어: It was meant to land on July 4, the 200th birthday of the United States, but photographs from orbit showed the chosen place was too rough, and over two weeks went on finding a new one. The orbiter that came with it photographed all of Mars. In 1982 a wrong command sent from Earth turned its antenna away and contact was lost.
내려서는 72분 동안 신호를 보냈고, 전지가 다하기 전에 중계하던 카시니: After landing it sent signals for 72 minutes; before its battery ran out, Cassini, which was relaying them, sank below the horizon. The surface was at minus 179 degrees. It is named after Christiaan Huygens of the Netherlands, who found Titan in 1655.
마지막 다섯 달은 \"그랜드 피날레\"라 하여 토성과 고리 사이의 2,0: In its last five months, the "Grand Finale", it passed 22 times through the gap of about 2,000 km between Saturn and its rings, where no spacecraft had ever been. What it measured then showed that the rings may be far younger than Saturn.
가장 가까이 지나는 동안에는 관측에 바빠 지구와 교신하지 않았고, 무사하: At its nearest it was too busy observing to talk to Earth, and the signal that it was safe came only 13 hours later. Even light takes four and a half hours to cross that distance. Sending all it had gathered back to Earth took 16 months.
이름은 1301년에 본 핼리 혜성을 그림 속 베들레헴의 별로 그린 이탈리: It is named after Giotto, the Italian painter who put the Halley's Comet he saw in 1301 into a painting as the Star of Bethlehem. In 1986 five spacecraft went out to meet Halley, two Soviet Vegas and Japan's Suisei and Sakigake among them: the "Halley Armada". In 1992 Giotto also passed another comet, Grigg-Skjellerup.
지구에서 보낸 신호가 닿는 데 지금은 하루쯤 걸립니다. 전기는 플루토늄이: A signal from Earth now takes about a day to reach it. Its power comes from the heat of plutonium and falls by about 4 watts a year; by about 2030 it is thought no science instrument can be kept on. In about 40,000 years it will pass 1.6 light-years from a star in Camelopardalis.
이 사진은 모두 60장으로 이루어진 \"태양계 가족사진\"의 한 부분입니: This picture is one part of the "Family Portrait" of the solar system, 60 frames in all. Venus, Earth, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune are in it; Mercury was too near the Sun and Mars was lost in sunlight scattered in the camera. In 2020, for its 30th birthday, NASA brought out a new version made from the same data.
동도는 높이 98.6m, 서도는 168.5m입니다. 동도에는 등대와 경비: The east island is 98.6 m high and the west island 168.5 m. On the east island are a lighthouse and a guard post. Black-tailed gulls, storm petrels and shearwaters raise their young here, and the sea round it, where cold and warm waters meet, is full of fish.
가는 길에 나트륨 기체를 뿜어 주황빛 구름을 만들었고, 지구의 천문대들이: On the way it let out sodium gas to make an orange cloud, and observatories on Earth photographed it to check its path. It carried two metal balls stamped with the Soviet emblem, which scattered on impact. Eight months earlier Luna 1 had missed the Moon by about 6,000 km and become the first made thing to orbit the Sun.
사진 신호는 팩스와 같은 방식이어서, 영국 조드럴 뱅크 천문대가 받아 신: Its picture signal worked like a fax, so the Jodrell Bank Observatory in Britain received it, decoded it with a newspaper's machine and published it before the Soviet Union did. It sent several panoramas over three days and its battery ran out. It was a success after many failures.
서베이어는 모두 일곱 대를 보내 다섯 대가 내렸습니다. 1호는 첫 시도에: Seven Surveyors were sent in all and five landed. The first succeeded at the first try. Its own photographs showed that its footpads had sunk only a few cm into the ground.
티코는 달에서 아주 젊은 큰 분화구라 과학자들이 고른 자리입니다. 앞선: Tycho is a very young large crater on the Moon, and scientists chose the place. The six before it had studied landing places for Apollo; the seventh was purely for science. It also photographed laser beams fired at it from Earth.
번개에 계기가 모두 꺼졌을 때 관제사 존 에런이 \"SCE를 AUX로\": When the lightning knocked out all the instruments, the controller John Aaron remembered a switch, "SCE to AUX", and saved the mission. They took the first colour television camera to the Moon's surface, but it was pointed at the Sun by mistake and ruined. The parts of Surveyor 3 they brought back showed how a machine changes in two and a half years on the Moon.
아폴로 11호와 12호가 이미 사람 손으로 돌을 가져온 뒤였지만, 사람을: Apollo 11 and 12 had already brought rock back by hand, but this showed it could be done without sending people. The capsule came down in Kazakhstan. Luna 20 and 24 later brought soil too: the Soviet Moon samples come to about 300 g in all.
달의 밤 2주 동안은 뚜껑을 닫고 방사성 물질의 열로 버텼고, 낮에는 뚜: Through the two weeks of the lunar night it shut its lid and kept warm on the heat of radioactive material; by day it charged from the solar cells inside the lid. Its place was later lost, then found again in 2010 in a photograph by the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter, and its mirror still sends laser light back.
셰퍼드는 1961년 미국인으로 처음 우주에 나간 사람으로, 귓병을 고치고: Shepard was the first American in space, in 1961; cured of an ear trouble, he came back ten years later and walked on the Moon. The two turned back without finding the rim of Cone Crater; it turned out later that they had come within about 20 m of it. Stuart Roosa in the command ship circled the Moon with hundreds of tree seeds, and the "Moon trees" grown from them were planted in many places.
떠나기 전 스콧은 숨진 우주비행사 14명의 이름을 새긴 판과 작은 알루미: Before leaving, Scott laid on the Moon a plaque with the names of 14 astronauts who had died and a small aluminium figure, the "Fallen Astronaut". 태양의 홍염이 가끔 끊어져 날아가고, 작은 혜성이 해로 뛰어들어 사라집니: Now and then a prominence on the Sun tears loose and flies off, and a small comet dives into the Sun and is gone.
태양 가장자리에서 가끔 플레어가 번쩍하고, 목성의 띠가 서로 다른 빠르기: A flare flashes at the Sun's edge now and then, and Jupiter's belts flow at different speeds.
Close to the ground on Mars you can see the dark tracks left by dust devils.
Uranus has thin rings and an aurora.
금성의 밤 쪽이 어렴풋이 빛나고 가끔 번개가 칩니다. 혜성의 가스 꼬리가: The night side of Venus glows faintly and lightning strikes now and then. A comet's gas tail sometimes breaks off.
금성이나 수성이 태양 앞을 지나는 자리에 서면 태양면 통과를 알려 줍니다: Stand where Venus or Mercury passes in front of the Sun and the game tells you of the transit.
소라가 말이 많아졌습니다. 가까운 천체 이야기, 뒤를 볼 때, 사진을 찍: Sora talks more: about the body nearby, when looking back, when taking a photo, when seeing a sight.
별자리와 은하, 성단의 이름이 휴대전화에서도 뜨고, 화면 가운데로 바라보: Names of constellations, galaxies and clusters show on a phone too, with a line about the one at the middle of the screen.
하늘에 히아데스, 벌집성단, 이중성단, 큰부리새자리 47, 프톨레마이오스: The sky has the Hyades, the Beehive, the Double Cluster, 47 Tucanae, the Ptolemy Cluster and the Coalsack.
The game starts at sunrise over Earth's night side.
설정과 도움말에도 글자 크기 단추(가−, 가+)가 생겼습니다. 수첩과 함: The settings and the help have text size buttons too. They change together with the notebook.

The night side of the Moon and of other moons shows dimly in light thrown back by their planet (earthshine).
대기광, 토성 육각형, 타이탄·명왕성·화성의 안개 고리에 알림이 붙었습니: Notices added for airglow, Saturn's hexagon and the haze rings of Titan, Pluto and Mars.
The version line moved from the note to the top of the settings, beside the title.
오로라, 번개 같은 볼거리 알림은 하루에 한 번만 뜹니다. 열 때마다 되: Notices of sights such as auroras and lightning come up once a day only, not at every opening.
별자리 선이 태양 위로 지나가 보이던 것을 고쳤습니다. 태양이 뒤의 선과: Fixed constellation lines showing across the Sun. The Sun hides the lines and stars behind it.
수첩의 사진첩에 \"지나온 길 돌아보기\"가 생겼습니다. 찍은 사진이 오: The album has "Look back on the way": your photos pass one by one from the oldest.
넓은 화면에서 움직임 단추 넷이 오른쪽 아래에 나란히 서고, 화면 밖 화: On a wide screen the four move buttons stand in a row at the lower right, and off-screen arrows keep clear of the minimap and the target panel.
휴대전화에서 화면 밖 화살표가 고도 표시와 목적지 칸을 가리지 않고 그: On a phone the off-screen arrows no longer cover the altitude and the target panel but show below them.
\"다음 곡\" 단추를 누르면 곡이 바로 바뀌고, 단추 옆에 곡 이름이: Press "Next tune" and the music changes at once, with the tune's name beside the button.
The paper-doll character is gone. The only character is pixel-art Sora.
Fixed the Moon's midday ground washing out to white beside Danuri.
화면 위 오른쪽 끝에 설정 단추가 생겼습니다. 최근 1주일 동안 바뀐 것: A settings button at the top right corner. See there what changed in the last week.
한국어 기기에서는 도킹과 착륙을 한국어로 셉니다. \"도킹 준비 중. 삼: On a Korean device the docking and landing counts are spoken in Korean.
Removed the notice that came up when the tune changed.
The four move buttons are now as large as the buttons at the top.
미니맵에서 지구와 그 바깥 행성 옆에 영어 이름 첫 글자가 붙습니다. 토: On the minimap, Earth and the planets beyond it carry the first letter of their English names. Saturn is S.
Between Earth and the Moon, an arrow toward the Moon shows too.
목성과 토성 위로 위성의 그림자가 지나갑니다. 언제 지나가는지는 수첩의: Shadows of moons cross Jupiter and Saturn. The notebook's "Sky news" tells when.
The loading screen lifts as soon as the game is ready.
The version moved to the foot of grandma's note.
Touched up the looks of Triton, Neptune's Great Dark Spot, the small moons and the comets.
The notebook's text size can be changed with its two buttons.
볼거리 아홉이 늘었습니다. 토성의 오로라, 지구의 야광운, 핼리 혜성의: Nine more sights: Saturn's aurora, Earth's night-shining clouds, the jets of Halley's Comet and others.
The notes of 1969, 1979 and 1986 are read over four pages.
묘기 비행 넷이 생겼습니다: 달까지 달리기, 달 스치기, 지구 한 바퀴,: Four stunts: a run to the Moon, skimming the Moon, once around Earth, through the gap in Saturn's rings.
찍은 사진을 엽서 그림으로 저장할 수 있습니다. 할머니의 답장도 사진마다: A photo can be saved as a postcard picture. Grandma's reply differs with each photo.
발사대, 착륙선, 탐사차 모형이 이야기 장소에 섭니다. 밤인 곳은 살펴보: Models of launch pads, landers and rovers stand at the story places. Where it is night, a light shines while you look.
The game clock now runs at 50 times real time. A day on Earth takes 29 minutes.
게임 시계를 실제의 100배로 늦췄습니다. 배경 음악이 열한 곡으로 늘었: The game clock is slowed to 100 times real time. The background music grew to eleven tracks.
이야기 「할머니의 수첩」이 들어왔습니다. 할머니의 쪽지, 천체마다의 메모: The story "Grandma's Notes" is in: grandma's notes, a memo for every body, and the last slot.
Send grandma a photo postcard and a reply and stars come the next day.
여행 코스 아홉 개와 오늘의 부탁이 생겼습니다. 이야기 카드마다 문제가: Nine tours and a request for each day. Every story card has a question.
Twenty story places beyond the Moon and Mars, with their photos.
Sora talks to herself. Five little companions can follow her.
태양의 홍염과 코로나, 성운 셋, 혜성의 먼지 꼬리, 토성의 육각형이 생: The Sun's prominences and corona, three nebulae, a comet's dust tail and Saturn's hexagon.
수첩이 갈래별 쪽으로 나뉘었습니다. 휴대전화 화면의 이름표와 글자를 크게: The notebook is divided into tabs. Labels and text on a phone are much smaller.
넓은 창에서는 휴대전화 모양 틀 안에 게임이 뜹니다. 화면 글씨가 프리텐: In a wide window the game shows inside a phone-shaped frame. The screen font is now Pretendard.
The minimap, the Milky Way, twenty constellations and four nearby galaxies.
Twelve moons, Ceres, Pluto, Charon, Halley's Comet and the asteroid belt.
탐사선과 망원경 스물두 대에 도킹할 수 있습니다. 붙을 때 숫자를 세어: You can dock with twenty-two probes and telescopes. A voice counts as you close in.
달과 화성의 착륙지 서른두 곳, 독도, 달의 명소 열두 곳이 이야기 장소: Thirty-two landing sites on the Moon and Mars, Dokdo and twelve sights of the Moon became story places.
Press the label of a place you have been to and jump there. There is a photo album.
Saturn's rings are drawn down to their gaps, and ice grains scatter as you pass through.
오늘의 하늘 배치, 배경 음악 여섯 곡, 첫 안내, 천체마다 사실 한 문: Today's real sky, six tracks of background music, a first guide and one fact for every body.
주인공이 도트 그림 소라로 바뀌었습니다. 키를 놓으면 그 속도로 계속 납: The heroine is now pixel-art Sora. Let go of the key and she keeps flying at that speed.
만들기 시작했습니다. 태양과 여덟 행성, 달 사이를 실제 크기대로 납니다: The making began. Fly among the Sun, the eight planets and the Moon at their real sizes.
The explorer's notebook and eight photo tasks.
Sound effects, and the game can be installed as an app that runs without the internet.
The name was settled: Space Oddity.
설정의 \"Changes\"가 만들기 시작한 날부터의 기록을 모두 보여: "Changes" in the settings shows everything since the day the making began.
우주멍: 글자와 단추 숨기기: Just looking: hide the words and buttons
우주멍 끝내기: 모두 다시 보이기: Stop just looking: show everything again
Tab 키 / 오른쪽 아래 구석의 달 모양 단추. 글자, 단추, 이름표를: Tab key / the moon-shaped button in the lower right corner. It hides every word, button and label and leaves only the view. Drag the screen to look around, and press it again to bring them back.
오른쪽 아래 구석에 우주멍 단추가 생겼습니다. 누르면 글자와 단추가 모두: A "just looking" button in the lower right corner. Press it and every word and button goes, leaving only the view.
목표 고정이 땅과 함께 돌아 같은 곳 위에 머뭅니다. 화면을 끌어 둘러봐: The target lock turns with the ground and stays over the same spot. Dragging to look around no longer lets go.
Lightning flickers inside the typhoon on the night side and shows its spiral.
화성의 먼지 회오리가 휘어 선 먼지 기둥이 되어 감아 돌고, 땅에 긴 그: Mars's dust devils are now bent columns of dust that wind as they turn and lay long shadows on the ground.
에트나 화산이 짙은 화산재를 뿜고 90초마다 터집니다. 분화구가 붉게 타: Etna pours out dark ash and bursts every 90 seconds. Its crater burns red, and lava runs down by night.
별똥별이 굵고 밝아져 흰빛, 초록, 금빛, 푸른빛으로 타고, 가끔 불덩이: Shooting stars are thicker and brighter, burning white, green, gold and blue, and now and then a fireball bursts. A shower comes every two minutes.
크루 드래건의 발사 장면에 소리가 납니다. 엔진이 울리고, 단이 갈라지고: Crew Dragon's launch has sound: the engines roar, the stages part, and the first stage lights again.
이것은 한 사람에게는 작은 한 걸음이지만: That's one small step for a man…
통. 통. 통. 이거 재밌는데?: Boing. Boing. Boing. This is fun!
야호! 닐에게는 작은 걸음, 나한테는 큰 걸음: Whoopie! Small for Neil, long for me
1968년 1월 10일. 서베이어 일곱 대 가운데 마지막인 7호가 달 남: January 10, 1968. Surveyor 7, the last of the seven Surveyors, comes down toward the Moon's southern highlands.
앞서 내린 넷은 모두 평평한 용암 평원을 골랐습니다. 이번 목표는 티코에: The four that landed before it all chose flat lava plains. This time the target is a field of rocks thrown out of Tycho.
01시 05분(세계시), 무게 306kg의 몸이 티코 북쪽 가장자리 바깥: At 01:05 (Universal Time) its 306 kg body stood on three legs outside the northern rim of Tycho.
사진 21,091장을 보내고 삽으로 흙을 팠습니다. 2월 21일에 마지막: It sent 21,091 photographs and dug the soil with its scoop. Its last signal stopped on February 21.
세기의 사진을 찍다: Taking the picture of the century
1966년 11월 24일. 루나 오비터 2호가 아폴로가 내릴 자리를 찾아: November 24, 1966. Lunar Orbiter 2 is circling low over the Moon, looking for places where Apollo can land.
높이 46km, 분화구에서 남쪽으로 240km 떨어진 곳. 카메라가 아래: It is 46 km up, 240 km south of the crater. The camera looks not down but toward the horizon.
찰칵. 지름 93km 분화구의 계단진 벽과 가운데 봉우리가 산 위에서 보: Click. The terraced walls and central peaks of the crater, 93 km across, were caught at a slant, as if seen from a mountain top.
그때까지 달 사진은 거의 위에서 내려다본 것이었습니다. 신문들은 이 한: Until then almost every photograph of the Moon had looked straight down. The newspapers called this one the "picture of the century".
1965년 2월 20일. 미국의 레인저 8호가 사흘을 날아 고요의 바다로: February 20, 1965. America's Ranger 8, after three days of flight, falls straight toward the Sea of Tranquility.
높이 2,510km에서 카메라 여섯 대가 켜집니다. 부딪히기 전 23분: At a height of 2,510 km its six cameras come on. In the 23 minutes before it hits, it sends 7,137 pictures.
초속 2.7km로 부딪혔습니다. 마지막 사진에는 크기 1.5m의 것까지: It hit at 2.7 km a second. The last pictures showed things as small as 1.5 m across.
바다는 사람이 내릴 만큼 평평했습니다. 4년 뒤 아폴로 11호가 여기서: The sea was flat enough for people to land on. Four years later Apollo 11 landed about 70 km from here.
비의 바다를 만든 충돌: The impact that made the Sea of Rains
39억 년 전. 지름 250km쯤의 작은 행성 하나가 달의 앞면 북쪽으로: 3.9 billion years ago. A small planet about 250 km across draws near the north of the Moon's near side.
이 무렵 달에는 큰 충돌이 잇따랐습니다. 이번 것은 그 가운데서도 손꼽히: Great impacts came one after another on the Moon around this time. This one is among the very largest of them.
부딪혔습니다. 지름 1,100km가 넘는 분지가 파이고, 둘레의 땅이 5: It hit. A basin more than 1,100 km across is dug, and the land round it is pushed up more than 5 km to become mountain ranges.
튀어 나간 돌은 800km 밖까지 긴 홈을 팠습니다. 그 뒤 용암이 2: The rocks thrown out cut long grooves as far as 800 km away. Later lava rose 2 → 5 km deep in it and made it a sea.
미안. 좀 세게 부딪혔네: Sorry. I hit a bit hard
1651년. 이탈리아 볼로냐의 예수회 신부 리치올리가 1,500쪽이 넘는: 1651. Riccioli, a Jesuit priest of Bologna in Italy, brings out a book of astronomy of more than 1,500 pages.
책에는 동료 그리말디가 망원경으로 보고 그린 달 지도가 실렸습니다. 이름: In the book was a map of the Moon that his colleague Grimaldi drew from what he saw through a telescope. Riccioli gave the names.
서쪽의 가장 넓은 어두운 땅에는 \"폭풍의 대양\"이라고 적었습니다. 달: On the widest dark land in the west he wrote "Ocean of Storms". It was a time when people believed the Moon changed the weather.
고요의 바다, 티코, 코페르니쿠스도 이 지도에서 나온 이름입니다. 370: The Sea of Tranquility, Tycho and Copernicus are names from this map too. 370 years on, they are still used as they were.
달에서 가장 큰 충돌: The largest impact on the Moon
42억 5,000만 년 전. 지름 200km쯤의 천체가 달의 남쪽으로 비: 4.25 billion years ago. A body about 200 km across flies in at a slant toward the south of the Moon.
땅과 이루는 각도는 30도 아래로 봅니다. 달이 생긴 지 3억 년이 채: Its angle with the ground is thought to be under 30 degrees. Not quite 300 million years have passed since the Moon was formed.
부딪혔습니다. 지름 2,500km, 깊이 8km의 분지가 파입니다. 달: It hit. A basin 2,500 km across and 8 km deep is dug. Its width is close to a quarter of the way round the Moon.
In June 2024 Chang'e 6 brought back 1,935 g of soil from inside it. The age of the impact was measured from those rocks.
가구야가 섀클턴 바닥을 보다: Kaguya sees the floor of Shackleton
2007년 11월 19일. 일본의 가구야가 달 남극 위를 지납니다. 섀클: November 19, 2007. Japan's Kaguya passes over the Moon's south pole. The floor of Shackleton is always in shadow.
태양은 가장자리 안쪽 벽의 윗부분만 비춥니다. 그 벽에서 되비친 희미한: The Sun lights only the upper part of the inner wall of the rim. Faint light thrown back from that wall reaches the floor.
찰칵. 10m까지 가려내는 카메라가 처음으로 바닥을 찍었습니다. 드러난: Click. A camera that can make out things 10 m across photographed the floor for the first time. No bare ice was seen.
바닥은 영하 183도 아래로 어림됐습니다. 2023년에는 다누리의 섀도캠: The floor was reckoned to be below minus 183 degrees. In 2023 Danuri's ShadowCam photographed it more sharply.
1971년 7월 30일. 아폴로 15호의 착륙선 팰컨이 아펜니노 산맥을: July 30, 1971. Falcon, the lander of Apollo 15, crosses the Apennine Mountains on its way down.
산을 넘자마자 내려야 해서 내려가는 각도가 26도입니다. 앞선 착륙의 1: It must land as soon as it is over the mountains, so it comes down at an angle of 26 degrees: far steeper than the 15 degrees of the landings before.
22시 16분(세계시), 높이 3.5km의 해들리 델타 산 아래에 섰습니: At 22:16 (Universal Time) it stood at the foot of Mount Hadley Delta, 3.5 km high. It was 550 m from its target.
스콧과 어윈은 67시간쯤 머물렀습니다. 처음 실어 간 월면차로 27.9k: Scott and Irwin stayed about 67 hours. In the first Moon car ever taken there they drove 27.9 km, and they brought back 77 kg of rock.
알프스 계곡을 내려다보다: Looking down on the Alpine Valley
1967년 8월 14일. 루나 오비터 5호가 달의 북극과 남극 위를 지나: August 14, 1967. Lunar Orbiter 5 is circling on a path that passes over the Moon's north and south poles.
다섯 대 가운데 마지막입니다. 착륙 후보지는 앞선 탐사선들이 찍어 두어,: It is the last of the five. The earlier probes have already photographed the candidate landing places, so this time it mostly photographs places chosen by scientists.
찰칵. 302km 거리에서 알프스 산맥을 곧게 가르는 골짜기가 끝에서 끝: Click. From 302 km away, the valley that cuts straight through the Alps was caught from end to end in one picture.
함께 찍은 고해상도 사진에는 바닥의 가는 홈도 보였습니다. 폭 600m쯤: The high-resolution picture taken with it showed the thin groove on the floor too. About 600 m wide, it could barely be seen from Earth.
1686년 5월 30일. 네덜란드의 하위헌스가 초점 거리 123피트의 긴: May 30, 1686. Huygens of the Netherlands turns a long telescope with a focal length of 123 feet on the Moon.
토성의 고리와 타이탄을 찾아낸 사람입니다. 이제 쉰일곱 살이고, 렌즈는: He is the man who found Saturn's ring and Titan. He is now fifty-seven, and he ground the lens with his own hands.
구름의 바다에서 자로 그은 듯한 곧은 선이 보였습니다. 그는 이틀 밤에: In the Sea of Clouds he saw a straight line, as if drawn with a ruler. He drew it over two nights.
그림은 1925년에야 전집에 실려 알려졌습니다. 길이 110km, 높이: The drawing became known only in 1925, when it was printed in his collected works. It is a fault slope 110 km long and 240 → 300 m high.

The Tanegashima Space Center stands on the shore of Tanegashima, an island south of Kyushu in Japan. It opened in 1969 and is the largest launch site in Japan. Set between blue sea and green headlands, it is sometimes called the most beautiful launch site in the world. On September 7, 2023, H-IIA Flight 47 left its Yoshinobu launch complex carrying the X-ray telescope XRISM and the Moon lander SLIM. SLIM landed on the Moon four months later, on January 20, 2024, and Japan became the fifth country to land there.

From 2001 to June 2025 it flew fifty times and succeeded forty-nine times. Tanegashima is also the island where firearms first reached Japan, in 1543. The nearer a launch site is to the equator, the more help it gets from the turning of the Earth. That is why this island south of the main islands was chosen.

오는 길에 목성의 중력을 빌려 방향을 틀고, 태양계를 가로질러 날아왔습니: On the way it borrowed Jupiter's gravity to turn, and flew across the solar system.
고리 바깥을 지나 구름 꼭대기 위 2만 1천km를 스칩니다. 고리 평면을: It passes outside the rings and skims 21,000 km above the cloud tops. Everyone held their breath as it crossed the ring plane.
새 고리 F를 찾았고, 모르고 있던 작은 위성 곁을 수천km 차이로 스쳐: It found a new ring, F, and brushed past a small unknown moon with a few thousand km to spare.
뒤따르던 보이저 1호와 2호는 이 길이 안전한 것을 알고 왔습니다. 신호: Voyager 1 and 2, coming behind, knew this way was safe. Its signal ended in November 1995.
2019년 1월 1일. 명왕성을 지난 지 3년 반, 뉴허라이즌스가 카이퍼: 1 January 2019. Three and a half years after passing Pluto, New Horizons nears Arrokoth, a small body in the Kuiper belt.
태양에서 65억km. 사람이 만든 것이 찾아간 가장 먼 천체입니다. 신호: 6.5 billion km from the Sun. It is the farthest body anything made by people has visited. A signal takes six hours to reach Earth.
3,500km 곁을 초속 14km로 지나갑니다. 길이 36km, 붉은 덩: It passes 3,500 km away at 14 km a second. Arrokoth was 36 km long and shaped like a snowman: two red lumps joined together.
둘은 아주 천천히 다가와 살며시 붙었습니다. 45억 년 전 행성이 만들어: The two drew near very slowly and gently joined. It is just as it was 4.5 billion years ago, when the planets were forming.
아로코스는 포우하탄 말로 하늘이라는 뜻입니다. 뉴허라이즌스는 지금도 태양: Arrokoth means sky in the Powhatan language. New Horizons is still flying out of the solar system.
2024년 10월 14일 유로파 클리퍼가 떠났습니다. 날개를 펴면 30m: Europa Clipper left on 14 October 2024. Over 30 m with its wings spread, it is the largest probe NASA has sent to a planet.
목성까지 곧장 갈 힘은 없습니다. 먼저 화성 곁을 지나며 그 중력으로 길: It lacks the power to go straight to Jupiter. First it passes Mars and uses its gravity to change course.
2025년 3월 1일, 화성 위 884km를 지나갑니다. 지나는 김에 열: On 1 March 2025 it passes 884 km above Mars. On the way by, it tested its thermal camera and radar.
2026년 12월에는 지구 곁을 지나며 속도를 얻습니다. 29억km를 날: In December 2026 it passes Earth and gains speed. It flies 2.9 billion km and reaches Jupiter in April 2030.
목성의 달 유로파를 49번 스쳐 지나며 얼음 밑 바다를 살핍니다. 지구의: It skims Jupiter's moon Europa 49 times to study the sea under the ice: about twice the water of all Earth's oceans together.
2023년 11월 1일. 목성 트로이 소행성으로 가던 루시가 연습 삼아: 1 November 2023. Lucy, on its way to Jupiter's Trojan asteroids, passes the small asteroid Dinkinesh as practice.
초속 4.5km, 430km 거리. 카메라 받침대가 소행성을 놓치지 않고: 4.5 km a second, 430 km away. Today tests whether the camera platform can turn to follow the asteroid without losing it.
너비 790m인 소행성 뒤에서 작은 달이 나타났습니다. 아무도 모르던 달: From behind the asteroid, 790 m wide, a small moon appeared. A moon nobody knew of.
더 지나가서 보니 그 달은 덩어리 둘이 붙은 것이었습니다. 이런 달은 처: From farther on, the moon proved to be two lumps joined together. No such moon had been seen before. Its name is Selam.
루시는 12년 동안 소행성 열한 곳을 찾아갑니다. 이름은 320만 년 전: Lucy visits eleven asteroids in 12 years. Its name comes from Lucy, a human fossil 3.2 million years old.
2012년 8월 6일. 화성 정찰 궤도선이 화성을 돕니다. 오늘은 땅이: 6 August 2012. Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter circles Mars. Today it must photograph the sky, not the ground.
큐리오시티가 대기로 뛰어들었습니다. 낙하산에 매달려 있는 시간은 2분도: Curiosity has plunged into the air. It hangs under its parachute for less than 2 minutes.
찰칵. 340km 떨어진 곳에서 낙하산과 그 아래 매달린 탐사차를 찍었습: Click. From 340 km away it caught the parachute and the rover hanging below it. The parachute is 16 m across.
2008년 피닉스가 내려올 때도 이렇게 찍었습니다. 다른 행성에 내리는: It took a picture like this in 2008 too, when Phoenix came down. That was the first picture ever of a landing on another planet.
2006년 3월에 도착해 지금껏 화성을 돕니다. 카메라는 300km 높이: It arrived in March 2006 and circles Mars to this day. From 300 km up, its camera can make out something the size of a desk.
2009년 6월 18일 떠난 달 정찰 궤도선이 나흘 반 만에 달에 닿았습: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter left on 18 June 2009 and reached the Moon in four and a half days. It came to make the most detailed map of the Moon.
7월, 카메라를 시험하며 아폴로가 내렸던 자리 위를 지납니다. 40년 만: In July, testing its camera, it passes over the places where Apollo landed. They are seen again after 40 years.
찰칵. 착륙선의 아랫단이 그대로 서 있고 긴 그림자가 졌습니다. 7월 1: Click. The lander's lower stage still stands, casting a long shadow. The pictures were released on 17 July.
나중에 더 낮게 날며 찍은 사진에는 우주인들이 걸어 다닌 발자국 길과 월: Later pictures, taken from lower down, show even the trails of the astronauts' footprints and the tracks of the rover's wheels.
달의 남극에서는 영하 238도인 그늘을 쟀습니다. 태양계에서 잰 가장 추: At the Moon's south pole it measured shade at minus 238 degrees. It is among the coldest places measured in the solar system.
2022년 8월 5일 한국의 첫 달 탐사선 다누리가 떠났습니다. 연료를: Danuri, Korea's first Moon probe, left on 5 August 2022. To save fuel it chose a roundabout way of four and a half months.
태양 쪽으로 155만km까지 나갔다가 돌아옵니다. 가는 길에 지구와 달을: It goes out 1.55 million km toward the Sun and comes back. On the way it took a picture with Earth and the Moon in one frame.
12월 17일 새벽, 엔진을 13분 동안 켜 속도를 줄입니다. 달의 중력: Before dawn on 17 December it fires its engine for 13 minutes to slow down. The Moon's gravity has caught it.
다섯 번에 나눠 줄일 계획이었지만 세 번 만에 해냈습니다. 12월 27일: The plan was to slow in five burns, but it did it in three. On 27 December it entered an orbit 100 km above the Moon.
한국은 달에 탐사선을 보낸 일곱 번째 나라가 됐습니다. 싣고 간 카메라는: Korea became the seventh country to send a probe to the Moon. Its camera photographs the insides of craters where sunlight never reaches.
2009년 3월 7일 케플러가 떠났습니다. 백조자리와 거문고자리 사이,: Kepler left on 7 March 2009. For four years it gazes at just one patch of sky, between Cygnus and Lyra.
별 15만 개의 밝기를 30분마다 잽니다. 행성이 별 앞을 지나면 별빛이: It measures the brightness of 150,000 stars every 30 minutes. When a planet passes in front of a star, the starlight dims very slightly.
When a planet the size of Earth covers a star the size of the Sun, the light drops by about 1/10,000. Three repeats, and it counts as a planet.
이렇게 행성 2,600개 넘게를 찾았습니다. 별에는 행성이 있는 것이 보: It found more than 2,600 planets this way. We learned that it is usual for a star to have planets.
2013년 자세를 잡는 바퀴가 고장 났지만 햇빛의 미는 힘으로 균형을 잡: In 2013 a wheel that held it steady broke, but it balanced on the push of sunlight and worked on. In 2018 its fuel ran out and it went to sleep.
On 23 July 1999 Chandra goes up aboard the space shuttle Columbia. Commander Eileen Collins is the first woman to command a shuttle.
왕복선이 올린 것 가운데 가장 무거운 짐이었습니다. 엑스선은 공기에 막혀: It was the heaviest load a shuttle ever lifted. X-rays are stopped by the air and never reach the ground, so they must be seen from space.
It circles in a long orbit that goes out a third of the way from Earth to the Moon. On 12 August it opens its cover.
8월 19일, 첫 사진입니다. 320년쯤 전에 터진 별의 잔해 카시오페이: 19 August: the first picture. Cassiopeia A, the remains of a star that blew up some 320 years ago, and at its heart a dot nobody had seen.
터지고 남은 중성자별이었습니다. 찬드라는 그 뒤로 블랙홀과 은하단을 25: It was the neutron star left by the blast. Chandra has since watched black holes and galaxy clusters for over 25 years.
2023년 7월 1일 유럽의 유클리드가 떠났습니다. 한 달 뒤 지구에서: Europe's Euclid left on 1 July 2023. A month later it reached its post, 1.5 million km from Earth.
지름 1.2m 거울로 하늘을 한 조각씩 찍어 이어 붙입니다. 한 번에 보: With a mirror 1.2 m across it photographs the sky patch by patch and joins them. Each shot holds the area of two and a half full Moons.
6년 동안 하늘의 3분의 1, 은하 수십억 개를 담습니다. 100억 년: In six years it takes in a third of the sky and billions of galaxies. It sees galaxies as they were 10 billion years ago.
은하의 모양이 조금씩 찌그러진 것을 재면, 보이지 않는 암흑 물질이 어디: By measuring how the shapes of galaxies are slightly bent, we can tell where the unseen dark matter lies.
우주의 95%는 암흑 물질과 암흑 에너지입니다. 그것이 무엇인지는 아직: 95% of the universe is dark matter and dark energy. Nobody yet knows what they are.
2021년 4월 29일, 중국의 우주정거장 톈궁의 첫 조각 톈허가 올라갑: 29 April 2021. Tianhe, the first piece of China's space station Tiangong, goes up. It is 16.6 m long: the room where people live.
6월 17일 선저우 12호가 첫 세 사람을 태우고 와 붙습니다. 셋은 석: On 17 June Shenzhou 12 arrives with the first three people and docks. The three stayed three months.
2022년 7월 24일 실험실 원톈이 옵니다. 앞문에 붙은 뒤 옆문으로: On 24 July 2022 the laboratory Wentian arrives. It docks at the front port, then is moved to a side port.
10월 31일 두 번째 실험실 멍톈이 올라갑니다. 11월 3일 옆문으로: On 31 October the second laboratory, Mengtian, goes up. On 3 November it moves to a side port, making a T: a year and a half after the first piece.
무게는 국제우주정거장의 4분의 1쯤입니다. 세 사람이 여섯 달씩 번갈아: It weighs about a quarter of the International Space Station. Crews of three take turns living there, six months each.
도킹하는 탐사선 스물둘 모두에 그날로 장면이 생겼습니다. 해왕성, 아로코: All 22 craft you dock with now have a "That day" scene. 13 are new: Neptune, Arrokoth, building Tiangong…
1954년 8월 10일. 동도 북쪽 옛 선착장 곁, 바다에서 5m 솟은: 10 August 1954. By the old pier on the north of the east island, iron posts go up on a rock 5 m above the sea.
높이 10m의 네모난 철탑입니다. 지키는 사람 없이 혼자 켜지는 무인 등: It is a square iron tower 10 m tall. It was an unmanned lighthouse that lit by itself, with no keeper.
불이 켜졌습니다. 독도 등대의 첫 불빛이 동해를 지나는 배들에게 섬이 여: The light is on. The first light of Dokdo Lighthouse tells ships crossing the East Sea that the island is here.
1998년 12월 10일, 동도 꼭대기에 높이 15m의 흰 등대가 새로: On 10 December 1998 a new white lighthouse 15 m tall stood on top of the east island. Since then people have kept it.
불빛은 10초에 한 번 깜빡이고 46km 밖까지 닿습니다. 등대원들이 번: The light flashes once every 10 seconds and reaches 46 km. The keepers take turns staying on the island.
독도에 내려서면 그날로 갑니다. 1954년 첫 등대에 불이 켜지고 빛줄기: Land at Dokdo for "That day": in 1954 its first lighthouse is lit and the beam sweeps the sea.
그날로 장면에 금빛 줄이 생겨 얼마나 남았는지 보이고, 끝나면 알려 줍니: A gold line now shows how much of a "That day" scene is left, and a note says when it ends.
우주는 진공이라 실제로는 아무 소리도 들리지 않습니다. 엔진 소리와 착륙: Space is a vacuum, so in truth nothing can be heard there. The sounds of engines and landings were put in to make the scenes better to watch.
착륙 장면마다 소리가 납니다. 엔진이 울리고, 낙하산에 바람이 일고, 공: Every landing scene has sound: engines roar, wind fills the parachute, air bags bounce.
달의 여덟 곳에서 그날을 다시 봅니다. 떠나고, 내리고, 굴러 나오고,: Eight places on the Moon play their day again: leaving, landing, rolling out, falling over, hitting.
1972년 12월 14일. 서넌과 슈미트가 사흘을 머문 타우루스-리트로: December 14, 1972. Cernan and Schmitt make ready to leave the Taurus-Littrow valley, where they have stayed three days.
상승단이 하강단을 발사대 삼아 솟구칩니다. 금박 조각이 사방으로 흩어집니: The ascent stage leaps up, using the descent stage as its launch pad. Scraps of gold foil fly off every way.
이 장면은 두고 온 월면차의 카메라가 찍었습니다. 지구에서 2초 앞을 내: The camera on the rover they left behind filmed this. It was worked from Earth, and each command to tilt it up was sent two seconds early.
그 뒤로 달에 간 사람은 없습니다. 하강단과 월면차와 깃발은 지금도 그: No one has been to the Moon since. The descent stage, the rover and the flag are still there.
1970년 9월 20일 밤, 루나 16호가 풍요의 바다에 내렸습니다. 속: On the night of September 20, 1970, Luna 16 landed in the Sea of Fertility. Its hollow drill goes 35 cm into the ground.
이튿날, 흙 101g을 담은 공 모양 캡슐을 실은 로켓이 착륙선을 딛고: The next day a rocket carrying a ball-shaped capsule with 101 g of soil leaves straight up from the lander's back.
똑바로 올라가기만 하면 지구에 닿는 자리를 골라 내렸습니다. 가는 길에: It had landed at a place chosen so that going straight up was enough to reach Earth. It did not steer once on the way.
사흘 뒤 캡슐이 카자흐스탄에 떨어졌습니다. 로봇이 다른 천체의 흙을 가져: Three days later the capsule came down in Kazakhstan. It was the first time a robot brought back soil from another world.
1970년 11월 17일. 루나 17호가 비의 바다로 내려옵니다. 등에: November 17, 1970. Luna 17 comes down toward the Sea of Rains. On its back it carries a car with eight wheels.
내려앉자 경사로가 펴지고, 무게 756kg의 루노호트 1호가 천천히 굴러: Once it is down the ramps unfold, and Lunokhod 1, weighing 756 kg, slowly rolls down.
지구 밖의 천체를 달린 첫 차입니다. 소련의 다섯 사람이 화면을 보며 지: It was the first car to drive on a world other than Earth. Five people in the Soviet Union drove it from Earth, watching a screen.
낮에는 뚜껑의 태양 전지로 달리고 밤에는 뚜껑을 닫고 견뎠습니다. 열 달: By day it ran on the solar cells in its lid; by night it shut the lid and held out. In ten months it went 10.5 km.
2024년 1월 20일. 일본의 슬림이 시올리 분화구 곁, 목표에서 10: January 20, 2024. Japan's SLIM comes down beside the crater Shioli, aiming to land within 100 m of its mark.
높이 50m에서 주 엔진 둘 가운데 하나의 노즐이 떨어져 나갑니다. 몸이: At a height of 50 m the nozzle of one of its two main engines breaks off. It is pushed sideways.
닿기 직전 작은 로봇 둘을 내던지고, 슬림은 목표에서 55m 떨어진 곳에: Just before touching down it throws out two small robots, and SLIM comes to rest on its nose, 55 m from its mark.
공처럼 생긴 로봇 소라큐가 그 모습을 찍었습니다. 태양 전지가 서쪽을 봐: The ball-shaped robot SORA-Q took a picture of it. Its solar cells faced west, so it woke up only nine days later.
2024년 2월 22일. 미국 회사의 오디세우스가 달 남극에서 300km: February 22, 2024. Odysseus, built by an American company, comes down toward Malapert A, 300 km from the Moon's south pole.
거리를 재는 레이저가 꺼진 채였습니다. 실험 삼아 실은 NASA 장비를: Its range-finding lasers were switched off. It comes down on a NASA instrument carried only as a test, wired in at the last moment.
옆으로 미끄러지며 닿아 다리 하나가 부러졌고, 몸이 크게 기운 채 멈췄습: It touched down sliding sideways, broke a leg, and came to rest leaning far over. Still, its signal came through.
미국으로서는 아폴로 17호 뒤 51년 만이고, 민간 회사로는 처음 달에: For the United States it was the first landing in 51 years, since Apollo 17, and the first on the Moon by a private company. It worked for six days.
2023년 8월 23일. 인도의 착륙선 비크람이 달 남극 가까이, 남위: August 23, 2023. India's lander Vikram comes down near the Moon's south pole, at 69 degrees south.
내려앉았습니다. 인도는 달에 내린 네 번째 나라가 되었고, 남극 가까이에: It is down. India became the fourth country to land on the Moon, and the first to land near its south pole.
몇 시간 뒤 경사로가 펴지고, 여섯 바퀴 달린 26kg짜리 탐사차 프라그: A few hours later the ramp unfolds, and the six-wheeled rover Pragyan, 26 kg, rolls down.
둘은 달의 낮 하루, 지구 날로 두 주를 일했습니다. 남극 가까운 흙에서: The two worked through one lunar day, two weeks on Earth. In the soil near the south pole they found sulfur.
1959년 9월 14일. 소련의 루나 2호가 달로 떨어집니다. 속도를 줄: September 14, 1959. The Soviet Luna 2 falls toward the Moon. It has no engine to slow it down.
무게 390kg의 쇠공이 초속 3.3km로 다가옵니다. 소총 총알의 세: A metal ball weighing 390 kg comes in at 3.3 km a second, about three times as fast as a rifle bullet.
비의 바다 동쪽에 부딪혔습니다. 사람이 만든 물건이 처음으로 다른 천체에: It hit east of the Sea of Rains. It was the first time a thing made by people reached another world.
속에는 소련 문장을 새긴 오각형 쇳조각을 엮은 공이 있었습니다. 부딪히며: Inside were balls made of five-sided metal pieces stamped with the Soviet emblem, built to scatter on impact.
1969년 11월 19일. 콘래드와 빈이 탄 착륙선 인트레피드가 폭풍의: November 19, 1969. The lander Intrepid, with Conrad and Bean aboard, comes down toward the Ocean of Storms.
Its mark is beside Surveyor 3, a robot lander that came down two and a half years before: a target as small as a pinhole.

1971년 2월 5일. 셰퍼드와 미첼이 탄 착륙선 안타레스가 프라 마우로: February 5, 1971. The lander Antares, with Shepard and Mitchell aboard, comes down toward the Fra Mauro highlands.
높이를 재는 레이더가 잡히지 않았습니다. 차단기를 껐다 켜자 6,700m: The radar that measures height would not lock on. When a breaker was switched off and on, it barely came back at about 6,700 m.
8도쯤 기운 비탈에 섰습니다. 목표에서 30m쯤 떨어진 곳으로, 아폴로: It stood on a slope tilted about 8 degrees. It was about 30 m from the target: the most accurate landing of all the Apollos.
두 사람은 손수레를 끌며 두 번 나가 돌 42.8kg을 모았고, 셰퍼드는: Pulling a handcart, the two went out twice and gathered 42.8 kg of rock, and at the end Shepard hit two golf balls.
1971년 7월 30일. 스콧과 어윈이 탄 착륙선 팰컨이 아펜니노 산맥: July 30, 1971. The lander Falcon, with Scott and Irwin aboard, comes down at the foot of the Apennine Mountains, beside Hadley Rille.
보이지 않던 작은 분화구 가장자리에 닿아, 뒤로 6.9도 왼쪽으로 8.6: It touched the rim of a small crater that could not be seen, and stood tilted 6.9 degrees backward and 8.6 degrees to the left.
이튿날 접어 실어 온 월면차를 펴서 탔습니다. 달에서 사람이 차를 몬 것: The next day they unfolded the Moon car they had brought folded up and rode it. It was the first time anyone drove a car on the Moon.
두 사람은 67시간 가까이 머물며 월면차로 27.9km를 달렸고, 돌 7: The two stayed nearly 67 hours, drove 27.9 km in the Moon car, and came back with 77 kg of rock.
휴스턴, 팰컨은 해들리 평원에 내렸다: Houston, the Falcon is on the Plain at Hadley
1972년 4월 21일. 영과 듀크가 탄 착륙선 오리온이 달의 밝은 고지: April 21, 1972. The lander Orion, with Young and Duke aboard, comes down toward Descartes, in the Moon's bright highlands.
사령선의 엔진에 떨림이 생겨, 달 궤도에서 여섯 시간쯤을 기다린 끝에 허: The command ship's engine had begun to shake, and the landing was allowed only after a wait of about six hours in lunar orbit.
목표에서 북쪽으로 270m, 서쪽으로 60m 떨어진 곳에 섰습니다. 영은: It stood 270 m north and 60 m west of the target. Young jumped up and saluted the flag.
두 사람은 71시간을 머물며 월면차로 26.7km를 달렸고, 돌 95.7: The two stayed 71 hours, drove 26.7 km in the Moon car, and brought back 95.7 kg of rock.
1966년 6월 2일. 사흘 전 지구를 떠난 미국의 서베이어 1호가 폭풍: June 2, 1966. America's Surveyor 1, which left Earth three days ago, comes straight down toward the Ocean of Storms.
높이 75.3km에서 큰 로켓을 켜 초속 2,612m를 110m로 줄이고: At a height of 75.3 km it fires its big rocket, cuts its speed from 2,612 m a second to 110 m, and drops the rocket at about 11 km.
작은 엔진들로 천천히 내려오다 3.4m 위에서 끄고 그대로 떨어져, 초속: It came down slowly on its small engines, shut them off 3.4 m up and simply fell, touching the Moon at about 3 m a second.
미국이 처음 해 본 달 연착륙이 한 번에 됐습니다. 그 뒤 사진 1만 1: America's first try at a soft landing on the Moon worked the first time. Afterwards it sent more than 11,000 photographs to Earth.
1968년 1월 10일. 서베이어의 일곱째이자 마지막 착륙선이 티코 분화: January 10, 1968. The seventh and last Surveyor lander comes down toward the northern rim of Tycho Crater.
아폴로가 내릴 평평한 바다가 아닙니다. 과학자들이 고른, 바위가 널린 남: This is not a flat sea where an Apollo will land. It is the rock-strewn southern highlands, chosen by the scientists.
성분을 재는 장치가 제대로 내려가지 않자, 흙을 파던 삽으로 눌러 땅에: When the device that measures what the soil is made of did not go down properly, the scoop that had been digging soil pressed it down onto the ground.
사진 21,091장을 보냈고, 1월 20일에는 지구에서 쏜 레이저 두 줄: It sent 21,091 photographs, and on January 20 its camera caught two laser beams fired from Earth.
August 18, 1976. The Soviet Luna 24 comes down toward the Sea of Crises. It has come to scoop up the Moon's soil.
2년 전 루나 23호가 내리다 넘어진 곳에서 2.4km쯤 떨어진 자리입니: The spot is about 2.4 km from where Luna 23 fell over while landing two years before. The drill bores about 2 m down.
이튿날, 내린 지 23시간 만에 흙 170g을 담은 캡슐을 실은 로켓이: The next day, 23 hours after landing, a rocket carrying a capsule with 170 g of soil lifts off from the top of the lander.
8월 22일 캡슐이 시베리아에 내렸습니다. 그 뒤 2013년까지 37년: On August 22 the capsule came down in Siberia. For 37 years after that, until 2013, nothing landed on the Moon.
1973년 1월 15일. 소련의 루나 21호가 맑음의 바다 가장자리, 르: January 15, 1973. The Soviet Luna 21 comes down toward Le Monnier Crater, at the edge of the Sea of Serenity.
한 시간 사십 분 뒤 경사로가 펴지고, 바퀴 여덟 달린 840kg의 루노: An hour and forty minutes later the ramps unfold, and the eight-wheeled Lunokhod 2, 840 kg, rolls down.
둘레를 먼저 찍고, 30m쯤 가서는 돌아서서 저를 태워 온 착륙선을 찍었: It first photographed its surroundings, and after going about 30 m it turned round and photographed the lander that had carried it.
넉 달 동안 39km를 달리며 텔레비전 사진 8만여 장과 파노라마 86장: In four months it drove 39 km and sent more than 80,000 television pictures and 86 panoramas to Earth.
2013년 12월 14일. 중국의 창어 3호가 비의 바다 북쪽으로 내려옵: December 14, 2013. China's Chang'e 3 comes down north of the Sea of Rains. It is the first Moon landing in 37 years.
높이 100m쯤에서 멈춰 떠서 돌과 구덩이가 없는 자리를 스스로 고르고,: It hovers at a height of about 100 m, picks for itself a spot free of rocks and pits, and shuts off its engine 4 m up.
일곱 시간 반쯤 뒤, 여섯 바퀴 달린 140kg의 탐사차 위투가 경사로를: About seven and a half hours later the six-wheeled rover Yutu, 140 kg, rides the ramp down onto the Moon.
중국은 달에 내려앉은 세 번째 나라가 됐습니다. 위투는 114.8m를 가: China became the third country to land on the Moon. Yutu went 114.8 m and stopped, and still sent signals after that.
토끼가 달에 왔어요~: A bunny has come to the Moon~
2019년 1월 3일. 중국의 창어 4호가 지구에서 보이지 않는 달 뒷면: January 3, 2019. China's Chang'e 4 comes down toward Von Kármán Crater, on the far side of the Moon that cannot be seen from Earth.
지구의 전파가 닿지 않는 곳입니다. 지난해 5월 달 너머 6만 5천km에: Earth's radio waves do not reach this place. Queqiao, placed 65,000 km beyond the Moon in May of the year before, passes the words along.
내려앉았습니다. 달의 뒷면에 내린 첫 탐사선입니다. 열두 시간쯤 뒤 위투: It is down. It is the first probe to land on the far side of the Moon. About twelve hours later Yutu 2 comes down the ramp.
위투 2호는 무게 140kg에 바퀴가 여섯입니다. 달 뒷면의 흙에 처음으: Yutu 2 weighs 140 kg and has six wheels. It made the first wheel tracks in the soil of the Moon's far side.
2020년 12월 1일. 중국의 창어 5호가 폭풍의 대양 북쪽, 륌케르산: December 1, 2020. China's Chang'e 5 comes down near Mons Rümker, north of the Ocean of Storms.
드릴로 땅속 1m쯤을 뚫고 로봇 팔로 겉흙을 떠 담습니다. 무게 12g의: It drills about 1 m into the ground and scoops up surface soil with its robot arm. It also unfurled a Chinese flag weighing 12 g.
이틀 뒤인 12월 3일, 흙 1,731g을 실은 상승선이 착륙선을 발사대: Two days later, on December 3, the ascent stage carrying 1,731 g of soil lifts off, using the lander as its launch pad.
달 궤도에서 궤도선과 만나 흙을 옮겨 실었고, 캡슐은 중국 시각 12월: In lunar orbit it met the orbiter and passed the soil across, and the capsule came down in Inner Mongolia before dawn on December 17, China time.
흙 한 봉지 포장이요~: One bag of soil to go!
2024년 6월 2일. 중국의 창어 6호가 달 뒷면 남극-에이트켄 분지: June 2, 2024. China's Chang'e 6 comes down toward the Apollo basin, inside the South Pole-Aitken basin on the Moon's far side.
뒷면이라 지구와 바로 말할 수 없습니다. 중계 위성 췌차오 2호를 거쳐,: On the far side it cannot talk with Earth directly. Linked through the relay satellite Queqiao 2, it picks its own spot and lands.
드릴과 로봇 팔로 흙을 담고, 현무암을 녹여 뽑은 실로 짠 국기를 펼친: It gathers soil with its drill and robot arm, unfurls a flag woven from thread drawn out of melted basalt, and on June 4 the ascent stage lifts off.
6월 25일 내몽골에 내린 캡슐에는 흙 1,935.3g이 들어 있었습니다: The capsule that came down in Inner Mongolia on June 25 held 1,935.3 g of soil. It is the first soil from the Moon's far side.
조심히 가. 흙 쏟지 말고: Safe trip. Don't spill the soil
2025년 3월 2일. 미국 파이어플라이의 블루 고스트가 위난의 바다,: March 2, 2025. Blue Ghost, built by Firefly of the United States, comes down beside Mons Latreille in the Sea of Crises.
1월 15일에 지구를 떠났습니다. 내려오는 끝에 바위를 피해 두 번, 스: It left Earth on January 15. At the end of its descent it shifts its spot twice, by itself, to avoid rocks.
키 2m의 몸이 목표 100m 안에 똑바로 섰습니다. 민간 착륙선이 넘어: Its 2 m tall body stood upright within 100 m of the target. It is the first private lander to land without falling over.
NASA의 장비 열 가지를 싣고 가 3월 16일 태양이 질 때까지 일했고: It carried ten NASA instruments and worked until the Sun set on March 16, sending more than 110 GB of data.
1971년 12월 2일. 소련의 마스 3호 착륙선이 모선에서 떨어져 나온: December 2, 1971. The Soviet Mars 3 lander enters the air of Mars 4 hours 35 minutes after separating from its mother ship.
초속 5.7km로 들어와 공기로 속도를 줄이고, 낙하산을 편 뒤 땅 가까: It comes in at 5.7 km a second, slows down against the air, opens a parachute, and fires braking rockets close to the ground.
13시 52분, 358kg의 둥근 캡슐이 땅에 닿았습니다. 꽃잎 넷을 펴: At 13:52 the round 358 kg capsule touched the ground. It opens four petals to stand, and 90 seconds later begins to send a signal.
신호는 20초쯤 만에 끊겼습니다. 그래도 화성에 부서지지 않고 내린 첫: The signal stopped after about 20 seconds. Even so, it is the first probe to land on Mars without breaking.
1976년 9월 3일. 바이킹 2호 착륙선이 궤도선에서 떨어져 나와 유토: September 3, 1976. The Viking 2 lander separates from its orbiter and comes down toward Utopia Planitia.
높이 6km에서 지름 16m의 낙하산을 펴고, 그것을 버린 뒤 엔진 셋으: At a height of 6 km it opens a parachute 16 m across, drops it, and slows to 2.4 m a second with three engines.
다리 하나가 돌 위에 얹혀 8.2도 기운 채 섰습니다. 분화구 미에서 서: It stood tilted 8.2 degrees, with one leg resting on a rock. The spot is about 200 km west of the crater Mie.
1호보다 훨씬 북쪽인 북위 48도의 땅입니다. 이곳에서 1980년 4월: This is land at 48 degrees north, much farther north than Viking 1. It worked here until April 11, 1980.
어이쿠, 돌을 밟았네: Oops, I stepped on a rock
2003년 12월 25일. 엿새 전 마스 익스프레스에서 떨어져 나온 비글: December 25, 2003. Beagle 2, which separated from Mars Express six days ago, comes down toward Isidis Planitia.
시속 2만km쯤으로 대기에 들어와 낙하산을 펴고, 높이 200m쯤에서 공: It enters the air at about 20,000 km an hour, opens a parachute, and inflates its air bags at a height of about 200 m.
33.2kg의 착륙선은 땅에 닿았지만 신호를 보내지 않았습니다. 지구에서: The 33.2 kg lander reached the ground but sent no signal. On Earth it was thought to have been wrecked.
2015년 1월에 사진으로 찾았습니다. 겨눈 곳에서 5km쯤 떨어진 데에: It was found in photographs in January 2015. It lay about 5 km from where it was aimed, with its solar panels not fully opened.
메리 크리스마스... 들리니?: Merry Christmas... can you hear me?
2004년 1월 4일. 스피릿이 낙하산에 매달려 구세프 분화구로 내려옵니: January 4, 2004. Spirit comes down toward Gusev Crater, hanging under a parachute. Four air bags wrap its body.
로켓이 땅 위 10→15m에서 떨어지는 속도를 0으로 만들고, 공기 주머: Rockets bring its falling speed to 0 at 10→15 m above the ground, and drop it, air bags and all, to the ground.
스물여덟 번을 튀었습니다. 작은 분화구에 한 번 빠졌다 나오기도 하며 굴: It bounced twenty-eight times. It rolled on, once falling into a small crater and coming out again, and stopped.
꽃잎을 열고 선 곳은 컬럼비아 기념 기지라 부릅니다. 그 안에 185kg: The place where it opened its petals and stood is called the Columbia Memorial Station. Inside rode a rover of 185 kg.
2004년 1월 25일. 스피릿의 쌍둥이 오퍼튜니티가 낙하산에 매달려 메: January 25, 2004. Opportunity, Spirit's twin, comes down toward Meridiani Planum, hanging under a parachute.
낙하산과 로켓으로 속도를 줄인 뒤, 공기 주머니에 싸인 채 떨어져 스물여: After slowing with its parachute and rockets it fell wrapped in air bags, and bounced and rolled twenty-six times.
멈춘 곳은 지름 22m의 작은 분화구 안이었습니다. 겨눈 것이 아니라 우: It stopped inside a small crater 22 m across. It was not aimed but chance, so it was called "a hole in one".
스피릿이 내린 지 3주 만입니다. 쌍둥이 탐사차 둘이 화성의 서로 반대편: It is 3 weeks since Spirit landed. The two twin rovers stood on opposite sides of Mars.
2021년 5월 15일. 석 달 동안 화성을 돌던 톈원 1호에서 착륙선이: May 15, 2021. A lander separates from Tianwen-1, which has circled Mars for three months, and comes down toward Utopia Planitia.
대기에 들어서 땅에 닿기까지 9분쯤. 덮개와 낙하산, 역추진 엔진을 차례: From entering the air to touching the ground takes about 9 minutes. It slowed down using a shield, a parachute and a braking engine in turn.
베이징 시각 오전 7시 18분에 닿았습니다. 240kg의 탐사차 주룽은: It touched down at 7:18 a.m. Beijing time. The 240 kg rover Zhurong was still riding on top of the lander.
Seven days later, on May 22, Zhurong rode the ramp down onto the ground of Mars. It is China's first landing on Mars.
2021년 2월 18일. 1,025kg의 퍼서비어런스가 지름 21.5m의: February 18, 2021. Perseverance, 1,025 kg, opens a parachute 21.5 m across and comes down toward Jezero Crater.
내려오며 찍은 땅을 지도와 맞대어 보고, 바위와 비탈을 피해 내릴 자리를: It matched the ground it photographed on the way down against a map, and picked its own landing spot, avoiding rocks and slopes.
로켓을 뿜는 하강단이 줄로 차를 매달아 내립니다. 시속 2.7km로 바퀴: A descent stage on rockets lowers the rover on cables. When the wheels touch at 2.7 km an hour it cuts the cables and flies away.
내리는 모습은 제 카메라에 영상으로 담겼습니다. 낙하산 무늬에는 '대담하: Its landing was caught on video by its own cameras. Hidden in the pattern of the parachute was a coded message: "Dare mighty things".
2008년 5월 25일. 피닉스가 시속 2만 1천km 가까운 속도로 대기: May 25, 2008. Phoenix enters the air at nearly 21,000 km an hour and comes down toward a plain at 68 degrees north.
낙하산은 예정보다 7초쯤 늦게 펴졌습니다. 그것을 버린 뒤 추진기 열두: The parachute opened about 7 seconds later than planned. After dropping it, Phoenix comes down firing twelve thrusters.
시속 8km쯤으로 세 다리가 닿았습니다. 기울기는 0.3도. 거의 반듯하: Its three legs touched at about 8 km an hour. The tilt was 0.3 degrees. It stood almost perfectly level.
공기 주머니 없이 엔진으로 화성에 내린 것은 1976년 바이킹 2호 뒤로: It is the first landing on Mars by engines, without air bags, in the 32 years since Viking 2 in 1976.

2018년 11월 26일. 인사이트가 시속 19,800km로 화성 대기에: November 26, 2018. InSight enters the air of Mars at 19,800 km an hour and comes down toward Elysium Planitia.
높이 11km쯤에서 낙하산을 펴고, 그것을 버린 뒤 역추진 엔진 열두 개: At a height of about 11 km it opens a parachute, drops it, and fires twelve braking engines. It all took about 7 minutes.
함께 날아온 작은 위성 둘이 신호를 중계해, 내린 소식과 첫 사진이 곧바: Two small satellites that flew along with it relayed the signal, so news of the landing and the first photograph reached Earth at once.
첫 사진에는 렌즈 덮개에 붙은 먼지가 점점이 찍혔습니다. 358kg의 착: The first photograph was speckled with dust stuck on the lens cover. The 358 kg lander opened two solar panels 2.15 m across.

추류모프-게라시멘코 혜성은 곁에 가기만 해도 필레가 내리던 날을 볼 수: Beside comet 67P you can now watch Philae's landing without setting down on it.
소행성이나 탐사선이 떨어지는 장면에서, 말하는 것이 화면에 보일 때 말풍: In scenes where an asteroid or a probe falls, its bubble now shows while it is in view.
지도에서 고르기 화면이 남색과 금빛으로 바뀌었습니다. 둘레에 별이 반짝이: The map sheet is night blue and gold now: stars twinkle round it and a comet goes by.
