14 January 2008. MESSENGER skims 200 km above Mercury. No spacecraft has come here for 33 years.
1974년 매리너 10호는 이 분지를 절반만 보았습니다. 나머지 절반은: In 1974 Mariner 10 saw only half of this basin. The other half lay in the night.
찰칵. 멀어지며 돌아본 사진에 분지가 통째로 들어왔습니다. 지름은 알던: Click. Looking back as it left, it caught the whole basin. It was 1,550 km across, larger than thought.
한가운데에는 골짜기 수백 줄이 바큇살처럼 뻗어 있었습니다. 연구자들은 거: At its centre hundreds of troughs ran out like the spokes of a wheel. The team nicknamed it the Spider.
매리너 선배, 나머지 반쪽은 제가 찍을게요: Mariner, I’ll take the other half from here
북극의 그늘에서 얼음을 찾다: Finding ice in the shadows of the north pole
2012년 11월 29일. 메신저 팀이 발표합니다. 수성 북극의 그늘진: 29 November 2012. The MESSENGER team announces it: there is water ice in the shadowed craters of Mercury’s north pole.
1991년 지구의 레이더에 북극이 밝게 비친 뒤로 스무 해 넘게 풀지 못: Since radar from Earth found the pole bright in 1991, the question had stood for more than twenty years.
메신저는 수성을 돌며 북극에서 나오는 중성자를 셌습니다. 수소가 많은 곳: Circling Mercury, MESSENGER counted the neutrons coming from the pole. Where hydrogen was plentiful, there was water.
얼음은 1,000억 톤에서 1조 톤쯤입니다. 지구의 얼음에 대면 몇만 분: The ice comes to some 100 billion to 1 trillion tons. That is tens of thousands of times less than Earth’s ice, but astonishing right beside the Sun.
수성에 얼음이라니, 믿어져?: Ice on Mercury. Can you believe it?
수성의 절벽을 처음 찍다: The first picture of a cliff on Mercury
29 March 1974. Mariner 10 passes 703 km above Mercury. It is the first spacecraft to go there.
금성의 중력으로 방향을 꺾어 온 길입니다. 다른 행성의 힘을 빌려 간 것: It came by bending its path with the gravity of Venus. That, too, was a first: borrowing another planet’s pull.
찰칵. 사진 속 땅에 길이 650km의 턱이 분화구들을 가로질러 뻗어 있: Click. Across the ground in the picture ran a step 650 km long, cutting through the craters.
매리너 10호는 수성을 세 번 지나며 겉의 45%를 찍었습니다. 나머지는: In three passes Mariner 10 photographed 45% of the surface. The rest waited for MESSENGER.
행성이 쪼그라든 자국이래: The mark of a planet that shrank
1974년 3월 29일. 수성을 처음 지나는 매리너 10호가 사진을 잇달: 29 March 1974. On its first pass of Mercury, Mariner 10 sends picture after picture back to Earth.
그 가운데 언덕과 골짜기가 뒤죽박죽인 땅이 있었습니다. 분화구의 둘레마저: Among them was a ground of hills and valleys all jumbled together. Even the rims of the craters had crumbled.
연구자들은 달리 부를 말이 없어 기묘한 지형이라고 적었습니다. 넓이는 5: With no better word for it, the team wrote down “weird terrain”. It covers more than 500,000 square kilometres.
지도에서 정반대편을 찾아보니 커다란 칼로리스 분지가 있었습니다. 둘은 한: Looking for the exact opposite point on the map, they found the great Caloris basin. The two were the front and the back of one impact.
반대편까지 흔들렸구나: It shook all the way round here
지름 1,550km의 큰 충돌 자국입니다. 1974년 매리너 10호가 절: A great impact scar 1,550 km across. Mariner 10 photographed half of it in 1974, MESSENGER all of it in 2008.
북극의 얼음 분화구: Prokofiev, an ice crater at the north pole
태양에 가장 가까운 행성의 북극 분화구입니다. 햇빛이 들지 않는 바닥에: A crater at the north pole of the planet nearest the Sun. On its floor, where sunlight never comes, there is water ice.
길이 650km, 높이 2km의 절벽입니다. 수성이 식으며 쪼그라들 때: A cliff 650 km long and 2 km high. It rose when Mercury cooled and shrank and the ground was pushed up.
칼로리스 분지의 정반대편입니다. 언덕과 골짜기가 뒤죽박죽이라 매리너 10: The exact opposite side from the Caloris basin. Its hills and valleys are so jumbled that the Mariner 10 team called it the weird terrain.
칼로리스 분지는 지름 1,550km로, 수성 지름의 3분의 1에 가깝습니: The Caloris basin is 1,550 km across, close to a third of Mercury’s diameter. It was made 3.8 to 3.9 billion years ago, when a body more than 100 km wide struck. Round its edge stands a ring of mountains up to 2 km high. When Mariner 10 passed in 1974 the basin lay on the line between day and night and only half was photographed; in January 2008 MESSENGER took the first picture of all of it. The name is Latin for heat. At every second closest approach of Mercury to the Sun, the Sun stands right above it.
The Caloris basin photographed by MESSENGER in exaggerated colour. The yellowish part is the floor of the basin.
Prokofiev is a crater 112 km across near Mercury’s north pole. Mercury’s axis is hardly tilted at all, so sunlight never reaches the floors of the craters at its poles. The ground by day heats to 430 degrees, but this shade stays below minus 170. In 1991 radar sent from Earth found the craters of the north pole unusually bright, and in 2012 MESSENGER confirmed that it was water ice. The ice is thought to have been brought by comets or asteroids.
메신저가 잰 수성 북극의 온도. 붉을수록 뜨겁고, 보랏빛 분화구 바닥이: The temperature of Mercury’s north pole as MESSENGER measured it. The redder, the hotter; the purple crater floors are the coldest.
디스커버리 절벽은 길이 650km, 높이 2km로 수성에서 손꼽히게 큰: Discovery Rupes is 650 km long and 2 km high, one of the greatest cliffs on Mercury. As its inside cooled, Mercury’s radius shrank by as much as 7 km. The ground of its surface then had too much room, one side was pushed up over the other, and that step became the cliff. The cliff cuts across old craters. It was found in the pictures of Mariner 10 in 1974. It is named after the ship Discovery, which sailed on the last voyage of James Cook.
Discovery Rupes photographed by MESSENGER. The step runs right across a crater.
칼로리스 분지의 정반대편에는 언덕과 골짜기가 뒤죽박죽 섞인 땅이 있습니다: On the exact opposite side from the Caloris basin lies a ground of hills and valleys all jumbled together. It covers more than 500,000 square kilometres, and its hills are 5 to 10 km wide and up to 1.8 km high. The researchers who saw it in the pictures of Mariner 10 in 1974 called it the weird terrain. It is thought that the seismic waves of the impact that made Caloris went round the planet, met on the far side and shook the ground apart. Another account is that the rock thrown out by the impact came down together here.
The weird terrain photographed by Mariner 10. Hills and valleys are mixed together.
분지 한가운데에는 판테온 포사라는 골짜기 수백 줄이 바큇살처럼 뻗어 있습: At the centre of the basin hundreds of troughs called Pantheon Fossae run out like the spokes of a wheel. The researchers who first saw them called them the Spider. Near their middle is a crater 40 km across. Why the troughs took this shape is not yet known.
달의 극지에도 같은 까닭으로 얼음이 있습니다. 수성의 얼음은 군데군데 검: There is ice at the poles of the Moon for the same reason. Mercury’s ice is covered here and there by a dark material, thought to be organic matter rich in carbon. The name Prokofiev comes from a Russian composer. It was settled that the craters of Mercury are named after artists.
수성의 절벽들에는 탐험에 쓰인 배의 이름을 붙입니다. 이런 절벽과 주름은: The cliffs of Mercury are named after ships of exploration. There are thousands of such cliffs and ridges all over the planet. MESSENGER also found small cliffs less than 50 million years old. That means Mercury is still shrinking, little by little.
달에서도 큰 분지의 정반대편에 비슷하게 주름진 땅이 보입니다. 수성은 쇠: On the Moon, too, a similarly wrinkled ground is seen on the opposite side from a great basin. Mercury’s iron core fills more than eight tenths of its radius, which is thought to have helped the seismic waves to meet. On the official maps it is written as hilly and lineated terrain.

유럽과 일본이 함께 보낸 수성 탐사선입니다. 2018년에 떠나 수성을 여: A Mercury probe sent by Europe and Japan together. It left in 2018, has passed Mercury six times, and in November 2026 becomes the second craft to circle it.
2018년 10월 20일 베피콜롬보가 떠났습니다. 유럽의 궤도선과 일본의: On 20 October 2018 BepiColombo left. Europe’s orbiter and Japan’s orbiter Mio travel bound together as one.
수성은 태양의 중력 깊숙이 있어 가서 멈추기가 어렵습니다. 지구 한 번,: Mercury lies deep in the Sun’s gravity, so it is hard to get there and stop. It sheds speed by passing Earth once, Venus twice and Mercury six times.
2021년 10월 1일, 수성 위 199km를 처음 지나갑니다. 몸에 달: On 1 October 2021 it passes 199 km above Mercury for the first time. Small cameras on its body photographed the cratered ground.
2024년 엔진의 힘이 달려 길을 바꿨습니다. 도착은 2025년 12월에: In 2024 its engines ran short of power and the route was changed. The arrival slipped eleven months, from December 2025 to November 2026.
수성에 닿으면 둘은 갈라져 따로 돕니다. 이름은 수성을 여러 번 스치는: At Mercury the two part and circle it separately. The name comes from the Italian scientist who found the path that passes Mercury again and again.
밝은 구덩이의 정체를 알아내다: Learning what the bright patches are
2011년 3월 18일. 메신저가 6년 반을 날아 수성 둘레를 도는 첫: 18 March 2011. After six and a half years of flight MESSENGER becomes the first craft to circle Mercury.
스쳐 지날 때보다 훨씬 가까이, 날마다 찍을 수 있게 됐습니다. 분화구: Now it can photograph every day, from far closer than on a pass. It begins with the bright patches on crater floors.
찰칵. 얼룩은 테두리 없이 얕게 꺼진 구덩이들의 무리였습니다. 다른 곳에: Click. The patches were clusters of shallow pits with no rims. Nothing like them had been seen anywhere else.
연구자들은 움푹 팬 곳이라는 뜻으로 할로라고 불렀습니다. 지금도 새로 생: The researchers called them hollows. New ones may still be forming today.
햇볕에 땅이 날아가 버렸대: They say the sunlight carried the ground away
지구의 레이더가 먼저 찾다: Radar from Earth finds it first
1991년. 미국 골드스톤의 큰 안테나가 수성으로 전파를 쏘고, 되돌아오: 1991. The great antenna at Goldstone in the United States sends radio waves to Mercury and catches the echo that comes back.
탐사선이 찍지 못한 쪽의 땅에서 유난히 밝은 점들이 잡혔습니다. 그 가운: On the side no spacecraft had photographed, unusually bright spots showed up. One of them is this crater.
The That Day scene at Hokusai crater is shorter (22 s → 14 s).
사진보다 전파에 먼저 찍혔어: Radio caught me before any camera did
수성 표면 10,000km 안에서 수성이 화면 높이의 60% 이상을 채우: From within 10,000 km of Mercury’s surface, with Mercury filling 60% or more of the height of the view (Mariner 10, 1974)
이름을 준 과학자는 어느 나라 사람인가?: What country was the scientist it is named after from?
베피콜롬보는 유럽우주국과 일본이 함께 만든 수성 탐사선입니다. 2018년: BepiColombo is a Mercury probe built by the European Space Agency and Japan together. It left on an Ariane 5 rocket on 20 October 2018. Europe’s orbiter and Japan’s orbiter Mio travel bound together as one. It shed speed by passing Earth once, Venus twice and Mercury six times, and is due to enter orbit round Mercury on 21 November 2026.
수성에 닿으면 둘은 갈라집니다. 유럽의 궤도선은 수성 480km에서 1,: At Mercury the two part. Europe’s orbiter will circle 480 to 1,500 km above Mercury and study its ground and its inside, while Mio measures the magnetic field from a long orbit that swings out to 11,640 km. On the way it used ion engines. The name comes from the nickname of Giuseppe Colombo, the scientist from Italy who found the path that passes Mercury again and again and so helped Mariner 10.
테두리 없이 얕게 꺼진 밝은 구덩이들입니다. 땅속의 물질이 햇볕에 기체가: Bright, shallow pits with no rims. They are thought to be where something in the ground turned to gas in the sunlight and escaped.
밝은 빛줄기가 수천 km를 뻗는 젊은 분화구입니다. 1991년 지구에서: A young crater whose bright rays run for thousands of kilometres. Radar sent from Earth caught it first, in 1991.
할로는 수성에서만 볼 수 있는 지형입니다. 테두리 없이 바닥이 평평하게: Hollows are a landform seen only on Mercury. They are clusters of pits with flat floors and no rims, bright all round. They are tens of metres to a few kilometres wide. MESSENGER found them after it began to circle Mercury in 2011. It is thought that volatile material in the ground turned to gas in the hot sunlight and escaped, and the ground sank where it had been. They are among the youngest landforms on Mercury, and here in the Raditladi basin they gather on the inner ring of peaks.
메신저가 색을 강조해 찍은 라디틀라디 분지의 할로. 푸르스름하게 밝은 곳: The hollows of the Raditladi basin photographed by MESSENGER in strengthened colour. The bright bluish parts are where the ground has sunk.
호쿠사이는 지름 100km쯤의 분화구입니다. 여기서 튀어 나간 돌가루가: Hokusai is a crater about 100 km across. The powdered rock thrown out of it became bright rays that run for thousands of kilometres and cover much of the northern half of Mercury. Rays darken as the ages pass, so being this bright means the crater is young. Radar sent from Earth caught it first, in 1991, as an unusually bright spot, and it was then simply called B. A spacecraft photographed it only later. It is named after the Japanese painter Katsushika Hokusai.
메신저가 찍은 호쿠사이의 빛줄기. 밝은 줄들이 수성의 북반구를 가로지릅니: The rays of Hokusai photographed by MESSENGER. The bright streaks cross the northern half of Mercury.
라디틀라디 분지는 지름 258km이고 생긴 지 10억 년이 안 된 것으로: The Raditladi basin is 258 km across and thought to be less than a billion years old. MESSENGER found it on its first pass of Mercury in January 2008. Its name comes from a playwright and poet of Botswana. In 1974 Mariner 10 saw that the floors of some craters were unusually bright, but its pictures were too blurred to tell what they were.
레이더에 밝게 비친 까닭은 갓 튀어나온 돌밭이 거칠어 전파를 잘 되쏘기: It shone bright on radar because freshly thrown rubble is rough and sends radio waves back well. In the 2000s the Arecibo radio telescope looked again and learned that it was a crater with a train of rays. Hokusai is the painter famous for his picture of a great wave. The name was suggested by an astronomer who had studied this place by radar.
할로는 무엇이 달아나고 남은 자리로 보나?: Hollows are thought to be where what escaped?
빛줄기가 밝다는 것은 무슨 뜻인가?: What does it mean that the rays are bright?
수성의 태양이 뜨기 전 지평선에 솟는 코로나와, 멀리서 두 점으로 보이는: Tells of the corona over Mercury's horizon before sunrise, and of Earth and the Moon seen as two points from afar.
The light rose before the Sun.
Those two dots are Earth and the Moon.
태양은 아직 땅 밑인데 지평선 위로 흰 빛이 솟아 있습니다. 태양의 코로:
The Sun is still down, yet white light stands over the horizon: its corona.
Mercury has no air: the corona rises first.
저 푸른 점이 지구이고, 곁에 붙은 작은 점이 달입니다.\n2010년 탐:
The blue point is Earth; the small one beside it is the Moon.
In 2010 MESSENGER photographed the pair from 183 million km away.
수성에 비발디 분화구가 생겼습니다. 태양이 떴다가 지고 다시 뜨는 아침을: Vivaldi crater is new on Mercury: watch a morning when the Sun rises, sets and rises again. The notebook has 200 slots.
태양이 두 번 뜨는 아침 장면을 새 그림으로 바꿨습니다. 코로나와 홍염이: The morning the Sun rises twice is redrawn: a Sun with its corona and prominences rises over Mercury's mountains.
태양이 두 번 뜨는 아침: The morning the Sun rises twice
수성의 아침. 분화구 테두리 너머로 태양이 떠오릅니다. 지구에서 보는 태: Morning on Mercury. The Sun comes up over the crater's rim, about three times as wide as it looks from Earth.
But the Sun stops. Then it goes back down the way it came, and sets.
조금 뒤 태양은 같은 자리에서 다시 떠오릅니다. 이번에는 멈추지 않고 제: A little later it rises again at the same spot. This time it does not stop, and goes on its way.
수성이 태양에 가장 가까울 때는 공전이 자전을 앞질러 태양이 뒷걸음칩니다: When Mercury is nearest the Sun, its orbit outruns its spin and the Sun walks backward. Once in 176 Earth days.
태양이 졌다가 또 떴어: The Sun set, and rose again
테두리가 두 겹인 지름 213km의 분화구입니다. 이 경도에는 태양이 떴: A crater 213 km across with two rims. At this longitude there is a morning when the Sun rises, sets again and rises once more.
비발디는 지름 213km의 분화구입니다. 바깥 테두리 안에 지름이 절반쯤: Vivaldi is a crater 213 km across. Inside its outer rim stands a second ring of mountains about half as wide, so it looks like a target. It lies at 86 degrees west, near the longitude where morning comes when Mercury is nearest the Sun. Then, seen from here, the Sun starts to rise, stops, sets again and rises once more. From Mercury the Sun looks about three times as wide as from Earth. It is named after Vivaldi, the Italian composer of The Four Seasons.
메신저가 찍은 비발디 분화구. 가운데 둥근 산의 고리가 안쪽 테두리입니다: Vivaldi crater, photographed by MESSENGER. The round ring of mountains in the middle is the inner rim.
수성은 태양을 두 바퀴 도는 동안 꼭 세 번 자전합니다. 1965년 아레: Mercury turns exactly three times while it goes twice round the Sun. That came out in 1965, when the Arecibo radar found that its turn takes 59 days. So Mercury's day, from one sunrise to the next, is 176 Earth days long. For about eight days nearest the Sun its orbit is faster than its spin, and the Sun walks backward in the sky. Only near longitudes 90 and 270, where the Sun is on the horizon just then, does it rise twice or set twice.
태양이 떠오르다 도로 지는 것은 수성이 어디에 있을 때인가?: Where is Mercury when the Sun starts to rise and sets again?
태양에 가장 가까워질 때: when Mercury is nearest the Sun
태양에서 가장 멀어질 때: when Mercury is farthest from the Sun
일본의 금성 탐사선입니다. 2010년 궤도에 드는 데 실패하고 태양을 다: Japan's Venus probe. It failed to enter orbit in 2010, went round the Sun for five years, made it in 2015 on its small thrusters, and watched Venus's clouds until 2024.
다섯 해 만의 두 번째 시도: A second try, five years on
2010년 5월 21일 아카쓰키가 다네가시마에서 떠났습니다. 이름은 새벽: On 21 May 2010 Akatsuki left Tanegashima. Its name means "Dawn".
On 7 December that year it fired its engine beside Venus, but the engine cut out after two and a half minutes. The probe flew past Venus and began to circle the Sun.
주 엔진은 깨져 못 쓰게 되었습니다. 다섯 해 동안 태양을 돌며 금성을: The main engine was broken for good. For five years it went round the Sun, waiting to meet Venus again.
2015년 12월 7일, 자세를 잡는 작은 엔진 넷을 20분 동안 켰습니: On 7 December 2015 it fired four small thrusters, the ones that keep it steady, for 20 minutes. This time it went into orbit round Venus.
곧 구름 꼭대기에서 길이 1만 km의 활 모양 무늬를 찍었습니다. 아래의: Soon it photographed a bow-shaped mark 10,000 km long on the cloud tops: a wave made where the high ground below pushes the air up.
이름 아카쓰키는 무슨 뜻인가?: What does the name Akatsuki mean?
Akatsuki is Japan's Venus probe. Its name means "Dawn". It left Tanegashima on an H-IIA rocket on 21 May 2010. On 7 December that year it fired its engine to enter orbit round Venus, but the engine cut out after two and a half minutes and it flew past. After five years round the Sun it tried again on 7 December 2015, with four small thrusters meant for keeping it steady, and went into orbit. It was the first Japanese probe to orbit another planet.
카메라 다섯 대로 적외선과 자외선에서 구름을 찍었습니다. 금성은 243일: With five cameras it photographed the clouds in infrared and ultraviolet light. Venus turns once in 243 days, yet its clouds go round in four. Akatsuki studied how that fast wind is kept up, and found a bow-shaped mark 10,000 km long on the cloud tops. Contact was lost in April 2024 and the mission ended in September 2025. It is still going round Venus.
금성 하늘에 뜬 풍선: A balloon in the sky of Venus
1985년 6월 11일. 핼리 혜성으로 가던 소련의 베가 1호가 금성에: 11 June 1985. On its way to Halley's Comet, the Soviet probe Vega 1 drops a capsule at Venus.
캡슐이 구름 속에서 둘로 갈라집니다. 착륙선은 땅으로 내려가고, 풍선은: Inside the clouds the capsule parts in two. The lander goes on down to the ground, and the balloon fills at a height of 54 km.
지름 3.5m의 풍선이 13m 줄 끝에 측정 장치를 매달고, 시속 240: The balloon, 3.5 m across, hangs its instruments at the end of a 13 m line and rides a wind of 240 km/h.
그 높이는 기압이 지구의 절반, 온도가 30도쯤입니다. 금성에서 지구와: At that height the pressure is half of Earth's and it is about 30 degrees: the most Earth-like place on Venus.
46시간 동안 11,000km 넘게 떠다녔습니다. 지구 밖 하늘에 뜬 첫: It drifted for 46 hours, over 11,000 km: the first balloon in a sky beyond Earth.
1975년 10월 22일. 소련의 베네라 9호가 금성의 구름을 뚫고 내려: 22 October 1975. The Soviet probe Venera 9 comes down through the clouds of Venus. The craft that carried it stays above and goes into orbit.
낙하산은 높이 50km에서 버립니다. 그 아래로는 몸에 두른 둥근 판으로: It lets its parachute go at 50 km. Below that, the round plate about its body is enough to brake it in the thick air.
초속 7m로 돌이 널린 비탈에 내렸습니다. 485도, 지구의 90배 기압: It came down at 7 m a second on a slope strewn with stones. 485 degrees, and 90 times Earth's pressure.
카메라 덮개 둘 가운데 하나만 떨어졌습니다. 남은 한쪽으로 찍은 흑백 사: Only one of the two camera covers came off. The black-and-white picture taken through the other side is the first photograph from the ground of another planet.
1985년 6월 11일 소련의 베가 1호가 이곳 하늘에 풍선을 띄웠습니다: On 11 June 1985 the Soviet probe Vega 1 let a balloon go in the sky here. It drifted inside the clouds, 54 km up, for nearly two days.
1975년 10월 22일 금성에 내려 53분 동안 신호를 보냈습니다. 다: It landed on Venus on 22 October 1975 and sent signals for 53 minutes, with the first photograph taken on the ground of another planet.
Vega 1 and Vega 2 were twin probes the Soviet Union sent in December 1984. On their way to Halley's Comet they passed Venus and each dropped a capsule, out of which came a lander and a balloon. Helium filled the balloon, 3.5 m across, and its instruments hung at the end of a 13 m line. Inside the clouds 54 km up it rode a wind of 240 km/h for 46 hours, over 11,000 km. It was the first balloon in a sky beyond Earth.
그림으로 그린 금성 구름 속의 베가 풍선. 긴 줄 끝에 측정 장치가 매달: A drawing of a Vega balloon in the clouds of Venus, its instruments at the end of a long line. It is not a photograph.
소련의 베네라 9호는 1975년 10월 22일 금성에 내렸습니다. 땅은: The Soviet probe Venera 9 landed on Venus on 22 October 1975. The ground was at 485 degrees, under 90 times Earth's pressure. The lander sent signals for 53 minutes, and in that time took and sent a black-and-white photograph: the first taken on the ground of another planet. It shows a slope strewn with flat, sharp-edged stones. The craft that carried the lander stayed in orbit, the first probe to go round Venus.
베네라 9호가 찍은 금성의 땅. 아래쪽에 착륙선의 둥근 가장자리가 보입니: The ground of Venus as Venera 9 photographed it. The round rim of the lander shows at the bottom.
풍선은 프랑스 과학자 자크 블라몽이 낸 생각입니다. 지구 곳곳의 전파망원: The balloon was the idea of the French scientist Jacques Blamont. Twenty radio telescopes around the Earth worked together to find where it was. Where it floated the pressure is half of Earth's and it is about 30 degrees: the most Earth-like place on Venus. Nine months later the two Vegas passed Halley's Comet and photographed its nucleus. The name joins the first letters of the Russian words for Venus and Halley.
카메라는 둘이었지만 덮개 하나가 떨어지지 않아 한쪽만 찍었습니다. 사흘: There were two cameras, but one cover did not come off, so only one side was photographed. Its twin Venera 10, which landed three days later, fared the same. Expecting darkness under the thick clouds, the scientists had sent lamps along. But day on Venus is as bright as a cloudy summer day on Earth, and the lamps were not needed. The stones are sharp, not worn: the ground is thought to be young.
베네라 9호가 금성 땅에서 찍어 보낸 것은?: What did Venera 9 take and send from the ground of Venus?
둥실둥실. 구름 구경 간다~: Bobbing along. Off to see the clouds~
Venus has turned into a gold ring.
A rainbow target on the clouds.
태양을 등진 금성의 둘레가 온통 빛의 고리입니다.\n두꺼운 대기가 햇빛을:
With the Sun behind it, all the rim of Venus is a ring of light.
Its thick air bends the sunlight round. When Venus crosses the Sun, the ring shows from Earth too.
금성의 구름 위에 색 고리가 겹겹이 떴습니다.\n태양을 등지고 보면 구름:
Rings of colour lie one inside another on the clouds of Venus.
With the Sun at your back, the droplets of the clouds send its light back the way it came. Venus Express photographed it in 2011.
인도의 첫 화성 탐사선입니다. 2014년 첫 시도에 화성 궤도에 들었습니: India's first Mars probe. In 2014 it entered orbit round Mars on the first try. Built to last six months, it watched Mars for nearly eight years.
첫 시도에 화성으로: To Mars on the first try
2013년 11월 5일 망갈리안이 인도 스리하리코타에서 떠났습니다. 인도: On 5 November 2013 Mangalyaan left Sriharikota in India. It was the first probe India sent to another planet.
로켓의 힘이 모자라 곧장 가지 못했습니다. 지구를 한 달 가까이 돌며 궤: Its rocket was too weak to send it straight there. It circled Earth for nearly a month, widening its orbit, and left for Mars on 1 December.
열 달을 날아 화성에 다가갔습니다. 300일 동안 쉬던 주 엔진을 이틀: After ten months of flight it neared Mars. The main engine had slept for 300 days; two days before, it was fired for 4 seconds and was sound.
2014년 9월 24일, 엔진을 23분 동안 켜 속도를 줄였습니다. 화성: On 24 September 2014 the engine burned for 23 minutes to slow the craft down. Mars caught it.
첫 시도에 화성 궤도에 든 나라는 인도가 처음입니다. 여섯 달을 버티게: India was the first country to reach Mars orbit on its first try. Built to last six months, the craft worked for nearly eight years.
망갈리안은 인도가 보낸 첫 화성 탐사선입니다. 이름은 화성으로 가는 배라: Mangalyaan is the first Mars probe sent by India. Its name means a ship to Mars. It left Sriharikota on 5 November 2013 on a PSLV rocket. The rocket was too weak to send it straight, so it circled Earth for nearly a month, firing its engine several times to widen its orbit, and then set out for Mars. On 24 September 2014 it entered orbit round Mars. India was the first country to reach Mars orbit on its first try.
든 돈은 약 7,400만 달러로, 다른 나라 화성 탐사선의 몇 분의 일이: It cost about 74 million dollars, a fraction of what other countries' Mars probes cost. It went round once in three days on a long path that came within 421 km of Mars and swung out to 77,000 km. From far out it caught the whole of Mars in one picture. Built to last six months, it worked for nearly eight years, until contact was lost in April 2022. It goes round Mars still.
화성아. 한 번에 왔어: Mars, I made it in one go
소행성 베스타와 왜행성 세레스의 궤도에 차례로 든 탐사선입니다. 이온 엔: The probe that went round the asteroid Vesta and then the dwarf planet Ceres. It flew on ion engines. Its fuel ran out in 2018, and it goes round Ceres still.
왜행성에 처음 닿다: First to reach a dwarf planet
2007년 9월 27일 돈 탐사선이 떠났습니다. 태양계가 처음 생기던 때: On 27 September 2007 Dawn set out. It went to the asteroid belt to learn of the days when the solar system was new.
이온 엔진을 썼습니다. 미는 힘은 종이 한 장 무게쯤이지만, 몇 해를 쉬: It flew on ion engines. Their push is about the weight of a sheet of paper, but they can burn for years without a rest.
2011년 7월 소행성 베스타에 닿아 열네 달을 돌았습니다. 그러고는 궤: In July 2011 it reached the asteroid Vesta and went round it for fourteen months. Then it left that orbit and made for Ceres.
2015년 3월 6일, 세레스가 탐사선을 붙잡았습니다. 왜행성의 궤도에: On 6 March 2015 Ceres caught the craft. It was the first to orbit a dwarf planet, and the first to orbit two worlds in turn.
충돌구 안에 밝은 점들이 보였습니다. 땅속의 짠물이 올라와 마르고 남은: Bright spots showed inside a crater. They were salt, left when salty water from below came up and dried.
세레스의 밝은 점들은 무엇이었나?: What were the bright spots on Ceres?
돈 탐사선은 2007년 9월 27일에 떠났습니다. 이름은 영어로 새벽이라: Dawn set out on 27 September 2007. It went to Vesta and Ceres, the two largest bodies of the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter. Both are worlds that stopped short of becoming planets, so they keep the look of the days when the solar system was new. It went round Vesta for fourteen months from July 2011, and reached Ceres on 6 March 2015. No craft before it had orbited two worlds beyond Earth in turn.
이 일은 이온 엔진 덕에 할 수 있었습니다. 제논 가스에 전기를 걸어 내: Ion engines made this possible. They charge xenon gas with electricity and shoot it out; the push is about the weight of a sheet of paper, but they use very little fuel and can burn for years. The bright spots seen inside a crater on Ceres were salt, left when salty water from below came up and dried. On 1 November 2018 the fuel that kept it pointed ran out, and contact was lost. It goes round Ceres still.
유럽이 보낸 목성 얼음 위성 탐사선입니다. 2023년에 떠나 2031년: Europe's probe to Jupiter's icy moons. It left in 2023 and reaches Jupiter in 2031. It will skim Europa and Callisto and go into orbit round Ganymede.
달과 지구를 잇달아 스치다: Past the Moon and Earth, a day apart
2023년 4월 14일 주스가 프랑스령 기아나에서 떠났습니다. 목성의 얼: On 14 April 2023 JUICE left French Guiana. It is Europe's probe to three icy moons of Jupiter.
길이 16m 레이더 안테나가 펴지다 걸렸습니다. 한 달 가까이 몸을 흔들: Its 16 m radar antenna stuck as it unfolded. Nearly a month of shaking the craft and warming it in the Sun set it free.
2024년 8월 19일 달을, 하루 뒤 지구를 스쳤습니다. 달과 지구의: On 19 August 2024 it skimmed the Moon, and a day later Earth. No craft before it had borrowed the pull of both in a row.
2025년 8월에는 금성을 스쳤습니다. 지구를 두 번 더 스친 뒤 203: In August 2025 it skimmed Venus. After two more passes of Earth it reaches Jupiter in July 2031.
2034년에는 가니메데 둘레에 듭니다. 지구의 달이 아닌 다른 달을 도는: In 2034 it goes into orbit round Ganymede: the first craft to orbit a moon that is not our own.
주스는 유럽우주국이 목성의 얼음 위성으로 보낸 탐사선입니다. 이름은 목성: JUICE is the probe the European Space Agency sent to Jupiter's icy moons. Its name is made of the first letters of Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer. It left on 14 April 2023 on an Ariane 5 rocket. Too weak to go straight there, it skimmed the Moon and Earth in August 2024 and Venus in August 2025 to gain speed. After two more passes of Earth it is to reach Jupiter in July 2031.
목성에 닿으면 유로파를 2번, 칼리스토를 21번, 가니메데를 12번 스쳐: At Jupiter it will skim Europa twice, Callisto 21 times and Ganymede 12 times. All three moons are thought to hold a sea under their ice. In December 2034 it goes into orbit round Ganymede: no craft has yet orbited a moon other than our own. Sunlight at Jupiter is one twenty-fifth of what Earth gets, so it carries 85 square metres of solar panels. It also carries a radar that looks 9 km down into the ice.
목성 적도 조금 위(북위 6.5도) 구름 꼭대기의 돌입 자리 20,000: Reach within 20,000 km of the entry place on the cloud tops, a little north of Jupiter's equator (6.5° N)
1995년 12월 7일 갈릴레오의 탐사구가 이곳 구름 속으로 뛰어들었습니: On 7 December 1995 Galileo's probe plunged into the clouds here. For 58 minutes it measured the air of Jupiter itself.
1979년 보이저 1호가 찾은 겹겹의 둥근 무늬입니다. 지름 3,800k: Rings within rings, found by Voyager 1 in 1979. At 3,800 km across it is the largest many-ringed basin in the solar system.
가니메데에서 가장 큰 어두운 땅입니다. 1996년 갈릴레오가 이 달 곁을: The largest dark land on Ganymede. In 1996 Galileo, passing this moon, found that Ganymede has a magnetic field.
갈릴레오 탐사선은 목성에 닿기 다섯 달 전인 1995년 7월, 무게 33: In July 1995, five months before it reached Jupiter, the Galileo craft let go a probe of 339 kg. On 7 December the probe struck the air of Jupiter at 47 km a second: the fastest that anything made by people has entered an atmosphere. More than half of its heat shield burned away. Then it opened the parachute and went down 156 km in 58 minutes, measuring the heat, the wind and what the air is made of. Its signal stopped where the pressure is 23 times that of Earth and the heat is 153 degrees.
떠나기 전 조립실에 놓인 갈릴레오 탐사구. 위가 탐사구 본체, 아래가 열: Galileo's probe in the room where it was put together, before it left. Above is the probe itself, below it the heat shield.
발할라는 얼음으로 덮인 칼리스토에 있는 겹겹의 둥근 무늬입니다. 가운데에: Valhalla is a pattern of rings within rings on Callisto, a moon covered with ice. In the middle is a bright land 360 km across, and round it stand ridges and troughs in ring after ring. Measured to the outermost ring it is 3,800 km across, more than three quarters of Callisto's own width. A large body struck here about four billion years ago. Voyager 1 photographed it first, in March 1979. Its name is the hall where fallen warriors go in Norse myth.
보이저 1호가 찍은 발할라 분지. 밝은 가운데를 둥근 고리들이 겹겹이 에: The Valhalla basin as Voyager 1 saw it: a bright middle with ring upon ring about it.
가니메데는 지름 5,268km로 태양계에서 가장 큰 달입니다. 행성인 수: Ganymede is 5,268 km across, the largest moon in the solar system. It is larger even than the planet Mercury. Its face is part dark land and part bright. Galileo Regio is the largest of the dark lands, some 3,200 km across: old ice, four billion years old. The bright lands are furrowed ground, made later when the ice cracked and pulled apart. On 27 June 1996 the Galileo craft passed 835 km above and found that Ganymede makes a magnetic field of its own.
갈릴레오 탐사선이 가까이에서 찍은 가니메데. 갈릴레오 지역 곁의 고랑 지: Ganymede from close by, as the Galileo craft saw it: furrowed ground beside Galileo Regio.
탐사구가 떨어진 곳은 하필 구름이 걷힌 마른 자리였습니다. 그래서 물이: The probe happened to fall where the clouds had cleared and the air was dry. So it found far less water than expected, and for a while the scientists were puzzled. The wind did not slacken deeper down and blew at more than 500 km an hour. Wind that deep, where no sunlight comes, means that what drives Jupiter's weather is heat rising from within. Deeper still the probe melted and became part of Jupiter.
달의 큰 분지에는 높은 산이 둘러서 있지만 발할라에는 없습니다. 칼리스토: The great basins of the Moon have high mountains about them; Valhalla has none. Callisto's crust is ice, so the pit where the body struck slowly filled itself in. The rings are thought to be cracks made as the land round it was drawn inward while the pit filled. Callisto is the most thickly cratered body in the solar system. That means its ground has hardly been covered afresh in four billion years.
자기장이 있는 달은 가니메데 하나뿐입니다. 속에 녹은 쇠가 돌고 있다는: Ganymede is the only moon with a magnetic field. It means molten iron is turning inside it. Because of that field, auroras glow about Ganymede's poles. Hubble saw how little those auroras sway, and from that it was reckoned that a salty sea lies under the ice. It may hold more water than all the seas of Earth together. The name comes from Galileo Galilei, who found this moon in 1610.
탐사구가 내려가며 편 것은?: What did the probe open as it went down?
달 가운데 가니메데에만 있는 것은?: What does Ganymede alone have among moons?
1979년 3월 6일. 하루 전 목성을 스친 보이저 1호가 가장 바깥의: March 6, 1979. A day after skimming Jupiter, Voyager 1 passes Callisto, the outermost of the large moons.
가장 가까울 때 거리는 126,400km입니다. 어두운 얼음 땅은 크고: At its closest it is 126,400 km away. The dark, icy ground is covered edge to edge with craters large and small.

일본의 소행성 탐사선입니다. 소행성 류구에 두 번 내려 흙을 모아, 20: A Japanese asteroid probe. It landed twice on the asteroid Ryugu, gathered soil and sent it to Earth in a capsule in December 2020. Now it is on its way to another asteroid.
지구에서 태양 쪽으로 150만km 떨어진 L1 점에서 30년째 태양을 지: For 30 years it has watched the Sun from the L1 point, 1.5 million km from Earth toward the Sun. In its pictures people have found more than 5,000 comets.
유럽과 미국의 태양 탐사선입니다. 두꺼운 방패로 열을 막으며 수성보다 안: A European and American probe to the Sun. Keeping off the heat with a thick shield, it goes in closer than Mercury, and in 2025 it photographed the Sun's south pole for the first time.
중국의 첫 화성 탐사선입니다. 2021년 화성 궤도에 들어 탐사차 주룽을: China's first Mars probe. It went into orbit round Mars in 2021 and sent down the rover Zhurong; it still goes round Mars taking pictures.
소행성 베누의 흙과 돌을 2023년 지구로 가져온 미국 탐사선입니다. 지: The American probe that brought soil and stones from the asteroid Bennu to Earth in 2023. Now, under a new name, OSIRIS-APEX, it is on its way to the asteroid Apophis.
유럽의 소행성 탐사선입니다. 2022년 미국의 다트가 일부러 부딪혀 궤도: A European asteroid probe. It is on its way to look at the asteroid Dimorphos, whose orbit the American DART changed by crashing into it on purpose in 2022.
케플러를 이어 외계 행성을 찾는 위성입니다. 카메라 네 대로 하늘을 조각: A satellite that took over from Kepler in looking for planets of other stars. Sweeping the sky piece by piece with four cameras, it catches the moment a star's light dims a little.

Hayabusa2 is a Japanese asteroid probe that left on 3 December 2014. Its name means peregrine falcon. In June 2018 it reached Ryugu, an asteroid about 900 m across: shaped like a spinning top, bulging at the middle, and black, strewn with boulders. In February and July 2019 it touched down twice and picked up soil.
두 번째로 내리기 전에 구리 덩어리를 쏘아 지름 15m쯤의 구덩이를 팠습: Before the second landing it fired a lump of copper to dig a crater about 15 m across, so it took soil from underground too, unbleached by sunlight. On 6 December 2020 the capsule came down in the Australian desert with 5.4 g of soil inside. More than twenty amino acids, building blocks of life, were found in it. The probe only let the capsule go and flew on; it is due to reach the small asteroid 1998 KY26 in 2031.
소호 태양 관측선은 1995년 12월 2일에 떠난 유럽과 미국의 관측선입: The SOHO solar observatory is a European and American observatory that left on 2 December 1995. It circles the L1 point between Earth and the Sun, where the pulls of the two balance. From there the Sun can always be seen, never hidden by Earth or the Moon. Built to work for two or three years, it has been working for more than 30.
태양을 가리고 둘레의 코로나를 찍는 카메라에는, 태양에 바짝 다가갔다 타: Its camera that blocks out the Sun to photograph the corona round it often catches small comets that swoop close to the Sun and burn up. People all over the world, combing the pictures posted on the internet, found the 4,000th comet in 2020 and the 5,000th in 2024. Most of them found theirs at home, with no telescope. In 1998 it was out of touch for nearly four months and then came back to life.
솔라 오비터는 2020년 2월 10일에 떠난 유럽과 미국의 태양 탐사선입: Solar Orbiter is a European and American probe to the Sun that left on 10 February 2020. At its closest it comes within 42 million km of the Sun, inside the orbit of Mercury. The shield in front heats up past 500 degrees, and its cameras look out at the Sun through small windows in the shield.
지금까지 태양은 거의 적도 쪽에서만 보였습니다. 행성들이 모두 태양의 적: Until now the Sun has been seen almost only from near its equator, because the planets all go round on much the same plane as the Sun's equator. Each time Solar Orbiter passes Venus it tilts its orbit a little more; in February 2025 the tilt was 17 degrees. That March it photographed the Sun's south pole for the first time, and the magnetic field there was not neatly split into south and north but jumbled: a sign that the Sun is at its most active.
Tianwen-1 is China's first Mars probe, which left on 23 July 2020. Its name means "questions to heaven", from a poem by the Chinese poet Qu Yuan 2,300 years ago. It went into orbit round Mars in February 2021 and on 15 May sent its lander down onto Utopia Planitia. It was the first to do it all, orbiter, lander and rover, with a single launch.
탐사차 주룽은 화성의 땅 위를 1.9km 달리며 땅속을 레이더로 들여다봤: The rover Zhurong drove 1.9 km over the ground of Mars, looking under it with radar. After it went into hibernation in May 2022 it never woke up. The orbiter passed Zhurong's signals on to Earth and photographed the whole of Mars to make a map. It even let go of a small camera that took a picture of it over Mars.
OSIRIS-REx is an American asteroid probe that left on 8 September 2016. In December 2018 it reached Bennu, an asteroid about 500 m across. On 20 October 2020 it reached out its arm, tapped the ground for a few seconds and puffed nitrogen gas, catching the soil and stones that flew up.
땅이 생각보다 훨씬 무른 모래 더미 같아서, 팔이 0.5m나 파묻혔습니다: The ground was far looser than expected, like a soft heap of sand, and the arm sank 0.5 m into it. On 24 September 2023 the capsule landed in the Utah desert in America with 121.6 g inside. In that soil were minerals formed where water had soaked in, and amino acids. The probe flew on, and under a new name, OSIRIS-APEX, it will follow the asteroid Apophis, which passes Earth in April 2029.
헤라는 2024년 10월 7일에 떠난 유럽의 소행성 탐사선입니다. 가는: Hera is a European asteroid probe that left on 7 October 2024. It is going to the asteroid Didymos and the small moon that circles it, Dimorphos. On 26 September 2022 the American probe DART crashed into Dimorphos on purpose at 6 km a second. It was the first test of whether an asteroid can be pushed aside, should one someday come flying at Earth.
부딪힌 뒤 디모르포스가 디디모스를 한 바퀴 도는 시간은 11시간 55분에: After the crash, the time Dimorphos takes to go once round Didymos fell from 11 hours 55 minutes to 11 hours 23 minutes, 32 minutes shorter. Hera arrives at the end of 2026 to measure the scar and the changed shape. It brings two small satellites to send close to Dimorphos, and at the end it will set one of them down on it. In March 2025 it passed Mars and photographed its moon Deimos.
테스 외계 행성 탐사 위성은 2018년 4월 18일에 떠난 미국의 위성입: TESS is an American satellite for finding planets of other stars, which left on 18 April 2018. It goes round Earth once in 13.7 days on a long, stretched orbit. It is timed to go round exactly twice while the Moon goes round once, so that the Moon's pull does not shake its orbit.
카메라 네 대가 한 줄로 서서 하늘의 넓은 띠 하나를 27일씩 지켜봅니다: Its four cameras stand in a row and watch one broad strip of sky for 27 days at a time, catching the moment a star's light dims a little as a planet passes in front of it. In its first two years it swept three quarters of the sky. Because it watches nearby bright stars, the planets it finds are easy to look at again with big telescopes. So far it has found more than 7,000 candidate planets, over 600 of them confirmed.
탐사선 일곱이 새로 생겼습니다: 하야부사2, 소호, 솔라 오비터, 톈원: Seven new spacecraft: Hayabusa2, SOHO, Solar Orbiter, Tianwen-1, OSIRIS-REx, Hera and TESS.
2014년 12월 3일 하야부사2가 다네가시마에서 떠났습니다. 2018년: On 3 December 2014 Hayabusa2 left Tanegashima. In June 2018 it reached Ryugu, an asteroid 900 m across.
류구는 팽이 모양이고 온통 돌무더기였습니다. 평평한 곳이 없어 내리는 날: Ryugu was shaped like a spinning top and covered in boulders. With no flat ground, the touchdown was put off four months.
2019년 2월 22일 첫 착지. 뿔 끝이 땅에 닿는 순간 작은 총알을: 22 February 2019, the first touch. As the tip of its horn met the ground it fired a small bullet and caught the soil that flew up.
4월에는 구리 덩어리를 쏘아 구덩이를 팠고, 7월 11일 그 곁에 다시: In April it shot a lump of copper to dig a crater, and on 11 July it touched down beside it, catching soil from under the ground too.
2020년 12월 6일 캡슐이 호주 사막에 떨어졌습니다. 흙 5.4g 안: On 6 December 2020 its capsule came down in the Australian desert. In 5.4 g of soil were amino acids, building blocks of life.

1995년 12월 2일 소호가 떠났습니다. 지구에서 태양 쪽으로 150만: SOHO left on 2 December 1995. It settled at L1, 1.5 million km from Earth toward the Sun, and watches the Sun.
카메라 앞에 작은 원판을 세워 태양의 밝은 몸을 가립니다. 그러면 둘레로: A small disc set before a camera covers the bright Sun. Then the faint corona reaching out round it can be seen.
1998년 6월 연락이 끊겼습니다. 한 달 만에 아레시보 전파 망원경으로: In June 1998 contact was lost. A month later the Arecibo radio telescope found it, and in three months it was woken again.
사진 속에 해로 뛰어들다 녹아 없어지는 작은 혜성이 자꾸 보였습니다. 사: Its pictures kept showing small comets diving into the Sun and melting away. The pictures are put up for anyone to see.
2024년 3월, 그 사진으로 찾은 혜성이 5,000개가 되었습니다. 대: By March 2024, 5,000 comets had been found in them. Most were found by people looking through the pictures at home.
2020년 2월 10일 솔라 오비터가 미국 플로리다에서 떠났습니다. 유럽: On 10 February 2020 Solar Orbiter left Florida. It is a Sun probe built by Europe and the United States together.
태양 쪽 방패는 500도 넘게 달궈집니다. 방패에 낸 작은 문을 열고 그: Its sunward shield heats up past 500 °C. It opens small doors in the shield and looks at the Sun through the gaps.
처음 찍은 사진에 아주 작은 불꽃이 가득했습니다. 크기가 작은 나라만 해: Its first pictures were full of tiny flares. Each the size of a small country, they were named campfires.
금성을 스칠 때마다 궤도가 조금씩 기울었습니다. 2025년 2월에는 태양: Each pass by Venus tipped its orbit a little more. In February 2025 it was tipped 17 degrees from the Sun's equator.
2025년 3월 태양의 남극을 처음 찍었습니다. 남극의 자기장은 한쪽으로: In March 2025 it took the first pictures of the Sun's south pole. Its magnetic field there was not one way but tangled.
2020년 7월 23일 톈원 1호가 하이난섬 원창에서 떠났습니다. 궤도선: On 23 July 2020 Tianwen-1 left Wenchang on Hainan Island, carrying an orbiter, a lander and a rover all at once.
2021년 2월 10일 화성 궤도에 들었습니다. 석 달 동안 내릴 자리인: On 10 February 2021 it went into orbit round Mars. For three months it looked down on Utopia Planitia, where it would land.
5월 15일, 착륙선이 궤도선에서 떨어져 나갑니다. 낙하산을 펴고, 엔진: On 15 May the lander parts from the orbiter. It opens a parachute, fires its engine and comes down.
5월 22일 탐사차 주룽이 땅으로 내려섰습니다. 계획한 90일을 넘겨 1: On 22 May the rover Zhurong rolled onto the ground. Going past its planned 90 days, it drove 1,921 m over nearly a year.
처음 가는 길에 궤도에 들고, 내리고, 달리기까지 해낸 나라는 중국이 처: China was the first to orbit, land and drive on its very first trip. The rover is named after Zhurong, a god of fire.
2016년 9월 8일 오시리스-렉스가 떠났습니다. 2018년 12월 지름: OSIRIS-REx left on 8 September 2016. In December 2018 it reached Bennu, an asteroid 500 m across.
고운 모래밭일 줄 알았던 베누는 큰 바위투성이였습니다. 내릴 자리로 지름: Bennu, thought to be fine sand, was covered in big boulders. For the touch it chose Nightingale, a crater 20 m across.
2020년 10월 20일, 팔 끝을 땅에 6초 동안 댔습니다. 질소를 뿜: On 20 October 2020 it touched the ground with the end of its arm for 6 seconds, blew nitrogen and caught the stones and soil that flew up.
땅은 거의 버티지 못했습니다. 팔은 50cm 가까이 파고들었고, 그대로: The ground hardly held at all. The arm sank nearly 50 cm; had it stayed, the craft could have sunk in.
2023년 9월 24일 캡슐이 미국 유타 사막에 내렸습니다. 121.6g: On 24 September 2023 its capsule landed in the Utah desert. It held 121.6 g, with building blocks of life inside.
2022년 9월 26일. 미국의 다트가 초속 6km로 소행성 디모르포스에: 26 September 2022. NASA's DART flew into the asteroid Dimorphos at 6 km a second. It hit on purpose.
Dimorphos, about 150 m across, is a small moon of the larger asteroid Didymos. The test: can a rock headed for Earth be pushed aside?
한 바퀴에 11시간 55분 걸리던 것이 32분 줄었습니다. 부서져 나간: Its trip round, 11 hours 55 minutes, became 32 minutes shorter. Broken-off stones stretched out over 10,000 km like a tail.
2024년 10월 7일 유럽의 헤라가 떠났습니다. 2025년 3월 화성을: Europe's Hera left on 7 October 2024. In March 2025 it flew by Mars and took pictures of its small moon Deimos.
2026년 12월 디디모스에 닿아 부딪힌 자리를 살핍니다. 싣고 간 작은: In December 2026 it reaches Didymos to look at where DART hit. One small satellite it carries will try to land on Dimorphos.
2018년 4월 18일 테스가 미국 플로리다에서 떠났습니다. 케플러가 하: On 18 April 2018 TESS left Florida. Where Kepler watched one patch of sky, TESS watches almost all of it.
카메라 넷이 길게 이어진 하늘의 띠 하나를 27일 동안 바라봅니다. 그다: Its four cameras watch one long strip of sky for 27 days, then move on to the next strip.
달과 박자를 맞춘 궤도를 13.7일에 한 바퀴 돕니다. 달에 끌려 흔들리: It goes round once every 13.7 days, in step with the Moon. Not pulled about by the Moon, it can stay there a long time.
가까이 있는 밝은 별들을 봅니다. 그래서 찾은 행성은 다른 망원경으로 그: It watches bright stars nearby, so other telescopes can look at the planets it finds, even at their air.
행성 후보를 7,000개 넘게 찾았고 그중 600개 넘게가 행성으로 밝혀: It has found over 7,000 likely planets, and over 600 have been shown to be planets. Several are the size of Earth.

새 탐사선 일곱에 \"그날로\" 장면이 생겼습니다. 장면은 모두 138개: The seven new craft now have "That day" scenes. There are 138 scenes in all.
2010년 2월 13일. 카시니가 토성의 작은 위성 미마스 곁을 지나갑니: 13 February 2010. Cassini passes Saturn's small moon Mimas, a ball of ice 396 km across.
가장 가까울 때 거리는 9,500km입니다. 그때까지 미마스에 가장 가까: At its closest it is 9,500 km away, nearer to Mimas than any craft had come before.
찰칵. 지름 130km의 허셜 분화구가 한쪽 얼굴을 다 차지했습니다. 한: Click. Herschel, a crater 130 km across, fills one whole face. The peak in its middle is 6 km high.
같은 날 잰 온도는 팩맨 모양으로 나뉘어 있었습니다. 충돌이 조금만 더: Temperatures taken that day fell into a Pac-Man shape. A little harder a blow and Mimas would have shattered.

미마스의 허셜 분화구에 \"그날로\" 장면이 생겼습니다. 장면은 모두 1: Herschel crater on Mimas now has a "That day" scene. There are 139 scenes in all.

목성과 이오 사이에 대리석 판 하나가 떠 있습니다. 가로, 세로, 두께가:
A slab of marble floats between Jupiter and Io. Its width, height and thickness go 1 : 4 : 9.
Nobody knows who put it there, or why. The ship before it seems to have come to look at it too.
목성과 이오 사이에 대리석 모노리스가 생겼습니다. 그 앞에 우주선 한 척: A marble Monolith now floats between Jupiter and Io, with a ship stopped before it.
목표를 고정한 채 순간 이동하거나 바라보기를 누르면 고정이 저절로 풀립니: With a target locked, a Jump or "Face" now lets go of the lock by itself.
지어낸 이야기입니다. 우주선 한 척이 목성까지 날아와, 목성과 이오 사이: A made-up story. A ship has flown all the way to Jupiter, and slows down before the slab floating between Jupiter and Io.
우주선은 엔진 불을 끄고, 가운데 바퀴를 천천히 돌리며 판 쪽으로 미끄러: The ship puts out its engines and glides on toward the slab, the wheel at its middle slowly turning.
우주선이 판 앞에 멈춥니다. 판의 두께, 너비, 높이는 1:4:9, 1,: The ship stops before the slab. Its thickness, width and height go 1:4:9, the squares of 1, 2 and 3.
태양이 판의 꼭대기에 걸렸습니다. 누가 왜 두었는지는 아직 아무도 모릅니: The Sun rests on the top of the slab. Who put it there, and why, nobody knows yet.
모노리스 곁에서 판을 고르면 \"그날로\" 장면을 볼 수 있습니다. 우주: Choose the monolith from beside it to watch its "That day" scene: a ship comes in and stops before the slab.

Between Earth and Mars a china teapot goes round the Sun.
It is the philosopher Russell's figure: a thing too small for anyone to prove it is not there.

On a little star in the asteroid belt there are three volcanoes, a baobab sprout and a single rose.
It looks just like a star from a book you may have read.
In the Moon's crater Tycho stands a marble slab of 1:4:9, like the one by Jupiter.
In the novel and the film, once it was dug up, it sent a signal toward Jupiter.
Just like the one at Jupiter.
지구와 화성 사이에 러셀의 찻주전자, 소행성대에 장미가 있는 작은 별,: Russell's Teapot now goes round between Earth and Mars, a little star with a rose sits in the asteroid belt, and a Monolith stands in the Moon's crater Tycho.
They say a teapot goes round between Earth and Mars.
They say there is a strange slab in Tycho.
They say a star in the belt has a rose on it.
They say a white slab floats out toward Io.
달의 판이 깨어나다: The Slab on the Moon Wakes
지어낸 이야기입니다. 달의 티코 분화구에서 자기장이 이상한 곳을 파 보니: A made-up story. Where the magnetism ran strangely in the Moon's crater Tycho, people dug, and found a slab buried there.
우주복을 입은 사람들이 파낸 구덩이로 내려와 판을 둘러섭니다. 판은 아주: People in spacesuits come down into the dug pit and stand round the slab. It had lain buried there since long, long ago.
한 사람이 장갑 낀 손으로 판을 쓸어 봅니다. 다 같이 판 앞에 서서 사: One of them runs a gloved hand over it. They all line up before it to have their picture taken.
그때 태양이 판 위로 떠올라 처음으로 햇빛이 닿습니다. 판이 날카로운 신: Just then the Sun rises over the slab and sunlight touches it for the first time. The slab sends a piercing signal toward Jupiter.
1952년, 철학자 버트런드 러셀은 이렇게 썼습니다. 지구와 화성 사이에: In 1952 the philosopher Bertrand Russell wrote: suppose a small china teapot goes round the Sun between Earth and Mars.
찻주전자는 너무 작아서 아무리 큰 망원경으로도 보이지 않습니다. 그러니: It is too small to be seen by even the greatest telescope. So nobody can prove it is not there.
Russell said nobody may be asked to believe it only because it cannot be disproved. The proof is for whoever says it is there.
But in this game's universe, the teapot really is here.
작은 별의 하루: A Day on the Little Star
책 속 이야기를 닮은 별입니다. 아주 작아서, 의자를 몇 걸음만 옮기면: A star like one in a book. It is so small that moving the chair a few steps lets you watch the Sun set again.
별의 주인은 아침마다 화산을 청소합니다. 불이 꺼진 화산도 언제 깰지 모: Every morning the star's keeper sweeps the volcanoes, the dead one too, since nobody knows when it may wake.
바오밥 싹은 보이는 대로 뽑아야 합니다. 그냥 두면 뿌리가 별을 뚫고 별: Baobab sprouts must be pulled as soon as they are seen. Left alone, their roots would bore through the star and split it.
유리 덮개 아래 장미 한 송이가 바람을 피해 있습니다. 주인이 날마다 물: Under a glass cover a single rose is kept from the wind. Its keeper waters it and looks after it every day.
달의 모노리스, 러셀의 찻주전자, 장미가 있는 작은 별에도 \"그날로\": The Monolith on the Moon, Russell's Teapot and the Little Star with a Rose now have their "That day" scenes too.
책과 영화, 이야기에서 온 상상 속 장소입니다. 수첩 칸에는 들지 않고,: Imagined places from books, films and stories. They are not notebook slots; once you have been, you can jump to them any time.
탐험 수첩에 \"상상\" 칸이 생겼습니다. 상상 속 장소 넷을 모아 두고: The notebook has a new "Imagined" tab: the four imagined places, each one you have been to a jump away.
달이 지구 쪽으로 제 앞면을 보입니다. 지금까지는 127도 돌아간 옆얼굴: The Moon now shows Earth its near side. Until now it showed a side turned 127 degrees away.

난데없이 하늘에 생겨난 고래는 이게 뭔지, 자기가 누군지 궁금해하며 떨어: Out of nowhere in the sky, the whale falls wondering what all this is, and who it is.

이 게임 속 우주에서는 다행히 둘 다 떨어지지 않고 지구 앞에 떠 있습니: In this game's universe, luckily, neither falls: both float ahead of Earth.
지어낸 이야기입니다. 토성 곁에 누군가 두고 간 구멍이 나타났습니다. 둘: A made-up story. Beside Saturn a hole appeared that someone had left. The light round it seems to bend.
정거장은 바퀴처럼 돌며 안쪽에 무게를 만듭니다. 작은 우주선 한 척이 정: The station turns like a wheel, making weight inside it. A small spaceship leaves the station.

구조대가 올 때까지 그는 감자로 버텼습니다. 이 게임 속 화성에도 그 밭: He lived on potatoes until the rescue came. The farm is still there on this game's Mars.

겉면에는 트는 법과, 펄서 14개로 태양의 자리를 알리는 지도가 새겨져: On its cover are how to play it and a map giving the Sun's place by 14 pulsars.

It gathers up the scattered rubbish and squashes it hard into square blocks.
It stacks the blocks neatly one on another, and the tower grows one more storey.
일을 마친 로봇이 고개를 들어 하늘을 봅니다. 저 멀리 밝은 점 하나가: Its work done, the robot looks up at the sky. Far off, one bright dot is the Sun.

지구 남아프리카공화국 서덜랜드의 SALT(남위 32.4도, 동경 20.8: Land within 60 km of SALT at Sutherland, South Africa, on Earth (32.4° S, 20.8° E)
남아프리카공화국 서덜랜드의 해발 1,798m 언덕에 있습니다. 육각형 거: It stands on a hill 1,798 m up near Sutherland, South Africa. Its 11 m mirror is made of 91 hexagonal pieces.
베라 C. 루빈 천문대는 칠레 안데스산맥의 세로 파촌 산, 해발 2,64: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory stands on Cerro Pachón in the Chilean Andes, 2,647 m above the sea. Its 8.4 m telescope carries a 3,200-megapixel camera the size of a small car, the largest digital camera in the world. Its first pictures came out on 23 June 2025: in a little over ten hours of photographs it found 2,104 new asteroids. For ten years it will photograph the whole southern sky every three or four nights and catch everything that moves or changes.
저녁 무렵 칠레 세로 파촌 산(해발 2,682m) 위의 루빈 천문대. 지: The Rubin Observatory at dusk on Cerro Pachón, Chile (2,682 m up). With an 8.4 m mirror and a 3,200-megapixel camera it photographs the whole southern sky every three or four nights, making a ten-year film of how the sky changes.
미어캣은 남아프리카공화국 북케이프주의 카루 반사막에 있는 전파망원경입니다: MeerKAT is a radio telescope in the semi-desert Karoo of South Africa's Northern Cape. Its 64 dishes, each 13.5 m across, are spread up to 8 km apart and used as one large telescope. It opened on 13 July 2018. In 2022 it photographed the heart of our galaxy and showed about 1,000 thin radio threads, some tens of light years long. The SKA, the largest radio telescope in the world, is being built on this site, and MeerKAT's dishes will become part of it.
남아프리카공화국 카루 반사막에 늘어선 미어캣의 접시 안테나들. 지름 13: MeerKAT’s dishes lined up in the semi-desert Karoo of South Africa. Sixty-four dishes 13.5 m across, spread over 8 km, work as one radio telescope; they photographed the huge radio bubbles blown out of the centre of our galaxy.
SALT는 남아프리카공화국 북케이프주 서덜랜드 근처, 해발 1,798m: SALT is an optical telescope on a hill 1,798 m up near Sutherland in South Africa's Northern Cape. Its 91 hexagonal mirrors, each about 1 m across, make up one large mirror 11 m by 9.8 m. It is one of the largest optical telescopes in the southern hemisphere. The mirror always looks at the sky tilted at 37 degrees, and the whole telescope turns on the ground to change direction. A device above the mirror follows the stars as they move. It opened on 10 November 2005.
은빛 돔을 쓴 남아프리카 대형 망원경 SALT. 지름 1m짜리 육각 거울: SALT, the Southern African Large Telescope, under its silver dome. Ninety-one hexagonal mirrors 1 m across are joined like a honeycomb and used as one mirror 11 m wide. The tower beside it keeps the pieces of mirror lined up.
이름은 미국 천문학자 베라 루빈에게서 왔습니다. 루빈은 1970년대에 은: It is named after the American astronomer Vera Rubin. In the 1970s she measured that the stars in the outer parts of galaxies go round faster than expected, and gave evidence for unseen dark matter. The US National Science Foundation and Department of Energy built it together, and about 20 terabytes of pictures pile up in a single night.
이름은 아프리카 초원에 사는 몽구스과 동물 미어캣에서 따왔습니다. 처음: It is named after the meerkat, a small mongoose of the African grasslands. The first plan was a smaller "Karoo Array Telescope" (KAT); when it grew, "meer", Afrikaans for "more", was put in front. The land around it is a radio quiet zone, so mobile phones and Wi-Fi cannot be used freely.

South Africa led, with the United States, Germany, Poland, India, the United Kingdom and New Zealand. Sutherland is known as the coldest town in South Africa, and its dark, clear skies have drawn telescopes from many countries.

In Jaipur, India, stand 19 astronomical instruments made of stone and brass. The largest sundial is 27 m tall.
FAST는 중국 구이저우성 핑탕현의 다워당이라는 카르스트 분지에 있는 전: FAST is a radio telescope in a karst basin called Dawodang, in Pingtang County, Guizhou, China. Its name stands for Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical radio Telescope. The dish is 500 m across and is made of about 4,450 triangular panels. It is the largest single-dish radio telescope in the world. It was finished on 25 September 2016 and went into full operation in January 2020. So far it has found more than 1,000 pulsars. In China it is called "Tianyan" (天眼), the Eye of the Sky.
중국 구이저우 산골짜기의 움푹한 분지에 놓인 FAST. 지름 500m 접: FAST in a hollow among the hills of Guizhou, China. Its 500 m dish is made of 4,450 panels and changes its shape little by little under the receiver hung above it to follow the stars. It is the largest single-dish radio telescope in the world.
잔타르 만타르는 인도 자이푸르에 있는 천문대입니다. 마하라자 사와이 자이: Jantar Mantar is an observatory in Jaipur, India. Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II began building it in 1728 and finished in 1734. Nineteen instruments of stone and brass stand there. The largest, the Samrat Yantra, is a sundial 27 m tall. Its shadow moves about 1 mm a second, so it tells the time to about 2 seconds. It became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2010.
자이푸르 잔타르 만타르의 가장 큰 해시계, 삼라트 얀트라. 높이가 27m: The Samrat Yantra, the largest sundial of Jantar Mantar in Jaipur. It stands 27 m tall, so its shadow moves about 1 mm a second and the time can be read to two seconds. Jai Singh II built it around 1734.
A radio-quiet zone of 5 km surrounds it, and mobile phones may not be brought in. The people who lived inside were moved elsewhere. The telescope was built using a hollow dissolved out of the limestone as its bowl.
\"잔타르 만타르\"는 산스크리트어에서 온 이름으로 \"계산하는 기구\": "Jantar Mantar" is a name from Sanskrit meaning "calculating instrument". Jai Singh built such observatories in five cities of India, and the one in Jaipur is the largest and the best preserved today.
중국에서는 이 망원경을 \"톈옌\"이라 부른다. 무슨 뜻인가?: In China this telescope is called "Tianyan". What does it mean?
가장 큰 해시계의 높이는?: How tall is the largest sundial?

1930년 2월 18일 이곳에서 명왕성을 찾았습니다. 퍼시벌 로웰이 화성: On 18 February 1930 Pluto was found here. Percival Lowell built the observatory in 1894 to watch Mars.
지구 미국 캘리포니아의 팔로마 천문대(북위 33.4도, 서경 116.9도: Land within 40 km of Palomar Observatory in California, USA, on Earth (33.4° N, 116.9° W)
1948년 6월 3일 지름 5.1m의 헤일 망원경이 문을 열었습니다. 1: On 3 June 1948 the Hale Telescope, 5.1 m across, opened. It was the largest telescope in the world until 1975.

1980년 10월 10일 문을 열었습니다. 지름 25m 접시 27개가 Y: It opened on 10 October 1980. Twenty-seven dishes, each 25 m across, work on rails in a Y as one telescope.
로웰 천문대는 미국 애리조나주 플래그스태프의 마스 힐, 곧 \"화성 언덕: Lowell Observatory stands on Mars Hill, the "Mars hill", in Flagstaff, Arizona, USA. The wealthy Percival Lowell built it in 1894 to watch Mars for years on end. On 18 February 1930 Clyde Tombaugh found Pluto here. With the 13-inch (33 cm) Abbot Lawrence Lowell Astrograph he took two photographs of the same patch of sky that January, flicked between them, and picked out one dot that had changed its place. The observatory still watches the stars today, and it welcomes visitors.
마스 힐의 클라크 망원경 돔. 안에는 1896년에 들여온 지름 24인치(: The Clark Telescope dome on Mars Hill. Inside is a refractor 24 inches (61 cm) across, brought here in 1896. Lowell drew Mars with it, and from 1912 Vesto Slipher used it to find the first signs that the galaxies are moving away from us.
팔로마 천문대는 미국 캘리포니아주 남부 팔로마산의 해발 1,700m쯤 되: Palomar Observatory stands on Palomar Mountain in southern California, USA, at about 1,700 m above sea level. The mirror of the Hale Telescope is 200 inches, or 5.1 m, across. It was poured in 1934, and grinding it smooth took 11 years. The telescope opened on 3 June 1948 and was the largest in the world until 1975. It still watches the sky every night.
팔로마산 꼭대기에 선 헤일 망원경의 돔. 높이 41m쯤 되는 이 둥근 지: The dome of the Hale Telescope on top of Palomar Mountain. Under this round roof, about 41 m high, stands the telescope with its 5.1 m mirror. It weighs over 500 tonnes, yet it floats on a thin film of oil and turns smoothly with a small motor.
VLA는 \"아주 큰 배열\"이라는 뜻의 영문 머리글자(Very Larg: VLA stands for Very Large Array. It lies on a high, wide plain west of Socorro, New Mexico, USA. Twenty-seven dishes, each 25 m across, sit on three lines of rail laid out in a Y, and each dish weighs about 230 tonnes. When the radio waves they gather are combined, the picture is as sharp as from one dish 36 km across. It opened on 10 October 1980.
뉴멕시코의 평원에 늘어선 VLA의 접시들. 지름 25m, 무게 230톤의: The VLA’s dishes lined up on the plain of New Mexico. Twenty-seven dishes, each 25 m across and 230 tonnes, move along railway tracks laid out in a Y. Spread wide they work as one telescope 36 km across, and they change places about every four months.
\"명왕성\"이라는 이름은 영국 옥스퍼드의 열한 살 소녀 베네티아 버니가: The name "Pluto" was chosen by Venetia Burney, an eleven-year-old girl from Oxford, England. Its first two letters, P and L, are also the initials of Percival Lowell. Lowell believed there was another planet beyond Neptune and searched for it, but he died in 1916. Tombaugh found Pluto 14 years later.
이름은 천문학자 조지 엘러리 헤일에게서 왔습니다. 헤일은 이 망원경을 지: It is named after the astronomer George Ellery Hale. He led the fund-raising to build this telescope but died in 1938 and never saw it finished. The telescope with its mount weighs about 530 tonnes, and a clockwork drive turns it slowly to follow the stars.
1997년 영화 \"콘택트\"에서 외계의 신호를 듣는 곳으로 나와 널리: It became widely known as the place where a signal from beyond Earth is heard in the 1997 film "Contact". Every few months the dishes are moved along the rails to change the layout. Gathered close, they see wide objects well; spread far apart, they see small things sharply.
헤일 망원경의 거울은 지름이 얼마인가?: How wide is the mirror of the Hale Telescope?

칙술루브의 \"그날로\" 장면에 공룡 셋이 생겼습니다. 언덕에 서 있다가: Chicxulub's "That day" scene now has three dinosaurs: they stand on a rise and look up at the asteroid coming down.
칙술루브 충돌구 카드의 사진이 땅속 충돌구의 둥근 테가 보이는 중력 지도: The Chicxulub crater's card now shows a gravity map, where the buried crater's round rings can be seen.
2010년 8월, 태양 관측 위성 SDO가 자외선으로 찍은 태양. 가장자: The Sun in ultraviolet light, taken by the SDO observatory in August 2010. A prominence rises from its edge.
2008년, 메신저호가 수성을 지나가며 찍은 사진. 땅의 차이가 잘 보이: Mercury as MESSENGER passed it in 2008, its colours heightened to show the different ground.
1974년, 매리너 10호가 찍은 금성의 구름. 짙은 구름이 별 전체를: Venus's clouds, taken by Mariner 10 in 1974. Thick cloud covers the whole planet.
1972년 12월, 아폴로 17호 우주비행사들이 달로 가는 길에 찍은 지: Earth, taken by the Apollo 17 astronauts on their way to the Moon in December 1972. It is called "The Blue Marble".
The full Moon, taken through a telescope from the ground in 2010.

2008년, 화성 정찰 궤도선(MRO)이 찍은 포보스. 커다란 스티크니: Phobos, taken by the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter in 2008. The large Stickney crater can be seen.

Jupiter, taken by Cassini as it passed on its way to Saturn in December 2000. The Great Red Spot can be seen.

갈릴레오 탐사선이 찍은 유로파. 얼음 껍질에 갈색 금이 그물처럼 나 있습: Europa, taken by the Galileo probe. Brown cracks run like a net across its shell of ice.

Callisto, taken by the Galileo probe. It is covered all over with craters.

Mimas, taken by Cassini in 2010. The huge Herschel crater stands out.

Tethys, taken by Cassini. It is a moon of ice, cratered all over.
Dione, taken by Cassini in 2008 in the colours the eye would see.

2005년, 카시니가 사람 눈에 보이는 색으로 찍은 타이탄. 짙은 주황색: Titan, taken by Cassini in 2005 in the colours the eye would see. A thick orange haze hides the ground.
2007년, 카시니가 찍은 이아페투스. 한쪽은 숯처럼 검고 한쪽은 눈처럼: Iapetus, taken by Cassini in 2007. One side is as dark as charcoal, the other as white as snow.
1986년 1월, 보이저 2호가 지나가며 찍은 천왕성. 지금까지 천왕성에: Uranus, taken by Voyager 2 as it passed in January 1986. Voyager 2 is still the only probe to have visited it.
1986년, 보이저 2호가 찍은 미란다. 조각을 이어 붙인 듯 울퉁불퉁한: Miranda, taken by Voyager 2 in 1986. Its ground looks as if it had been patched together from pieces.
1986년, 보이저 2호가 찍은 아리엘. 천왕성의 위성 가운데 가장 밝습: Ariel, taken by Voyager 2 in 1986. It is the brightest of Uranus's moons.
1986년, 보이저 2호가 찍은 움브리엘. 천왕성의 큰 위성 가운데 가장: Umbriel, taken by Voyager 2 in 1986. It is the darkest of Uranus's large moons.
1986년, 보이저 2호가 찍은 티타니아. 천왕성의 위성 가운데 가장 큽: Titania, taken by Voyager 2 in 1986. It is the largest of Uranus's moons.
1986년, 보이저 2호가 찍은 오베론. 천왕성의 큰 위성 가운데 가장: Oberon, taken by Voyager 2 in 1986. It circles farthest out of Uranus's large moons.

1989년, 보이저 2호가 찍은 사진을 이어 붙인 트리톤. 아래쪽 분홍빛: Triton, pieced together from Voyager 2's photos of 1989. The pinkish ground at the bottom is its south polar ice.
돈 탐사선이 찍은 세레스. 밝은 점들은 오카토르 충돌구에 남은 소금입니다: Ceres, taken by the Dawn probe. The bright spots are salt left in Occator crater.
2015년 7월, 뉴허라이즌스가 지나가며 찍은 명왕성. 하트 모양의 밝은: Pluto, taken by New Horizons as it passed in July 2015. The bright heart-shaped plain can be seen.
2015년 7월, 뉴허라이즌스가 찍은 카론. 북극 둘레의 붉은 땅은 \": Charon, taken by New Horizons in July 2015. The reddish ground round its north pole is called "Mordor".
1986년 3월, 유럽의 조토 탐사선이 찍은 핼리 혜성의 핵. 혜성의 핵: The nucleus of Halley's Comet, taken by Europe's Giotto probe in March 1986, the first close photo of a comet's nucleus.

A 1:20 model of Hayabusa2 shown at the Australian Space Discovery Centre.

2022년에 다 지어진 톈궁 정거장을 3D로 그린 그림. 아래로 지구가: A 3D drawing of the Tiangong station as completed in 2022, with Earth below.

톈원 1호, 톈궁, 아카쓰키, 하야부사2, 주노에도 \"사진 보기\"가: Tianwen-1, Tiangong, Akatsuki, Hayabusa2 and Juno now have a "View photo" key too: photos of models and drawings.
스캐너에 가까운 행성이나 위성의 땅이 지평선처럼 차오릅니다. 왼쪽 위에: On the scanner, the ground of a nearby planet or moon now rises like a horizon, with its name and distance in the upper left.
멀리 있는 탐사선 모형을 눌러도 이름표를 누른 것처럼 됩니다. 가 본 탐: Pressing a craft's model from afar now does what its name tag does: if you have met it, you jump over and dock.

설정의 쪽을 바꾸면 고른 쪽이 제 단추에서 혜성 꼬리를 그리며 펼쳐져 나: Turning to another page of the settings, the new page whirls out of its tab with comet tails.

돌무더기가 뭉친 팽이 모양의 소행성입니다. 오시리스-렉스가 떠 온 흙이: A spinning-top heap of loose rubble. Soil scooped up by OSIRIS-REx reached Earth in 2023.

베스타는 화성과 목성 사이 소행성대에서 세레스 다음으로 큰 천체로 지름이: Vesta is the second-largest body in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter, after Ceres, about 525 km across. About 9% of the mass of the whole asteroid belt is in Vesta alone. It was the fourth asteroid found, by Heinrich Olbers of Germany on 29 March 1807, and the mathematician Carl Friedrich Gauss chose for it the name of the Roman goddess of the hearth. Its surface is bright, so it is the only asteroid you can see with the naked eye. Its inside melted once: the heavy iron sank to the middle to make a core, and the lighter rock rose to make a crust. So it is seen as a "protoplanet", a planet that never quite became one.
돈 탐사선이 2011년부터 1년 넘게 곁을 돌았습니다. 남극에는 지름 5: The Dawn spacecraft circled it for more than a year from 2011. At its south pole is the Rheasilvia basin, 500 km across, and the peak in its middle, about 22 km high, is among the highest mountains in the solar system. That is about two and a half times the height of Mount Everest. The blow shook all of Vesta and cut deep grooves hundreds of kilometres long in a band round its equator. Pieces knocked off in that impact fall to Earth as meteorites: about one in twenty of the meteorites found on Earth came from Vesta. In the north, three craters side by side make a place called the "Snowman". It goes round the Sun once in 3.6 years, and its day is 5 hours 20 minutes.
베누는 지름 약 490m의 작은 소행성으로, 롯데월드타워의 높이(555m: Bennu is a small asteroid about 490 m across, a little less than the height of the Lotte World Tower in Seoul (555 m). LINEAR, an American asteroid search, found it on 11 September 1999. In a naming contest with more than 8,000 entries, the name sent in by Michael Puzio, an American third-grader, was chosen: a bird god of Egyptian myth, drawn as a heron. Rich in carbon, it is as black as charcoal, a rubble pile of big and small rocks loosely held together by weak gravity. It is shaped like a spinning top with a bulging equator. In 2019 pictures caught little bits of rock popping off its surface, to everyone's surprise. It goes round the Sun once in 1.2 years and comes near Earth every 6 years.
미국의 오시리스-렉스가 2018년 도착해 2020년 10월 20일 표면에: America's OSIRIS-REx arrived in 2018, touched its surface for a moment on 20 October 2020 and scooped up soil and stones. At the touch the ground gave way like water: it was not solid rock but a loose heap of pebbles that do not stick together. It was so soft that the craft would have sunk in had it stayed. The capsule came down in the Utah desert on 24 September 2023, with 121.6 g of soil and stones, more than twice the goal. In that soil were amino acids, the building blocks of life, and minerals left when salty water dries up, showing that water once flowed on the older body Bennu broke off from. The chance that it hits Earth in 2182 is about 1 in 2,700.
류구는 지름 약 900m의 소행성으로, 한라산 높이(1,947m)의 절반: Ryugu is an asteroid about 900 m across, about half the height of Hallasan, the highest mountain in South Korea (1,947 m). LINEAR, an American asteroid search, found it on 10 May 1999. Its name comes from the Dragon Palace under the sea that Urashima Taro visits in a Japanese folk tale. Just as Taro, a fisherman who saved a turtle, came back from the palace with a treasure box, Hayabusa2 came back from here with a box of soil. Like Bennu it is a rubble pile shaped like a spinning top, and rich in carbon, very dark. It reflects less than 5% of the sunlight, as dark as coal. It turns once in 7.6 hours.
일본의 하야부사2가 2018년 6월 도착했습니다. 그해 9월에는 작은 로: Japan's Hayabusa2 arrived in June 2018. That September it let down two little robots, which hopped about instead of rolling on wheels and sent back the first pictures taken on the surface of an asteroid. In 2019 it fired a lump of metal to make a man-made crater about 14.5 m across, and twice gathered soil, from the surface and from underground. The capsule came down in the Australian desert on 6 December 2020, and the 5.4 g of stones it brought held water and amino acids. Uracil, part of the genetic material of life, was found too. Hayabusa2 had fuel left and is on its way to another asteroid: it is due to reach the small asteroid 1998 KY26 in July 2031. Ryugu goes round the Sun once in 1.3 years.
디디모스는 지름 약 780m의 소행성으로, 작은 위성 디모르포스와 함께: Didymos is an asteroid about 780 m across that goes round with its little moon Dimorphos: a binary asteroid. That is about the length of one and a half Lotte World Towers laid end to end. Its name is Greek for "twin". The Spacewatch telescope at Kitt Peak Observatory in the United States found it on 11 April 1996. At first it was thought to be single, but in 2003 a steady flicker in its brightness and radar observations showed that a small moon goes round it. It is not in danger of hitting Earth, which made it a fit place for a test of changing an asteroid's path by striking it.
2.26시간에 한 바퀴씩 아주 빨리 돌아, 적도의 돌이 겨우 붙어 있을: It spins very fast, once in 2.26 hours, so fast that the rocks on its equator barely hold on. Bits flung off by that spin are thought to have gathered into Dimorphos. In 2022 the DART spacecraft came for the pair, and the pictures it took just before striking showed Didymos's ground strewn with big and small boulders. Europe's Hera spacecraft is due to arrive in December 2026. Hera is bringing two little satellites, Milani and Juventas, to look at the crater left on Dimorphos and look inside it with radio waves. It goes round the Sun once in 2.1 years.
디모르포스는 지름 약 150m로, 디디모스에서 약 1.2km 떨어져 돕니: Dimorphos is about 150 m across and goes round Didymos about 1.2 km away. It is a little bigger than a football pitch. Its name is Greek for "two forms", meaning how it looked before and after the impact. It was first known in 2003 from a flicker in Didymos's brightness, and was only named in 2020. No one had ever seen what it looked like: even in the DART spacecraft's camera it showed up as a dot of its own only about an hour before the impact. After the impact its squat, rounded body is thought to have been squashed into a slightly longer shape.
2022년 9월 26일 무게 570kg의 다트 탐사선이 초속 약 6km로: On 26 September 2022 the DART spacecraft, weighing 570 kg, struck it at about 6 km/s. It was a test of whether the path of an asteroid coming at Earth could be changed. Its orbit grew 32 minutes shorter, from 11 hours 55 minutes to 11 hours 23 minutes, and the rock and dust thrown out stretched more than 10,000 km like a tail. Because the flying rock and dust pushed back, it was shoved about 3.6 times harder than the spacecraft alone could have pushed it. LICIACube, a small Italian satellite that went along with DART, flew past 3 minutes after the impact and photographed the plume of dust, and the Hubble Space Telescope found 37 boulders, 1 to 7 m across, knocked loose and drifting away. It was the first time people changed the motion of a body in space.
아포피스는 지름 약 340m의 소행성으로, 프랑스 에펠탑(330m)과 비: Apophis is an asteroid about 340 m across, about the size of the Eiffel Tower in France (330 m). Roy Tucker, David Tholen and Fabrizio Bernardi found it at Kitt Peak Observatory in the United States on 19 June 2004; it was lost after a few days and found again in Australia that December. Soon after, the chance that it would hit Earth in 2029 rose as high as 2.7%, causing great worry. On the Torino scale, which rates the danger of an asteroid from 0 to 10, it was given a 4, a score no asteroid had ever reached before. Its name comes from the serpent of chaos in Egyptian myth that tries to swallow the sun god. It is also the name of a villain in "Stargate", a television series its finders liked to watch.
더 지켜본 끝에 2021년 앞으로 100년 넘게 부딪칠 일은 없다고 밝혀: After more watching it was shown in 2021 that it will not hit Earth for at least a hundred years. On 13 April 2029 it will pass about 32,000 km from Earth's surface, closer than geostationary satellites. That night it will be seen with the naked eye from Europe and Africa. An asteroid this size passes this close perhaps once in thousands of years. Earth's pull will change its orbit and its spin, and rocks may slide on its surface. OSIRIS-REx, back from Bennu, has been renamed OSIRIS-APEX and will follow it to take a close look. ESA's Ramses spacecraft is also planned to leave in 2028 and reach Apophis about two months before it passes Earth.

돈 탐사선이 2011년 찍은 사진으로 만든 베스타. 아래쪽 남극에 레아실: Vesta, made from pictures the Dawn probe took in 2011. The Rheasilvia basin is at the south pole, at the bottom.
2018년 12월 오시리스-렉스가 24km 거리에서 찍은 사진 12장을: Bennu in twelve pictures joined together, taken by OSIRIS-REx from 24 km away in December 2018.
Ryugu as seen by Hayabusa2, with a bulging ridge round its equator.
Didymos, with little Dimorphos on the right, taken by DART minutes before the impact.
부딪치기 2초 전 다트가 마지막으로 온전히 찍은 디모르포스. 돌무더기가: The last whole picture of Dimorphos, taken by DART two seconds before the impact. The heap of boulders shows plainly.
2021년 3월 미국의 전파 망원경이 1,700만km 밖에서 찍은 아포피: Radar images of Apophis (in the circles) made by American radio telescopes from 17 million km away in March 2021.
I once found Vesta through binoculars myself. It looked like a little star.
To think they brought soil from that little rubble pile back to Earth. What times we live in.
So you have been to the Dragon Palace. Do not go opening any treasure box.

In the spring of 2029, let us watch that rock go by together.
