Bennu again. Shaped like a spinning top, how sweet.
류구를 또 찍었구나. 이번엔 무슨 보물을 찾았니?: Ryugu again. What treasure did you find this time?
The twins again. They go round so nicely together.
Apophis again. A fearsome name, but a quiet rock.
작은 천체 여섯이 생겼습니다. 베스타, 베누, 류구, 디디모스와 디모르포: Six small bodies have appeared: Vesta, Bennu, Ryugu, Didymos and Dimorphos, and Apophis.
처음 찾은, 다른 별에서 온 천체입니다. 2017년 태양 곁을 지나 다시: The first object found that came from another star. It swept past the Sun in 2017 and left again for interstellar space.
세 번째로 찾은 별 사이 손님이자 혜성입니다. 2025년 10월 태양에: The third visitor from between the stars to be found, and a comet. It came closest to the Sun in October 2025.
다른 별에서 온 돌 위에 섰어!: I am standing on a stone from another star!
This ice might be older than the Sun.
2017.10. 하와이 망원경이 찾은 별 사이 손님이라고 신문에서 읽었다: Oct 2017. Read in the paper about a visitor from between the stars, found by a telescope in Hawaii.
Its name is Hawaiian for 'a messenger from afar arriving first'.
2025.7. 세 번째 별 사이 손님. 이번엔 꼬리 달린 혜성이라고 읽었: July 2025. The third visitor from between the stars. Read that this one is a comet with a tail.
A comet from another star! It is so fast.
오우무아무아는 2017년 10월 19일 하와이의 판스타스 망원경이 찾은,: ʻOumuamua, found on 19 October 2017 by the Pan-STARRS telescope in Hawaii, is the first body known to have come from outside the solar system. Robert Weryk, an astronomer from Canada, found it as a fast-moving dot in the telescope's pictures. By then it had already been nearest the Sun, on 9 September, had passed Earth too, and was on its way out. Its name means "a messenger from afar arriving first" in Hawaiian. It was first classed as a comet, then as an asteroid, and in the end a new class of interstellar objects was made, and it got the first number, "1I". It came in at 26 km/s on a path the Sun could not hold (a hyperbola), and left again.
밝기가 8시간쯤마다 열 배쯤 오르내려, 길쭉한 막대나 납작한 접시 모양으: Its brightness rose and fell about tenfold every 8 hours or so, so it is thought to be shaped like a long rod or a flat plate. It is roughly 100 to 400 m long, and slightly reddish. No tail was seen, yet it sped away a little faster than the Sun's gravity alone can explain, which puzzled people for a long time. Many think unseen hydrogen or nitrogen ice slowly escaping gave it a push; one astronomer claimed it was a light sail made by aliens, but few accept that. Since the Hubble Space Telescope last saw it in January 2018, it has been too far and too faint for anyone to see. In the game, this visitor's path in and out is replayed every 3 years of game time.
3I/아틀라스는 2025년 7월 1일 칠레에 있는 아틀라스 망원경이 찾았: 3I/ATLAS was found on 1 July 2025 by the ATLAS telescope in Chile. ATLAS is a set of telescopes that sweep the sky every night to find, in good time, anything that might hit Earth. After it was found, a search of older pictures showed it had already been caught from mid-June. It is the third visitor from between the stars to be found, after ʻOumuamua (2017) and Comet Borisov (2019). It is a comet that throws out ice and dust, and it came in at 58 km/s, the fastest visitor seen so far. It came from the direction of Sagittarius, where the centre of our galaxy lies, and passed through on a path tilted only about 5 degrees from the plane of the planets, going the opposite way round to them. The James Webb Space Telescope saw unusually much carbon dioxide gas around it.
2025년 10월 3일 화성 곁을 약 2,900만km 거리로 지나, 화성: On 3 October 2025 it passed Mars about 29 million km away, and the Mars orbiters took pictures. On 29 October it was nearest the Sun, just inside the orbit of Mars, but seen from Earth it was then hidden behind the Sun, so telescopes on the ground could not see it. On 19 December it came within about 270 million km of Earth and then drew away, and in March 2026 it passed Jupiter. Its nucleus is reckoned to be between 0.4 km and 5.6 km across. It may come from a group of stars older than the solar system, and it may be more than 7 billion years old. In the game, this visitor's path is replayed every 3 years of game time.
오우무아무아라는 이름은 어느 말에서 왔나?: Which language does the name ʻOumuamua come from?
2017년 10월 유럽 남천 천문대의 VLT 등 여러 망원경 사진을 겹친: ʻOumuamua (the dot in the blue circle) in pictures from the VLT and other telescopes stacked together, October 2017. The dotted lines are stars, smeared as the telescopes followed the visitor.
2025년 11월 30일 허블 우주망원경이 찍은 3I/아틀라스. 가운데: 3I/ATLAS taken by the Hubble Space Telescope on 30 November 2025, its nucleus in the middle wrapped in gas and dust.
다른 별에서 온 손님을 만났구나. 할머니 평생에 그런 날이 올 줄 몰랐다: You met a guest from another star. I never thought such a day would come in my life.
A comet from between the stars. Its tail must carry dust of far-off stars.
That guest again. Look your fill before it goes far away.
아틀라스를 또 찍었구나. 이번엔 꼬리가 어땠니?: ATLAS again. How was its tail this time?
별 사이에서 온 손님 둘, 오우무아무아와 3I/아틀라스 혜성이 게임 시간: Two visitors from between the stars, ʻOumuamua and Comet 3I/ATLAS, pass the Sun once every three game years.
The European star-mapping satellite that measured the places and distances of 1.8 billion objects in the sky. Its work ended in March 2025; it was moved onto a path away from Earth and switched off.
금속 소행성 프시케로 가는 미국 탐사선입니다. 푸른 빛을 내는 이온 엔진: An American probe on its way to the metal asteroid Psyche. It flies on an ion engine that glows blue, and arrives in August 2029.
가이아는 유럽우주국이 2013년 12월 19일 남아메리카 프랑스령 기아나: Gaia is a star-mapping satellite that ESA launched from French Guiana in South America on 19 December 2013. Its name comes from the earth goddess of Greek myth; it began as an English acronym, and the name stayed even after the design changed. Circling the L2 point, 1.5 million km from Earth on the side away from the Sun, it measured for 11 years the positions, distances and motions of more than 1.8 billion objects, stars of our galaxy above all. Even so, that is only about 1% of the stars in our galaxy. Its camera has about a billion pixels, the largest camera ever put in space. It is the most precise map of the sky ever made, with more than ten thousand times as many stars as the roughly 120,000 measured by the earlier Hipparcos satellite, launched in 1989.
지름 10m의 둥근 햇빛 가리개가 늘 태양을 가리고, 그 그늘에서 망원경: A round sunshade 10 m across always blocked the Sun, and in its shadow two telescopes slowly swept the sky. It measured distances by parallax, the way a star seems to shift back and forth a little over a year, with a precision like measuring the width of a hair from 1,000 km away. Tracing the motions of stars backwards, it showed that about 10 billion years ago our galaxy swallowed a small galaxy. In 2024, about 2,000 light years from Earth, it found a black hole as heavy as 33 Suns just from the way it sways its companion star. It also measured anew the orbits of hundreds of thousands of asteroids. It ended its mission on 27 March 2025 and was switched off after being moved onto a path away from Earth. New catalogues made from the data it gathered will keep coming out for some years yet.
프시케는 미국항공우주국이 2023년 10월 13일 미국 케네디 우주센터에: Psyche is an asteroid spacecraft that NASA launched on a Falcon Heavy rocket from Kennedy Space Center in the United States on 13 October 2023. It was meant to leave in 2022, but testing of its flight software ran late and it was put off by more than a year. It is going to the asteroid 16 Psyche between Mars and Jupiter, which is rich in iron and nickel and may be the bared metal core of an old planet. 16 Psyche was the sixteenth asteroid found, by Annibale de Gasparis of Naples, Italy, in 1852; it is about 280 km on its long side and is named after the Greek goddess of the soul. We cannot see Earth's metal core, so this is a chance to look inside one. It is the first spacecraft to visit a body made of metal.
태양 전지판에서 얻은 전기로 크세논 기체를 쏘는 이온 엔진으로 날며, 그: It flies by an ion engine that uses electricity from its solar panels to shoot out xenon gas, and the glow is blue. The push is very weak, about like holding three coins in your palm, but it pushes without rest for months on end and builds up great speed. It passed Mars in May 2026 to gain speed, and it is due to reach Psyche in August 2029 and circle it for more than two years. If Psyche keeps a trace of a magnetic field, that would show it was once a molten metal core, so the craft carries a magnetometer at the end of a long boom. It also carries a test device that exchanges data with Earth by laser, and in December 2023 it sent back a cat video from 31 million km away. It is a 15-second clip of Taters, a lab worker's tabby cat, chasing a laser dot.
가이아가 별까지의 거리를 잰 방법은?: How did Gaia measure the distances to stars?
프시케가 레이저로 보내 온 동영상의 주인공은?: Who starred in the video Psyche sent back by laser?
2013년 파리 에어쇼에 전시된 가이아 모형. 둥글게 펼친 판이 햇빛 가: A model of Gaia shown at the Paris Air Show in 2013. The round spread is the sunshield; the drum in the middle holds the two telescopes.
Psyche in May 2022, its wings folded, being readied for launch.
탐사선 둘이 생겼습니다. 일을 마친 별 지도 위성 가이아와, 금속 소행성: Two more craft: Gaia, the star-mapping satellite now retired, and Psyche, on its way to a metal asteroid.
달 뒤쪽(지구 반대편)에서 달 표면 6,200km 안을 지나기: Pass within 6,200 km of the Moon's surface on its far side, away from Earth
1959년 10월 7일 소련의 루나 3호가 달 뒤쪽을 돌며, 사람이 한: On 7 October 1959 the Soviet probe Luna 3 swung round behind the Moon and took the first pictures of its far side, which no one had ever seen.
지구 경주의 첨성대(북위 35.8도, 동경 129.2도) 40km 안에: Land within 40 km of Cheomseongdae in Gyeongju on Earth (35.8° N, 129.2° E)
신라 선덕여왕 때 경주에 세운 돌탑입니다. 동아시아에서 가장 오래된 천문: A stone tower built in Gyeongju in the time of Queen Seondeok of Silla. It is counted the oldest observatory in East Asia; it stands 9.17 m tall.
지구 영국의 스톤헨지(북위 51.2도, 서경 1.8도) 40km 안에 내: Land within 40 km of Stonehenge in England on Earth (51.2° N, 1.8° W)
영국 솔즈베리 평원에 큰 돌을 둥글게 세운 유적입니다. 하짓날 해가 돌: A ring of great standing stones on Salisbury Plain in England, set so that the Sun rises between them on midsummer morning.
지구 푸에르토리코의 아레시보 전파망원경(북위 18.3도, 서경 66.8도: Land within 40 km of the Arecibo Telescope in Puerto Rico on Earth (18.3° N, 66.8° W)
On 16 November 1974 a radio letter to other worlds was sent from here. The dish, 305 m across, collapsed in 2020.
루나 3호는 1959년 10월 4일 소련이 쏘아 올렸습니다. 달의 남극: Luna 3 was launched by the Soviet Union on 4 October 1959. It passed 6,200 km over the Moon's south polar region and swung round behind it, and on 7 October took 29 pictures in 40 minutes from about 65,000 km away. The film was developed and dried inside the craft, then read line by line like television and sent to Earth. The far side of the Moon, unlike the near side, had hardly any dark seas.
루나 3호가 1959년 10월 7일 찍어 보낸 달 뒷면. 흐릿하고 줄무늬: The far side of the Moon as Luna 3 sent it on 7 October 1959. Blurred and streaked, it is still the first look people ever had at the back of the Moon. One of the dark patches is the "Sea of Moscow".
첨성대는 경상북도 경주에 있는 신라의 천문대입니다. 선덕여왕(재위 632: Cheomseongdae is an observatory of the Silla kingdom in Gyeongju, North Gyeongsang Province. The Samguk Yusa records that it was built under Queen Seondeok (reigned 632 to 647). About 362 dressed granite stones are laid in 27 courses to a height of 9.17 m. People are thought to have climbed in by a ladder through the square window facing south halfway up. It became a National Treasure in 1962.
경주 첨성대. 아래가 넓고 위로 갈수록 좁아지는 병 모양의 돌탑이고, 가: Cheomseongdae in Gyeongju: a bottle-shaped stone tower, wide at the foot and narrowing upward, with a square window facing south halfway up. At the top, stones are laid in the shape of the character 井 (a well).
스톤헨지는 영국 잉글랜드 남부 솔즈베리 평원에 있는 돌 유적입니다. 기원: Stonehenge is a stone monument on Salisbury Plain in southern England. Work began around 3000 BC with a round ditch and bank, and the great stones were raised around 2500 BC. Sarsen stones up to 7 m tall and 25 tonnes were set in a ring with lintels laid across their tops. It is lined up with sunrise at midsummer and sunset at midwinter. It became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986.
하짓날 아침 스톤헨지의 돌 너머로 해가 떠오르는 모습. 해마다 이날이면: Sunrise over the stones of Stonehenge on midsummer morning. Thousands gather every year to watch it.
아레시보 전파망원경은 카리브해의 섬 푸에르토리코의 산골짜기 움푹한 땅에: The Arecibo Telescope was a dish 305 m across laid in a hollow among the hills of Puerto Rico, an island in the Caribbean. It opened in 1963 and for 53 years was the largest single-dish radio telescope in the world. On 16 November 1974 it sent the "Arecibo message", 1,679 bits holding numbers, the shape of a person and more, toward the star cluster M13, 25,000 light years away. On 1 December 2020 the cables holding its receiver snapped and the dish collapsed.
무너지기 전의 아레시보 전파망원경. 골짜기에 깐 지름 305m 접시 위로: The Arecibo Telescope before it fell: above the 305 m dish laid in the valley hangs the 900-tonne receiver, slung on cables from three towers.
보낸 사진 가운데 17장이 지구에 닿았고, 그 안에 달 뒷면의 70%쯤이: Seventeen of the pictures reached Earth, and between them they showed about 70% of the far side. The Soviet Union gave the places found on the far side names such as the "Sea of Moscow" and "Tsiolkovsky crater", and in 1960 used these pictures to publish the first atlas of the far side of the Moon. Luna 3 was also the first spacecraft to use a figure-of-eight path, bent by the Moon's gravity back towards Earth. Luna 3 fell silent afterwards, and in 1960 it entered Earth's air and burned up. The first people to see the far side with their own eyes were the three astronauts of Apollo 8, in December 1968. In January 2019 China's Chang'e 4 became the first to land on the far side.
돌의 수 362개는 1년의 날수와, 27단은 선덕여왕이 신라의 27대 임: It is said that the 362 stones match the days of a year, and the 27 courses Queen Seondeok being the 27th ruler of Silla. There are 12 courses below the window and 12 above it, which some read as the twelve months and the 24 seasonal divisions of the year. Whether it was really a place for watching the stars or an altar to the sky is still argued. Inside, it is filled with earth and stones up to the window, so people probably climbed in through the window and then went up another ladder inside to the top. It is counted the oldest surviving observatory in East Asia. It has stood through earthquakes for more than 1,300 years, and did not fall even in the magnitude 5.8 earthquake at Gyeongju in September 2016.
안쪽의 작은 \"블루스톤\"들은 250km 넘게 떨어진 웨일스의 프레셀리: The smaller "bluestones" inside were brought from the Preseli Hills in Wales, more than 250 km away. The "Altar Stone", some 6 tonnes, lying in the very middle, was shown in 2024 to have come from north-east Scotland, more than 700 km away. The big sarsen stones were brought from about 25 km to the north. How they were moved before there were wheels is not yet fully known; many think they were dragged on wooden sledges. At nearby Durrington Walls, a village site has been found where the builders gathered to feast. Human bones are buried there too, so it was probably a place both to honour the Sun and to remember the dead.
1965년에는 이곳의 레이더로 수성이 59일에 한 번 돈다는 것을 처음: In 1965 its radar first showed that Mercury turns once every 59 days. In 1974 Hulse and Taylor found here two neutron stars circling each other (a binary pulsar), and won the 1993 Nobel Prize in Physics for it. In 1992 Aleksander Wolszczan used the telescope to find planets going round a pulsar: the first planets confirmed outside the solar system. It also lit up asteroids passing near Earth with radar to map their shapes. It appears in the films "GoldenEye" and "Contact". It was badly damaged by Hurricane Maria in 2017, and after the collapse the United States chose not to rebuild the telescope but to use the site for science education.

명왕성보다 무거운 왜행성입니다. 이것이 발견되어 2006년 명왕성이 행성: A dwarf planet heavier than Pluto. Its discovery is why Pluto stopped being a planet in 2006.
럭비공처럼 길쭉한 왜행성입니다. 4시간에 한 바퀴 돌고, 가는 고리를 둘: A dwarf planet stretched like a rugby ball. It spins once in four hours and wears a thin ring.
부활절 무렵 발견된 왜행성입니다. 이스터섬 사람들이 섬기던 창조의 신 이: A dwarf planet found around Easter, named after the creator god of the people of Easter Island.
태양에서 가장 멀리 가는 천체 가운데 하나입니다. 한 바퀴에 1만 1천: One of the bodies that travel farthest from the Sun. One trip round takes over 11,000 years.
눈사람처럼 두 덩이가 붙은 천체입니다. 2019년 1월 1일 뉴허라이즌스: Two lumps stuck together like a snowman. New Horizons flew past it on 1 January 2019.
스펀지처럼 구멍이 숭숭 뚫린 토성의 위성입니다. 정해진 하루 없이 제멋대: A moon of Saturn riddled with holes like a sponge. It tumbles about with no steady day.
토성을 거꾸로 도는 먼 위성입니다. 숯처럼 검고, 카이퍼대에서 붙잡혀 온: A far-out moon that goes round Saturn backwards. Dark as charcoal, it is thought to be a captive from the Kuiper belt.
해왕성의 둘째로 큰 위성입니다. 어둡고 해왕성에 가까워 보이저 2호가 가: Neptune's second-largest moon. Dark and close to Neptune, it was not found until Voyager 2 got there.
목성 앞 60도에서 함께 도는 트로이 소행성입니다. 2027년 8월 루시: A Trojan asteroid that goes round 60 degrees ahead of Jupiter. Lucy will fly past it in August 2027.
거의 같은 크기의 둘이 서로 도는 쌍소행성입니다. 2033년 루시가 마지: A binary asteroid: two of almost the same size going round each other. Lucy will visit them last, in 2033.
파트로클로스와 짝을 이룬 소행성입니다. 둘은 680km 떨어져 4.3일에: The asteroid paired with Patroclus. The two, 680 km apart, go round each other once in 4.3 days.
White as a snowfield. It's dazzling.

Its partner Menoetius hangs in the sky.

Heavier than Pluto! And so white.
2017.10. 하우메아에도 고리가 있다고 신문에서 읽었다. 명왕성 너머: Oct 2017. Read in the paper that Haumea has a ring. A ring, out past Pluto.
Long like an egg! It has a ring too.
2008.7. 넷째 왜행성의 이름이 마케마케로 정해졌다고 신문에서 읽었다: July 2008. Read in the paper that the fourth dwarf planet was named Makemake.
이름이 노래 같아. 마케마케!: Its name sounds like a song. Makemake!
Mar 2004. Read in the paper they found a red world at the edge of the solar system. Named Sedna.
So red! One of the reddest in the solar system.
2019.1.1. 새해 첫날 뉴허라이즌스가 먼 눈사람을 찍었다고 신문에서: 1 Jan 2019. Read in the paper that on New Year's Day New Horizons photographed a far-off snowman.
2005.9. 카시니가 찍은 히페리온 사진을 신문에서 봤다. 꼭 스펀지: Sept 2005. Saw Cassini's picture of Hyperion in the paper. Just like a sponge.
1899년 피커링이 사진으로 찾았다고 책에서 읽었다. 사진으로 찾은 첫: Read in a book that Pickering found it on a photograph in 1899. The first moon found that way.
It goes round Saturn backwards! Black as coal.
1989.8. 보이저 2호가 해왕성에서 새 위성 여섯을 찾았다고 신문에서: Aug 1989. Read in the paper that Voyager 2 found six new moons at Neptune.
2021.10. 루시 탐사선이 목성의 트로이 소행성들로 떠났다고 신문에서: Oct 2021. Read in the paper that the Lucy probe set off for Jupiter's Trojan asteroids.
Read in a book that the Trojan asteroid Patroclus turned out in 2001 to be two.
2006년 파트로클로스의 짝에 아버지 이름 메노이티오스를 붙였다고 읽었다: Read that in 2006 Patroclus's partner was given his father's name, Menoetius.
It looks just like its partner.
에리스는 지름 약 2,326km로 명왕성보다 조금 작지만 27% 더 무거: Eris is a dwarf planet about 2,326 km across, a little smaller than Pluto but 27% heavier. It is the heaviest dwarf planet known. Mike Brown, Chad Trujillo and David Rabinowitz found it in January 2005 in pictures taken at Palomar Observatory in the United States. Those pictures had been taken in October 2003, but it was so far away and moved so slowly that it was found only when they were looked over again more than a year later. Before it got its proper name it went by the nickname "Xena", after the heroine of a television series. For a time it was called "the tenth planet"; this led the International Astronomical Union to define a planet anew in August 2006, and it became a dwarf planet together with Pluto.
이름은 그리스 신화에서 다툼과 불화의 여신에서 왔고, 위성 디스노미아는: Its name comes from the Greek goddess of strife and discord, and its moon Dysnomia is named after her daughter, the goddess of lawlessness. It is a fitting name for a body that stirred up a quarrel over what a planet is. It goes round the Sun once in 559 years on a long orbit, 38 AU away at its nearest and 98 AU at its farthest; it is near its farthest now, about 96 AU out. Sunlight takes about 13 hours to get there, and its orbit is tilted as much as 44 degrees from the plane of the planets. Its surface is covered with frozen methane frost that reflects 96% of the sunlight, and it is colder than 220 degrees below zero. When it comes near the Sun again in the 2250s, the frost may thaw into a thin atmosphere. It and its moon keep one face to each other, and it turns once in 15.8 days.
하우메아는 긴 쪽이 약 2,300km, 짧은 쪽이 약 1,000km인 럭: Haumea is a dwarf planet shaped like a rugby ball, about 2,300 km long and about 1,000 km at its shortest. Its long side is about twice the length of the Korean peninsula from north to south. It spins once every 3 hours 55 minutes, faster than any other known body more than 100 km across. Its fast spin is thought to have stretched it out. Long, long ago a great collision set it spinning this fast, and the ice fragments knocked off then still go round in a group on orbits like Haumea's. It was the first such family of bodies sharing one path to be found beyond Neptune. Its surface is white with crystalline water ice, with one dark red patch.
2004년 말 미국 마이크 브라운의 팀과 2005년 스페인 호세 루이스: Mike Brown's team in the United States, at the end of 2004, and José Luis Ortiz's team in Spain, in 2005, found it separately, and there was a dispute over who came first. Ortiz's team announced it first, but Brown's team pointed to signs that its observing records had been looked at; in the end the International Astronomical Union listed the place of discovery as the observatory in Spain and took the name Brown's team proposed. Its moons were found with the Keck telescope on Mauna Kea in Hawaii, so its name comes from the Hawaiian goddess of childbirth, and its moons Hiʻiaka and Namaka are named after her daughters. In 2017, watching from many places as Haumea passed in front of a star, astronomers found a ring about 2,287 km from its centre: the first ring found round a body beyond Neptune. It goes round the Sun once in 283 years.
마케마케는 지름 약 1,430km의 왜행성으로, 명왕성의 5분의 3쯤 되: Makemake is a dwarf planet about 1,430 km across, some three fifths the size of Pluto. It is the brightest body beyond Neptune after Pluto, so a large amateur telescope can find it as a faint dot. Mike Brown's team found it on 31 March 2005 in pictures taken at Palomar Observatory in California, a few days after Easter, so at first it went by the nickname "Easterbunny". It was then named after the creator god of the Rapa Nui people of Easter Island. Makemake was also the god of the yearly "birdman" contest, won by whoever first brought back a sea bird's egg. In July 2008 it became the fourth dwarf planet, after Ceres, Pluto and Eris.
표면은 메탄과 에탄이 얼어붙어 붉은 기운이 도는 밝은 색입니다. 메탄 얼: Its surface, of frozen methane and ethane, is bright with a reddish cast. Some of the methane ice grains are nearly 1 cm across, more like hail than snow. The surface is about 240 degrees below zero. When it passed in front of a star in 2011, the starlight went out and came back in an instant, so astronomers knew it has almost no atmosphere. Yet in 2025 the James Webb Space Telescope found methane gas above it: there may be a very thin atmosphere, or gas puffing out of the ground. In 2016 the Hubble Space Telescope found a little moon about 175 km across, as dark as charcoal, which people call MK2. No spacecraft has been there yet. It goes round the Sun once in 306 years, and its day is 22.8 hours.
세드나는 지름 약 1,000km의 붉은 천체로, 해왕성 바깥 아주 먼 곳: Sedna is a red body about 1,000 km across that goes round very far beyond Neptune. Mike Brown, Chad Trujillo and David Rabinowitz found it on 14 November 2003 in pictures taken at Palomar Observatory in the United States; at the time it was the farthest known body in the solar system. It is named after the Inuit goddess of the sea, who lives at the bottom of the cold ocean. In the story, Sedna's cut-off fingers became the seals and whales. It is one of the reddest bodies in the solar system, and many think it is large enough to be a dwarf planet. In 2023 the James Webb Space Telescope found ices such as ethane and acetylene on its surface.
태양에 가장 가까울 때도 76AU로 해왕성보다 두 배 넘게 멀고, 가장: Even at its nearest to the Sun it is 76 AU away, more than twice as far as Neptune, and at its farthest it goes out to about 940 AU. One trip round takes about 11,000 years: the last time it was here, the last ice age on Earth was coming to an end. From its farthest point the Sun would look like a single very bright star. Neptune's pull does not reach that far, so some think another star that passed close to the Sun long ago drew it out onto so long an orbit. Seeing that the orbits of far bodies like Sedna are bunched to one side, some have suggested there may be a ninth planet not yet seen. It will be nearest the Sun in 2076; now it is about 83 AU away.
아로코스는 길이 약 36km의 작은 천체로, 서울시의 동서 길이와 비슷합: Arrokoth is a small body about 36 km long, about the width of Seoul from east to west. It goes round the Sun once in 298 years in the Kuiper belt, beyond Neptune. Marc Buie's team found it in June 2014 with the Hubble Space Telescope, in a search for somewhere for New Horizons to visit. In 2017, 24 telescopes were set out across the plains of Argentina to watch it pass in front of a star, and from that it was guessed that it might be two lumps stuck together. At first it was nicknamed Ultima Thule, Latin for "beyond the known world". In 2019 it got its present name, which means "sky" in the language of the Powhatan, a Native American people, given with the consent of their elders.
2019년 1월 1일 뉴허라이즌스가 약 3,500km 곁을 지나며 찍었습: On 1 January 2019 New Horizons flew past about 3,500 km away and photographed it. It was then about 6.6 billion km from Earth, the farthest body a spacecraft has examined close up in passing. The craft sends data so slowly that it took nearly two years for all the pictures and readings to reach Earth. It is shaped like a snowman, two flat lumps that drew slowly together and touched gently; the larger is called Wenu and the smaller Weeyo. With only a few craters, it keeps almost unchanged the look of the time when the solar system formed. Its red colour is organic matter in the ice, scorched by sunlight over ages, and methanol ice was found on its surface too. New Horizons is still flying outward from the solar system.
히페리온은 크기가 약 360km × 266km × 205km인 감자 모양: Hyperion is a potato-shaped moon of Saturn about 360 km × 266 km × 205 km. Its long side is a little longer than the straight-line distance from Seoul to Busan (about 325 km). William Bond and his son George in the United States and William Lassell in Britain found it separately in 1848; it was the first moon found that is not round. Its name comes from the Titan of light in Greek myth, father of Helios, the god of the Sun. Being long in shape and tugged by Titan, it tumbles about with no steady axis, so its day has no fixed length. While Titan goes round Saturn four times, Hyperion goes round exactly three, so it is tugged again and again at the same places.
2005년 9월 카시니가 약 500km 곁을 지나며 찍은 사진에서, 스펀: In September 2005 Cassini flew past about 500 km away, and its pictures showed a surface packed with deep pits, like a sponge. It is so light that more than 40% of its inside is empty space, so when something hits it the ground is mostly pressed in and little is thrown out, and it is thought that is why such pits remain. It is much lighter than water: if there were a tub of water big enough to hold Hyperion, it would float. Dark material lies pooled at the bottoms of the pits. On that pass Cassini was hit by a beam of electrons streaming off Hyperion's surface, which sunlight and the particles round Saturn had charged with static to about minus 200 volts. It was the first time a charged surface was confirmed on any body other than the Moon. It goes round Saturn once in 21 days.
포에베는 지름 약 213km의 토성 위성으로, 서울에서 대구까지 직선거리: Phoebe is a moon of Saturn about 213 km across, a little less than the straight-line distance from Seoul to Daegu (about 240 km). It goes round about 13 million km from Saturn, some 34 times the distance from Earth to the Moon, in the opposite direction to the other large moons. William Pickering of the United States found it on photographic plates taken at an observatory in Peru in August 1898 and announced it in 1899; it was the first moon found by photography. Its name comes from the Titaness Phoebe of Greek myth, grandmother of Artemis, goddess of the Moon. Black as charcoal and covered in craters, it is thought to be a body from the Kuiper belt that Saturn captured.
2004년 6월 11일 카시니가 토성에 닿기 전 약 2,000km 곁을: On 11 June 2004, before reaching Saturn, Cassini flew past about 2,000 km away and photographed it close up for the first time. Bright ice showed beneath the dark topsoil in crater walls, revealing an icy body covered with dark dust. Some think there are signs that long ago its inside warmed up and it was nearly round. In 2009 the Spitzer Space Telescope found a very faint ring that wraps widely round Saturn along Phoebe's orbit. The ring is so big that a billion Earths could fit in it, the largest ring in the solar system. Dust spreading from this ring is thought to have painted one side of Iapetus dark. It goes round Saturn once in 545 days, and its day is 9 hours 16 minutes.
프로테우스는 지름 약 420km의 해왕성 위성으로, 트리톤 다음으로 큽니: Proteus is a moon of Neptune about 420 km across, the second largest after Triton. It was found in pictures taken by Voyager 2 as it drew near Neptune in June 1989. It reflects only about 10% of the sunlight, and it stays close to bright Neptune, so until then it could not be seen from the ground. Nereid, which is smaller, had been found with a telescope back in 1949, yet the bigger Proteus showed itself only 40 years later. It goes round about three times closer to Neptune than Triton does, and today the Hubble Space Telescope can see it as a faint dot.
중력이 몸을 둥글게 다듬을 수 있는 크기에 거의 이르렀지만, 아직 상자처: It is nearly large enough for gravity to pull it round, but it is still angular, like a box. On one side is a large crater, Pharos, about 250 km across. A crater more than half the body's width: hit a little harder, it would have been shattered. In 2013 Mark Showalter found a tiny moon, Hippocamp, about 34 km across, in old Hubble Space Telescope pictures, and it is thought it may be a chip knocked off Proteus in that very impact. Its name comes from the sea god of Greek myth who changes his shape at will. It goes round about 93,000 km above Neptune's clouds once in 27 hours, always showing Neptune the same face.
에우리바테스는 지름 약 64km의 소행성으로, 목성과 같은 궤도를 목성보: Eurybates is an asteroid about 64 km across, a Trojan asteroid that shares Jupiter's orbit, 60 degrees ahead of Jupiter. At this place, where the pulls of the Sun and Jupiter balance, and at the place 60 degrees behind, more than 10,000 asteroids are gathered. The French mathematician Joseph-Louis Lagrange found such places first by calculation in 1772, and the first asteroid was actually found there only 134 years later, in 1906. Those in the leading group are named after Greek heroes of the Trojan War, and those in the trailing group after Trojan heroes. Eurybates is the largest piece of a rare group among the Trojans: the fragments of one body broken in a great collision.
1973년 네덜란드와 미국의 천문학자들이 팔로마 천문대의 사진에서 찾았고: Astronomers from the Netherlands and the United States found it in 1973 in pictures taken at Palomar Observatory, and it was named after the herald who served Odysseus in the Trojan War. In 2020 Hubble Space Telescope pictures confirmed a tiny moon about 1 km across, Queta. Queta is the nickname of Enriqueta Basilio, who at the 1968 Mexico City Olympics became the first woman to light the Olympic cauldron. She was chosen because she carried the flame as a herald carries news, and from then on small Trojan asteroids may also be named after Olympic athletes. The Lucy spacecraft is due to fly past in August 2027. As it is a piece of a great collision, Lucy may get to see its inside laid bare. It turns once in 8.7 hours.
파트로클로스는 지름 약 113km의 소행성으로, 제주도 동서 길이(약 7: Patroclus is an asteroid about 113 km across, about one and a half times the width of Jeju Island from east to west (about 73 km). It is paired with Menoetius, almost the same size, and the two go round each other. It is a Trojan asteroid that shares Jupiter's orbit, 60 degrees behind Jupiter. August Kopff found it at Heidelberg in Germany in October 1906, the second Trojan asteroid ever found, after Achilles that February. In 2001 the Gemini telescope in Hawaii showed it has a partner. Seen from the ground the two are so close together that for a long time they looked like one.
뒤쪽 무리에는 보통 트로이 편 영웅의 이름을 붙이지만, 이 둘은 그리스: The trailing group is usually named after Trojan heroes, but these two were named after Patroclus, friend of the Greek hero Achilles, and his father. That is because they were named before the rule was set. The two are about 680 km apart, about twice the straight-line distance from Seoul to Busan, and go round each other once in 4.3 days, always facing each other with the same side. Every few years comes a season when, seen from Earth, the two take turns hiding each other; around 2018 astronomers watched such a season to measure their sizes and shapes. The Lucy spacecraft is due to visit them last, in March 2033. In that one meeting Lucy will look at two bodies at once.
메노이티오스는 지름 약 104km의 소행성으로, 파트로클로스와 거의 같은: Menoetius is an asteroid about 104 km across, Patroclus's partner of almost the same size. It was found in 2001 with the Gemini telescope on Mauna Kea in Hawaii, and in 2006 it was named after Menoetius, the father of Patroclus in Greek myth. When a device that corrects the shimmer of the air gathered the starlight sharply, a dot that had looked single split into two. It was the first time a partner was found for a Trojan asteroid. The Menoetius of myth was also one of the heroes who sailed on the Argo in search of the Golden Fleece.
둘의 무게 중심은 그 사이 빈 곳에 있어서, 큰 쪽이 작은 쪽을 거느리는: The centre of mass of the two lies in the empty space between them, so the larger does not lead the smaller: the two go round together. Both are a little lighter than water and seem to contain ice, so some think they formed far out when the solar system was young and were drawn into Jupiter's orbit. Such pairs of two similar-sized bodies are common in the Kuiper belt beyond Neptune, which supports that idea. It means the pair held together and survived even when the planets moved and the solar system was badly shaken up. They go round once in 4.3 days, each keeping the same face to the other. When Lucy visits in 2033, we will see what they look like close up for the first time.

하우메아를 그린 그림. 2017년에 잰 크기와 고리를 바탕으로 그렸습니다: A drawing of Haumea, based on its size and ring as measured in 2017. No close-up photograph of it exists yet.
2015년 4월 허블 우주망원경이 찍은 마케마케. 밝은 빛 바로 위에 아: Makemake as seen by the Hubble Space Telescope in April 2015. A very faint moon hides just above the bright light.
세드나의 땅에서 본 한낮의 하늘을 상상해 그린 그림. 태양은 밝은 별 하: An artist's idea of noon on Sedna: the Sun is no bigger than a bright star. In real photographs Sedna is only a dot.
2019년 1월 1일 뉴허라이즌스가 곁을 지나며 찍은 아로코스. 흑백 사: Arrokoth as New Horizons saw it flying past on 1 January 2019, colour added to the black-and-white pictures.
2005년 9월 카시니가 찍은 히페리온. 실제 색에 가깝게 맞춘 사진입니: Hyperion taken by Cassini in September 2005, processed to be close to its true colour.
2004년 6월 카시니가 토성에 닿기 전에 찍은 포에베. 충돌구가 가득합: Phoebe, taken by Cassini in June 2004 before it reached Saturn. It is covered in craters.
1989년 8월 보이저 2호가 찍은 프로테우스. 둥글지 않은 각진 모양이: Proteus taken by Voyager 2 in August 1989, showing its angular, not quite round shape.
2020년 1월 허블 우주망원경이 찍은 에우리바테스. 동그라미 안에 작은: Eurybates taken by the Hubble Space Telescope in January 2020. Its tiny moon Queta is in the circle.
2018년 2월 허블 우주망원경이 찍은 파트로클로스와 메노이티오스. 너무: Patroclus and Menoetius taken by the Hubble Space Telescope in February 2018. So far away, they look like two dots stuck together.
파트로클로스(왼쪽)와 메노이티오스(오른쪽)를 그린 그림. 루시가 2033: A drawing of Patroclus (left) and Menoetius (right). Lucy is due to photograph the real pair in 2033.

왜행성 에리스·하우메아·마케마케, 세드나, 아로코스, 위성 셋, 트로이: New: the dwarf planets Eris, Haumea and Makemake, Sedna, Arrokoth, three moons and three Trojan asteroids.
임무를 마친 탐사선 셋의 기념 모형이 생겼습니다. 혜성의 로제타, 목성의: Memorials to three craft whose missions are over: Rosetta at its comet, Galileo at Jupiter and MESSENGER at Mercury.
유럽의 혜성 탐사선입니다. 2014년부터 2년 동안 이 혜성 곁을 돌며: Europe's comet probe. From 2014 it went round this comet for two years and sent the lander Philae down to it, and on 30 September 2016 it ended its mission by coming down on the comet. What is here is in memory of it.
목성 둘레를 처음 돈 미국 탐사선입니다. 목성의 공기 속으로 탐사구를 내: An American probe, the first to go round Jupiter. It sent a probe down into Jupiter's air, went round Jupiter 35 times in 8 years, and in 2003 ended its mission by plunging into Jupiter. What is here is in memory of it.
수성 둘레를 처음 돈 미국 탐사선입니다. 4년 동안 수성 전체의 지도를: An American probe, the first to go round Mercury. In four years it mapped the whole of Mercury, and on 30 April 2015 it ended its mission by falling onto it. What is here is in memory of it.
독일 다름슈타트의 유럽우주국 관제 센터에 놓인, 로제타와 똑같이 만든 시: A test model built just like Rosetta, at the European Space Agency's control centre in Darmstadt, Germany. The big dish in front is its antenna.
1989년 발사 전, 조립을 마친 갈릴레오. 맨 위에 접혀 있는 것이 우: Galileo, fully assembled, before its launch in 1989. The folded thing at the very top is the umbrella-shaped antenna.
1990년대 후반 갈릴레오가 찍은 사진을 2014년에 다시 이어 붙인 유: Europa, from pictures Galileo took in the late 1990s, pieced together anew in 2014. Its shell of ice is covered in cracks.
2004년 발사 전, 조립 중인 메신저. 양옆에 태양 전지판이 달려 있습: MESSENGER being put together before its launch in 2004, a solar panel on each side.
2011년 3월 29일 수성 궤도에서 처음 찍은 사진(왼쪽)과, 2015: The first picture taken from orbit round Mercury, on 29 March 2011 (left), and the last, taken on 30 April 2015 just before it fell (right).
로제타가 마지막에 혜성에 내려앉은 빠르기는?: How fast was Rosetta going when it came down on the comet at the end?
갈릴레오가 끝내 다 펴지 못한 것은?: What did Galileo never manage to open fully?
메신저의 햇빛 가리개는 무엇으로 만들었나?: What was MESSENGER's sunshade made of?
로제타는 유럽우주국이 2004년 3월 2일 남아메리카 프랑스령 기아나에서: Rosetta is a comet spacecraft that ESA launched on an Ariane 5 rocket from French Guiana in South America on 2 March 2004. It was meant to go to another comet, but when a rocket accident put off its launch by more than a year, its destination was changed to Comet Churyumov-Gerasimenko. With its solar panels spread out it is 32 m wide, longer than a tennis court. It swung past Earth three times and Mars once to gain speed, flew for 10 years, and reached the comet on 6 August 2014. It was the first spacecraft to go round a comet, and on 12 November that year it set the lander Philae down on a comet, a first.
가는 길인 2008년과 2010년에는 소행성 슈테인스와 루테티아를 지나며: On the way, in 2008 and 2010, it flew past the asteroids Šteins and Lutetia and photographed them. For two years it watched from close by as the comet threw out gas and dust while nearing the Sun, and it found that the comet's water differs from the water of Earth's seas in the ratio of its parts. So the idea that Earth's seawater came from comets like this one lost ground. In the gas round the comet it found glycine, a building block of proteins, and phosphorus, which life cannot do without, and, unexpectedly, oxygen gas. The instrument that sniffed the gas reported that the comet smells of rotten eggs and horse stables. On 30 September 2016 it ended its mission by settling onto the comet at walking pace, and its last picture was taken about 20 m above the ground.
갈릴레오는 미국항공우주국이 1989년 10월 18일 우주왕복선 아틀란티스: Galileo is a Jupiter spacecraft that NASA sent off aboard the Space Shuttle Atlantis on 18 October 1989. It is named after Galileo Galilei, who in 1610 first found Jupiter's four large moons. It swung past Venus once and Earth twice to gain speed, and in 1991, passing the asteroid Gaspra, it became the first spacecraft to photograph an asteroid close up. In 1993 it found a small moon, Dactyl, beside the asteroid Ida. It was the first moon of an asteroid ever found. In July 1994 it alone looked straight on as pieces of Comet Shoemaker-Levy 9 struck Jupiter, on the side that could not be seen from Earth. On 7 December 1995 it became the first spacecraft to go round Jupiter.
지름 4.8m의 우산 모양 안테나가 끝내 다 펴지지 않아, 작은 안테나로: Its umbrella-shaped antenna, 4.8 m across, never fully opened, so it had to send its data a little at a time through a small antenna. New software that packed pictures tightly was sent up from afar, and it achieved about 70% of its goals. On the day it reached Jupiter, a small probe released months before plunged into Jupiter's atmosphere at about 47 km/s and measured the winds and gases in the clouds for 58 minutes before it was crushed and lost. Over 8 years it went round Jupiter 35 times, found evidence of a salty ocean under Europa's ice, found Ganymede's magnetic field, and studied Io's volcanoes up close. As its fuel ran low, it was sent diving into Jupiter on 21 September 2003, so that it would not strike Europa, where there might be life.
메신저는 미국항공우주국이 2004년 8월 3일 쏘아 올린 수성 탐사선입니: MESSENGER is a Mercury spacecraft that NASA launched on 3 August 2004. Its name is an English acronym for "Mercury Surface, Space Environment, Geochemistry and Ranging", and it also points to Mercury, the Roman messenger of the gods, and so to the planet. Mercury is close to the Sun, so a craft flying straight there would speed up too much to be caught into orbit round it. So it swung past Earth once, Venus twice and Mercury three times to slow down, and after travelling about 7.9 billion km over 6 years and 7 months it became, on 18 March 2011, the first spacecraft to go round Mercury. Before it, the only visitor had been Mariner 10, which flew past three times in 1974 and 1975 and photographed less than half of Mercury's ground.
태양 쪽에 세라믹 천으로 된 햇빛 가리개를 세워, 가리개 앞면이 350도: It stood a sunshade of ceramic cloth on its sunward side, so even when the front of the shade grew nearly 350 degrees hot, the instruments behind it stayed at room temperature. Over four years it photographed all of Mercury's ground to make maps, and found water ice inside polar craters where sunlight never reaches. That ice is covered by a dark material that seems to be organic. As its inside cooled, Mercury shrank, its radius shortening by about 7 km, and long cliffs formed then are left on its ground. It also found bright, shallow hollows seen nowhere else. When its fuel ran out it held on by using even the helium gas that had pushed the fuel, and on 30 April 2015 it fell onto Mercury at about 3.9 km/s. BepiColombo, from Europe and Japan, follows it and is due to reach Mercury in November 2026.

2023년 9월 26일, 지구에 돌아온 시료 통의 뚜껑을 연 모습. 가운: The sample canister back on Earth with its lid off, 26 September 2023. Black dust and sand-sized grains cling to the sampling head in the middle and all around it.
허블이 본 두 갈래 꼬리: The twin tail seen by Hubble
2022년 10월 허블 우주망원경이 찍은 디디모스와 디모르포스. 다트가: Didymos and Dimorphos, photographed by the Hubble Space Telescope in October 2022. Dust thrown out after DART's impact stretches away in two tails.
Arrokoth, photographed on 1 January 2019 by New Horizons as it drew away after flying past. Only the sunlit edge shines, like a crescent, and it showed the two lumps are flatter than had been thought.

사하라의 눈 고리 안, 바위 언덕에서 내려다본 모습. 땅 위에서는 고리가: Inside the Eye of the Sahara, seen from a rocky hill. On the ground the rings look like nothing more than low hills and sandy plains.
지구 모리타니의 사하라의 눈(북위 21.1도, 서경 11.4도) 40km: Land within 40 km of the Eye of the Sahara in Mauritania on Earth (21.1° N, 11.4° W)
사하라 사막 한가운데에 있는 지름 40km의 둥근 고리 무늬입니다. 우주: A round pattern of rings 40 km across in the middle of the Sahara. From space it looks like an eye, and astronauts steer by it.
사하라의 눈은 서아프리카 모리타니의 아드라르 고원, 사하라 사막 한가운데: The Eye of the Sahara is the Richat Structure, on the Adrar plateau of Mauritania in West Africa, in the middle of the Sahara. Rings about 40 km across lie one inside another. On the ground it is only a run of low hills and hard to make out; it became widely known after astronauts in the 1960s looked down on it from orbit. It was first taken for a crater left by a meteorite, but about 100 million years ago molten rock pushed the ground up into a round dome, and as wind and rain wore the dome down, only the hard layers of rock were left standing as rings.
2011년 12월 국제우주정거장에서 내려다본 사하라의 눈. 왼쪽 위의 흰: The Eye of the Sahara seen from the International Space Station in December 2011. The white at the upper left is cloud.
고리를 이룬 것은 비바람에 잘 깎이지 않는 단단한 규암층이고, 그 사이의: The rings are layers of hard quartzite that wind and rain wear down slowly; the softer layers between them were worn into valleys. From the middle outward the rocks get younger, the order you find when a round dome is worn down. Many stone hand axes used by people hundreds of thousands of years ago have been found inside the rings.
사하라의 눈은 무엇이 깎여서 생겼나?: What was worn down to make the Eye of the Sahara?
